meta.notice: First-pass routing is keyword-backed. Read evidence level and confidence before treating a connection as a finding.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

Most cells are low-dimensional synthetic sweeps over noise, sample size, and capacity. Multi-seed grids and one frozen latent-diffusion confirmation are material but far cheaper than training a modern image generator.

The primary supports expose true score, projection, topology, component mass, density, and volume. Every proposed cheap norm is evaluated prospectively against distinct, preregistered recovery endpoints.

Low-noise score singularity, manifold rates, finite-sample convergence, gradient-versus-solenoidal error, and geometry-aware training already exist. Novelty is the finite-noise cross-support audit and explicit no-universal-norm result, not another asymptotic bound.
Circle, torus, and disconnected-support pilots can separate raw L2, gradient-projected, high-quantile, and covering-grid errors within days; boundary and latent-transfer claims take longer.

assumptions: Population convolved scores and nearest-support projections can be computed analytically or to audited numerical tolerance for the primary low-dimensional support families.

A finite covering grid and adaptive adversarial residual search approximate the relevant uniform error closely enough to serve as an oracle diagnostic, while remaining clearly labeled unavailable in natural data.
Score networks can be trained across enough independent datasets and initializations to distinguish sample, optimization, and support-class variance.
The natural latent-space confirmation is a transfer check only and cannot validate unknown topology or manifold truth.

brief.title: Which score error buys which geometry? A finite-noise norm-gap audit
brief.thesis: Train score models on known connected, disconnected, boundary, and stratified supports across finite noise, sample size, capacity, and optimization budgets. Compare held-out denoising L2, the gradient component of score error, local high-quantile residuals, normal-versus-tangential residuals, and an oracle covering-grid sup error. Freeze a predictor on development supports and ask which observable signal forecasts tubular concentration, Hausdorff support error, topology, component weights, density, uniform-volume recovery, and sampler mixing on unseen support classes. Permit the correct result to be that no single norm orders all targets.
brief.motivation: Geometry-first score theory separates an order-sigma^-2 normal confinement term from order-one density structure, but its guarantees use asymptotic uniform error on a compact smooth manifold rather than an observable training loss. Covariance-based denoiser approximations show that simple statistics can explain part of a score field; statistic-learning work shows higher-order structure can emerge only later; and memorization studies show forward-noised training probes can diverge from actual reverse-trajectory states. Most importantly, current theory shows raw L2 score error can be arbitrarily large while the target marginal remains exact because solenoidal error is invisible to Fokker-Planck marginals. The missing bridge is a prospective finite-noise audit that distinguishes recovery targets and tests gradient-projected and local alternatives rather than assuming training risk transfers to geometry.
brief.research_question: Across finite sample, noise, capacity, and support regimes, which observable components of learned-score error prospectively predict support geometry, topology, component mass, density, and mixing—and when is any scalar norm provably or empirically non-ordering?
non_claims: The project does not claim the first manifold diffusion theorem, score decomposition, finite-sample bound, topology metric, or geometry-aware sampler.
Raw denoising L2 is not assumed to be monotone in marginal distribution quality or any geometric endpoint.
Support concentration, Hausdorff recovery, topology, curvature, density recovery, uniform-volume exploration, and fast mixing are separate outcomes.
Uniform manifold volume is a changed target, not a more accurate estimate of a nonuniform data distribution.
A low-dimensional synthetic phase diagram does not certify the unknown manifold of natural images or a production latent diffusion model.
subquestions: Does the gradient component estimated through a dual Sobolev identity predict marginal density while normal high-quantile error better predicts support concentration?
At what finite sigma and sample size do the asymptotic normal-versus-tangential error classes become visible, if at all?
Can two models with matched denoising L2 have different topology, component-mass, or mixing outcomes, and which residual diagnostic forecasts the split?
How do boundaries, intersections, density zeros, disconnected components, curvature, reach, and changing intrinsic dimension alter the ranking of norms?
Does a predictor frozen on analytic supports retain calibration on an unseen support generator and one latent diffusion checkpoint family?
method: Create audited support families with analytic or high-precision numerical convolved scores: circles, spheres, tori, curves with controlled reach, unequal disconnected components, intervals and disks with boundary, intersecting or stratified unions, and distributions with registered density zeros or bottlenecks.

Cross noise level, sample size, ambient and intrinsic dimension, network width/depth, training steps, and dataset resampling. Train standard denoising score matching models across at least eight seeds per primary cell and retain full checkpoint trajectories rather than selecting only best loss.

On disjoint forward-noised validation samples and reverse-trajectory states, measure standard L2, gradient-projected error through the dual Sobolev estimator, solenoidal residual, local 90th/99th-percentile error, Jacobian and curl diagnostics, oracle normal and tangential residuals, and adaptive covering-grid L-infinity error.

Sample with matched reverse SDE, probability-flow ODE, Langevin corrector, and tempered-score variants. Equalize score evaluations and discretization error so sampler differences cannot masquerade as learned-score geometry.

Evaluate tubular mass, Hausdorff and Chamfer support error, projection error, persistent-homology barcodes and Betti numbers, curvature and reach where identifiable, connected-component mass, on-support Wasserstein or KL density error, uniform-volume error, low-density bridges, hitting time, and effective mixing.

Fit sparse, monotone only where justified, uncertainty-calibrated maps from predeclared error features to each endpoint on development supports. Freeze features, thresholds, coefficients, and abstention rules before opening a support class with different boundary or topology.

After the synthetic audit, freeze one diagnostic panel and test a small latent diffusion family across checkpoints and noise levels using empirical neighborhood, held-out-density, memorization, and trajectory-shift proxies. Make no unobservable natural-manifold claim.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: This is a finite-noise calibration study, not a universal scaling law. Freeze the metric panel and response maps before changing support class, dimension, or latent model; report where calibration fails rather than fitting a new exponent after the fact.
supporting_evidence: On untouched support classes, one or more observable error components predict their registered recovery target with calibrated uncertainty beyond denoising L2, elapsed compute, and capacity alone.
Matched-L2 model pairs exhibit prospectively predicted differences in topology, component mass, density, or mixing, demonstrating why target-specific diagnostics matter.
Normal and tangential or gradient and solenoidal interventions produce the predicted selective endpoint changes at fixed total error magnitude.
Finite-noise response surfaces approach the asymptotic ordering only in identifiable regimes and abstain elsewhere.
The frozen panel directionally predicts held-out latent-model trajectory or memorization outcomes without selecting checkpoints on the final metric.
claim_blockers: No error feature improves held-out prediction beyond noise, sample size, capacity, and training step.
The gradient-projected or local metrics are too noisy to calibrate without using the target support oracle at test time.
Matched-L2 pairs do not yield stable endpoint differences or the result reverses across seeds and discretizations.
Persistent-homology and component-mass results are artifacts of sample count, neighborhood bandwidth, or sampler budget.
The frozen predictor requires support-specific threshold or exponent refitting.
The latent confirmation reverses the registered direction or ordinary trajectory-shift baselines dominate.
prospective_design: Develop metrics on circles, spheres, and one connected curved support; reserve disconnected, boundary, and stratified families.
Freeze noise grid, sample and capacity cells, seed count, sampler budgets, topology estimators, error features, and all abstention rules.
Open one unseen support family at a time and never recalibrate the primary predictor on its outcomes.
Freeze the final panel again before the latent diffusion check and publish all target-specific failures, not an aggregate success score.
why_small_models_fail: Low-dimensional oracles expose projection, normal bundles, topology, and density that are unknown in natural representations.
A fixed smooth support omits learned encoders, semantic conditioning, nonstationarity, and changing latent dimension.
Finite-grid uniform error is exponentially costly with dimension and cannot become a practical large-model validator unchanged.
Reverse diffusion is time-inhomogeneous, while fixed-noise Langevin stationary behavior can conceal discretization and trajectory-distribution effects.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Claim a target-specific finite-noise calibration only for support families and dimensions that pass untouched evaluation. If no observable norm generalizes, publish the non-ordering counterexamples and reject a universal geometry-first training certificate.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A frozen target-specific model using gradient-projected and local high-quantile score residuals will predict held-out support, topology, component-mass, and density error more accurately than denoising L2, training step, noise level, or capacity alone on unseen support classes.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Normal and tangential or gradient and solenoidal error interventions with matched total L2 will selectively change geometric versus marginal outcomes, creating preregistered matched-L2 counterexamples to a universal scalar ordering.
domains: Analytic connected circles, spheres, tori, and curved manifolds with controlled reach and curvature
Unequal disconnected components and narrow-bottleneck supports
Intervals, disks, manifolds with boundary, intersections, and stratified unions
One frozen low-dimensional latent diffusion checkpoint family as an external-validity check
baselines: Held-out denoising L2, train loss, training step, network capacity, and sample size
Gradient-component dual Sobolev estimate, solenoidal component, curl, local high-quantile residual, and adaptive sup-error oracle
Normal-only, tangential-only, gradient-only, solenoidal-only, random, and norm-matched injected score errors
Reverse SDE, probability-flow ODE, standard corrector, and tempered-score corrector at equal score evaluations
Raw sample quality, nearest-training distance, forward-probe gap, reverse-trajectory gap, and covariance-only denoiser predictors
ablations: Remove gradient projection, high-quantile error, normal-tangential decomposition, or trajectory-state measurements
Use forward-noised validation states only versus actual reverse-trajectory states
Hold total L2 fixed while rotating error among gradient, solenoidal, normal, and tangential components
Connected versus disconnected support and equal versus unequal component weights
Smooth closed support versus boundary, intersection, density-zero, and stratified cases
Equal sampler steps versus converged or extrapolated mixing estimates
experiment.primary_outcome: Held-out calibration and rank prediction for each preregistered recovery endpoint—support Hausdorff error, topology error, component-mass error, on-support density error, and mixing time—on unseen support families.
experiment.analysis: Use dataset draw and training seed as crossed random effects; compare nested frozen predictors with out-of-support-family log score, rank correlation, calibration slope, and interval coverage. Test matched-L2 interventions as randomized contrasts, correct the fixed endpoint family for multiplicity, and model censored non-mixing runs rather than dropping them. Report no aggregate winner when different norms govern different targets.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only target by target: the frozen observable panel must improve prediction over L2 and resource baselines with calibrated intervals on every registered holdout of that target, and matched-L2 component interventions must change the predicted endpoint selectively. If calibration requires oracle support access, post hoc thresholding, or support-specific refitting, reject the practical certificate.

falsifiers: Denoising L2 and simple resource variables match every richer observable on held-out support families.
Gradient-projected, high-quantile, or trajectory-state metrics cannot be estimated with useful variance from finite validation data.
Norm-matched component interventions fail to produce target-selective changes.
Topology or component recovery changes only with sampler discretization or sample count, not the registered error component.
The asymptotic sigma ordering does not appear anywhere in the finite-noise regime studied.
The frozen latent-space check reverses the diagnostic ranking.
evaluation: Held-out denoising L2, gradient-projected Sobolev error, solenoidal residual, curl, Jacobian spectrum, high-quantile error, normal and tangential error, and adaptive grid sup error
Tubular concentration, projection distance, Hausdorff and Chamfer support distance, coverage, and low-density bridge rate
Persistent-homology bottleneck distance, Betti-number error, component discovery, curvature, reach, boundary, and intersection recovery
Component-mass calibration, on-support Wasserstein and KL error, uniform-volume discrepancy, and density-zero leakage
Reverse-SDE and ODE error, sampler discretization, hitting time, autocorrelation, effective sample size, and censored mixing time
Checkpoint, samples, parameters, FLOPs, wall time, score evaluations, dataset seed, initialization seed, and uncertainty calibration
Latent forward-probe versus reverse-trajectory error, memorization gap, nearest-training distance, and held-out sample-distribution metrics
risks: Numerical score or projection oracles can be wrong on stratified supports. Validate against analytic special cases, refine quadrature and covers until tolerance is stable, and publish residual bounds.

A finite cover can miss narrow sup-error spikes. Combine deterministic covers, gradient-based adversarial residual search, and Lipschitz envelopes, while labeling it an oracle diagnostic rather than a scalable metric.
Persistent homology is sensitive to sample count and bandwidth. Match samples, use bootstrap barcodes and analytic topology, and report failure to resolve short-lived features.
Injected error fields may violate learned-network structure. Compare analytic interventions with naturally trained matched-L2 checkpoints and treat agreement as a separate gate.
Endpoint proliferation invites selective synthesis. Freeze five primary endpoints and allow different metrics—or none—to win each one.
Latent natural data lack geometric ground truth. Restrict transfer claims to observable trajectory and distribution metrics and do not back-infer topology.
first_week: Implement analytic circle, sphere, torus, and two-component mixture scores across a finite noise grid and verify them by automatic differentiation and quadrature.
Train eight seeds of one small score MLP over sample-size and width cells with checkpoint-complete logging.
Implement raw L2, dual-Sobolev gradient error, curl or solenoidal diagnostics, normal-tangential oracle error, high quantiles, and adaptive residual search.
Run equal-budget reverse SDE and Langevin sampling and compute support, component-mass, density, topology, and mixing outcomes.
Construct matched-total-error gradient-versus-solenoidal and normal-versus-tangential interventions, then preregister all holdouts and target-specific pass rules.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models Observe Only Gradients: A Geometric Perspective on Score Matching Errors
competitive_landscape.difference: Khelifa et al. prove raw L2 score error cannot monotonically lower-bound marginal divergence, decompose gradient and solenoidal error, and propose a dual-Sobolev estimator. The audit makes that estimator a required baseline and tests additional support, topology, component, and mixing outcomes at finite noise.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization Properties of Score-matching Diffusion Models for Intrinsically Low-dimensional Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Chakraborty et al. give finite-sample Wasserstein-p convergence governed by a generalized intrinsic dimension without manifold smoothness. The proposal empirically separates geometry, topology, density, and mixing rather than using one distributional endpoint.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Model for Manifold Data: Score Decomposition, Curvature, and Statistical Complexity
competitive_landscape.relationship: current manifold score and rate theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. decompose manifold scores, expose curvature dependence, and derive approximation and statistical rates. The audit tests which of those theoretically meaningful components can be estimated and calibrated across misspecified boundary and stratified supports.

competitive_landscape.title: Mathematical Analysis of Singularities in the Diffusion Model under the Submanifold Assumption
competitive_landscape.difference: Lu, Wang, and Bal characterize the normal score singularity near a manifold. The proposal turns asymptotic structure into finite-noise, finite-sample prediction tasks and includes supports that violate the smooth closed-manifold assumption.

competitive_landscape.title: Convergence of Diffusion Models under the Manifold Hypothesis in High-Dimensions
competitive_landscape.difference: Azangulov et al. provide intrinsic-dimension-sensitive score and sampling rates. Their assumptions and distributional targets become a theory baseline; the audit checks topology, components, boundaries, and observable norm calibration separately.

competitive_landscape.title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Models under the Manifold Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: This work gives foundational convergence guarantees under manifold structure. The proposed study stresses finite-noise diagnostics and explicit assumption violations rather than adding another broad convergence theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving the Euclidean Diffusion Generation of Manifold Data by Mitigating Score Function Singularity
competitive_landscape.difference: Niso and Tango modify training using normal and tangential score structure. They are direct method baselines; the audit asks which measured component predicts each endpoint before recommending an objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Resolving Memorization in Empirical Diffusion Model for Manifold Data in High-Dimensional Spaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Lyu et al. analyze empirical-distribution memorization and introduce an inertial update with finite-sample bounds. The proposed phase diagram includes dataset resampling and nearest-training behavior but focuses on norm-to-target calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models under Low-Noise Regime
competitive_landscape.difference: This work directly studies low-noise diffusion behavior. The audit crosses noise with sample, capacity, support type, error decomposition, and multiple recovery targets rather than treating low noise as one regime.

competitive_landscape.title: Manifolds, Random Matrices and Spectral Gaps: The Geometric Phases of Generative Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Ventura et al. study score-Jacobian spectra and geometric phase transitions. Jacobian and spectral diagnostics become candidate predictors here, tested against direct support and topology outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: Provable Maximum Entropy Manifold Exploration via Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: De Santi et al. target maximum-entropy manifold exploration with sequential model updates. The audit treats uniform volume as one deliberately changed target and measures when density and component weights are sacrificed.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization in Diffusion Models Arises from Geometry-Adaptive Harmonic Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: This work links diffusion generalization to geometry-adaptive harmonic structure. Harmonic or spectral diagnostics are compared with direct score-error components rather than assumed to determine support recovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards a Mechanistic Explanation of Diffusion Model Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Mechanistic approximations explain how diffusion can generalize beyond empirical points. The proposed study quantifies whether those mechanisms yield calibrated finite-noise geometry and density outcomes across support violations.

competitive_landscape.title: An Analytical Theory of Spectral Bias in the Learning Dynamics of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Spectral bias predicts which distributional modes are learned first. The audit tests whether checkpoint learning order translates into support, topology, density, and mixing in a target-specific way.

competitive_landscape.title: Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle: A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work gives a geometric account of the intermediate-noise memorization regime. The proposal uses forward and reverse state measurements and asks whether norm components predict geometry and density beyond the noise coordinate itself.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four relevant hash-pinned readings spanning 121 pages, 36 findings, 109 page anchors, and 29 competitor inspections covering 27 unique primary papers, plus current official arXiv review of three 2026 norm and finite-sample competitors: low-noise singularities, manifold convergence, score decomposition, finite-sample rates, spectral phases, memorization regimes, and geometry-aware objectives are established. The nonredundant contribution is a preregistered finite-noise benchmark that maps observable error components to distinct recovery targets across smooth, disconnected, boundary, and stratified supports; freezes calibration before support-class transfer; and explicitly allows no universal scalar norm. It does not duplicate the diffusion maturity brief, which predicts internal-verifier reliability under search rather than score-learning recovery.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four genuinely relevant full-text readings totaling 121 pages, with 36 page-attributed findings, 109 anchors, and 27 unique directly inspected primary competitors; unrelated papers from the same reading batch are deliberately not asserted as support. The root novelty audit added current official arXiv records on gradient-only score observability, finite-sample Wasserstein generalization, and curvature-aware manifold rates.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

The decisive factorial uses small synthetic classifiers and can be powered across many seeds cheaply. Only the frozen image-model replication and multi-seed SAE audits require material accelerator time.

True feature count, support distribution, dictionary geometry, clean margins, attack budget, and cross-feature leakage are observable in the primary generator, with exact or bounded robust radii and explicit function-preserving null transformations.

Two direct predecessors already intervene on superposition or derive interference-aligned attacks. Novelty is limited to separating geometric interference from SAE activation entropy, causal atom validity, margins, sensitivity, and coordinate artifacts in one preregistered factorial.
A linear or shallow-ReLU pilot can falsify a geometry effect within days; a credible SAE recovery audit and untouched real-data replication take longer.

assumptions: A known-factor generator can vary activation-support entropy and co-occurrence while holding the true feature ontology, width, labels, and input scale fixed.

Frame families with controlled coherence and spectra can be compared at matched column norms, bottleneck width, parameter count, clean accuracy, margin distribution, and registered sensitivity diagnostics.
The primary shallow networks are simple enough to estimate or certify robust radii, not merely report one attack's failure rate.
A frozen natural-image replication is treated as external validity evidence only; it cannot replace the synthetic ground-truth identification.

brief.title: Orthogonalize the cause, not the proxy: a superposition–robustness factorial
brief.thesis: Independently manipulate true dictionary interference and activation-support entropy in a known-factor classifier while matching width, clean accuracy, margins, gradient sensitivity, SAE reconstruction, and compute. Test certified or attack-based robust radius and targeted cross-feature leakage. An SAE-derived effective-feature count is admitted only after it recovers and causally reads and writes the known factors; function-preserving non-orthogonal coordinate changes are mandatory null controls. The claim passes only if geometric interference, rather than proxy entropy or a coordinate choice, prospectively changes vulnerability.
brief.motivation: Spectral Superposition gives a basis-invariant frame language but assumes an identifiable feature dictionary and proves equality-case geometry only under saturation and localization. How Many Features Can a Language Model Store separates representation from accessible decoding and shows that encoder or decoder geometry alone need not be identified. From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry shows correlations can make interference constructive, but stops at tied toys and qualitative language evidence. Superposition as Lossy Compression uses SAE activation entropy as a broad proxy and finds adversarial-training effects can reverse with capacity and task complexity, yet adversarial training is not an intervention on superposition. Direct 2025-2026 competitors already show that controlled superposition can create attacks; the unresolved measurement question is whether geometry remains causal after proxy validity, margins, sensitivity, support statistics, and reparameterization are separated.
brief.research_question: At fixed true feature count, activation support, width, clean function quality, margins, and sensitivity, does changing non-orthogonal feature interference causally change adversarial robust radius and targeted cross-feature leakage, and does an SAE entropy proxy track that cause rather than dictionary artifacts?
non_claims: Superposition, frame coherence, sparse autoencoders, adversarial examples, non-robust features, and interference-aligned attacks are not new.
The project does not claim that all adversarial vulnerability is caused by superposition or that adversarial training must reduce feature count.
Shannon perplexity of SAE activations is treated as support evenness, not a proven minimum number of continuous neurons.
A recovered SAE direction is not called a causal feature until presence, activation, ablation, and steering checks all pass.
Geometry that changes under a function-preserving coordinate transform cannot by itself explain an unchanged input-output robustness property.
subquestions: Does Gram coherence or a registered spectral interference statistic predict robust radius after true feature count, activation entropy, clean margin, and Jacobian norms are matched?
Can activation-support entropy change the SAE proxy without changing true geometric interference or vulnerability?
Which attacks follow analytically predicted cross-feature leakage, and when do generic non-robust input features explain more variance?
Do TopK and L1 SAEs recover the same known factors, and do read- and write-side causal audits agree with cosine recovery and aggregate entropy?
Does the frozen intervention reproduce directionally in one image model without selecting a layer, SAE, attack, or coefficient on the reported outcome?
method: Generate sparse latent factors z with a fixed named ontology and labels from a preregistered subset of factors. Cross independent factors controlling activation probability/evenness, pairwise co-occurrence, true feature count m, active sparsity k, and bottleneck ratio m/d while preserving the input and label scales.

Instantiate or regularize bottleneck dictionaries from orthogonal or least-coherent, equiangular or tight-frame, block-coherent, covariance-aligned, and randomized frame families. Match width, column norms, parameter count, reconstruction error, and downstream architecture; analyze the Gram matrix and frame operator rather than only pairwise cosine.

Train downstream classifiers across at least ten seeds per primary cell. Register equal-compute and equal-clean-performance estimands, then match clean accuracy, logit-margin distribution, loss, input-gradient norm, local Jacobian spectrum, Lipschitz upper bounds, and calibration before attributing a robustness difference to interference.

Add function-preserving controls D to TD with the following layer transformed by the corresponding inverse, restricted to numerically stable invertible T. These controls can change Euclidean dictionary geometry and SAE behavior while leaving the exact input-output function fixed; any proposed causal metric must be invariant or correctly predict a null robustness effect.

Train L1 and TopK SAEs across seeds and dictionary sizes on disjoint activations. Match atoms to ground-truth factors, then audit whether the atom fires when the factor is present, ablation suppresses its causal contribution, steering writes the expected factor, and collisions, splitting, antipodal pairs, or inactive atoms are absent. Compute effective-count proxies only after this gate.

Measure exact robust radius where the shallow model permits it, certified lower bounds otherwise, and PGD, AutoAttack, targeted factor-space attacks, transfer attacks, and random perturbations at matched budgets. Compare attack directions with the Gram-predicted interference direction and record cross-feature activation and logit leakage.

Freeze the winning or null prediction before one CIFAR-10 small-convnet or ViT replication. Use a single registered layer, SAE family, attack suite, and intervention; report it as transfer evidence without pretending the image model exposes a complete feature ontology.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The known-factor factorial identifies a causal boundary in a controlled code; it does not establish a universal account of large networks. Freeze the geometry statistic, SAE validity gate, matching protocol, attack suite, and effect direction before the image replication.
supporting_evidence: At fixed support entropy and matched clean function diagnostics, lower interference increases certified or empirical robust radius and reduces targeted cross-feature leakage across frame families and seeds.
Changing activation entropy at fixed geometry moves the SAE effective-count proxy without reproducing the robustness effect, separating proxy from cause.
Function-preserving coordinate transforms correctly produce no robustness change even when Euclidean dictionary or SAE metrics move.
Causally validated SAE atoms recover the known-factor geometry and predict the same vulnerable pairs; cosine-only or inert atoms do not.
The frozen geometry statistic predicts directional vulnerability or leakage in the untouched image replication beyond margin, Jacobian, and non-robust-feature baselines.
claim_blockers: The geometry effect disappears after matching clean margins, Jacobian or Lipschitz diagnostics, and achieved loss.
Activation entropy or SAE hyperparameters explain the proxy and robustness as well as true dictionary interference.
Function-preserving coordinate changes alter the proposed causal score without correctly predicting the null behavioral effect.
SAE atoms match by cosine but fail presence, activation, ablation, steering, or collision checks.
Attack directions do not align with predicted leakage or a non-robust-input-feature baseline dominates held-out prediction.
The frozen direction reverses or vanishes in the image replication.
prospective_design: Develop frame construction and exact-radius code on a small latent ontology and reserve one feature-support family unopened.
Freeze the factorial cells, seed count, match tolerances, SAE causal gate, geometry metrics, attacks, and multiplicity correction before the held-out support family.
Select no image layer or SAE from robustness outcomes; register them from clean reconstruction and causal-audit criteria only.
Publish all failed matches, inert atoms, transform condition numbers, null attacks, and real-data failures alongside positive cells.
why_small_models_fail: A known one-dimensional factor ontology avoids splitting, hierarchy, nonlinear manifolds, and distributed computation found in real representations.
Exact frame control may be impossible after end-to-end training in a deep residual network.
Certified radii for shallow networks and finite PGD results for image models answer different robustness questions.
Natural-image adversarial vulnerability can arise from non-robust input features, decision-boundary geometry, architecture, or optimization even if superposition contributes in the toy setting.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only the ground-truth factorial passes, claim that geometric interference is sufficient and causal in that registered code. Claim an image-model association only if the frozen transfer gate passes, and never call superposition the primary or universal cause without ruling out the registered alternatives.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: Reducing registered Gram interference at fixed true feature count, activation-support entropy, width, clean margin distribution, loss, Jacobian spectrum, and compute will increase robust radius and reduce targeted cross-feature leakage across held-out seeds and frame families.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: SAE activation entropy will not be sufficient: support reweighting can move the proxy without moving robustness, whereas only causally validated atoms and ground-truth Gram structure will identify the vulnerable feature pairs.
domains: Sparse known-factor linear classifiers with exact robust-radius calculations
Shallow ReLU bottleneck classifiers with certified lower bounds and white-box attacks
Independent and correlated factor supports at fixed feature ontology and bottleneck width
One frozen CIFAR-10 convnet or ViT representation replication
baselines: Orthogonal or least-coherent, tight-frame, block-coherent, covariance-aligned, and random dictionaries
SAE effective feature count, raw activation entropy, participation ratio, stable rank, pairwise cosine, spectral localization, and true Gram coherence
Margin, input-gradient norm, Jacobian spectrum, Lipschitz bound, clean loss, and calibration predictors
Non-robust-feature, random-direction, decision-boundary, and interference-derived attacks at matched norm and query budget
Function-preserving orthogonal and non-orthogonal coordinate transforms plus deliberately function-changing geometry interventions
L1 and TopK SAEs across seeds and dictionary sizes, with cosine-only versus full causal feature validation
ablations: Hold geometry fixed and vary feature activation entropy or correlations
Hold support fixed and vary coherence, spectral concentration, or association-scheme structure
Remove margin, Jacobian, loss, or Lipschitz matching one at a time
Use SAE cosine recovery without activation checks, then add read-ablation and write-steering gates
Untie encoder and decoder dictionaries and compare encoder, decoder, and cross-geometry
Remove one-dimensional factors in favor of a registered two-dimensional circular factor to test ontology dependence
experiment.primary_outcome: The seed-blocked change in certified or strongest-attack robust radius and targeted cross-feature logit leakage caused by the registered geometry intervention at matched support entropy, clean margin, sensitivity, loss, and compute.
experiment.analysis: Use a preregistered factorial mixed model with geometry, support entropy, correlation, and bottleneck ratio as randomized factors; seed and latent-support draw are blocks. Estimate geometry main effects and interactions with simultaneous intervals, verify matching through equivalence tests, and compare held-out predictive value of true geometry, SAE proxy, margins, Jacobians, and non-robust-feature scores. Analyze the image replication once with frozen signs and no retuning.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if the geometry intervention changes robust radius and cross-feature leakage in the registered direction with positive simultaneous intervals after all match tolerances pass; entropy-only proxy changes do not reproduce the effect; function-preserving transforms yield the predicted null; and causally validated rather than cosine-only SAE atoms recover the vulnerable pairs. Otherwise reject the claimed causal separation.

falsifiers: Margin, loss, Jacobian, Lipschitz, or non-robust-feature differences account for the apparent geometry effect.
Support entropy changes robustness at fixed geometry exactly as strongly as geometric interference.
A function-preserving reparameterization changes the proposed causal score while leaving robustness unchanged.
SAE effective count is unstable across seed, dictionary size, L1 versus TopK, splitting, merging, or atom collisions.
Ground-truth vulnerable feature pairs are not recovered by causal atom audits or attack-direction alignment.
The frozen real-data replication reverses the synthetic prediction.
evaluation: True feature count, active sparsity, activation entropy, support correlations, bottleneck ratio, Gram coherence, frame spectrum, localization, and stable rank
Clean accuracy, NLL, calibration, logit margins, reconstruction, parameters, FLOPs, input-gradient norm, Jacobian spectrum, and Lipschitz bounds
Exact or certified robust radius, PGD and AutoAttack robust accuracy, targeted success, transfer rate, query budget, and perturbation norm
Predicted-versus-observed attack alignment, cross-feature activation leakage, logit leakage, and pairwise vulnerability rank correlation
SAE ground-truth recovery, activation precision/recall, ablation specificity, steering specificity, read/write inertness, collisions, splitting, and seed overlap
Effective-count proxy stability across SAE type and size, and invariance or calibrated response under function-preserving transforms
Ten-seed intervals, equivalence tests for matching, multiplicity-adjusted factorial effects, and untouched image-replication prediction error
risks: Changing a dictionary can change the represented function. Refit downstream layers under registered matching tolerances and separate exact function-preserving null transforms from deliberately function-changing causal interventions.
Geometry families may differ in condition number. Bound transformation condition numbers, use higher precision checks, and report numerical residuals before interpreting robustness.
Exact clean-margin and sensitivity matching can remove much of the causal pathway. Report total and controlled direct effects as separate estimands instead of choosing the more favorable one.
A one-dimensional feature ontology privileges linear superposition. Include one multidimensional registered factor and bound all claims to the tested ontology.
SAE causal audits can still miss distributed features. Ground-truth factor interventions remain authoritative in the synthetic study; SAE results are a measurement evaluation, not the ontology.
The image replication lacks complete ground truth. Treat null or contradictory transfer as a failed scale gate rather than searching layers or attacks post hoc.
first_week: Implement a fixed-ontology sparse factor generator and unit-test feature count, support entropy, correlations, labels, and perturbation semantics.
Construct orthogonal or least-coherent, tight-frame, and block-coherent dictionaries with matched norms and verify Gram and frame spectra numerically.
Train ten seeds of a shallow classifier per reduced factorial cell and establish clean-margin, loss, Jacobian, and compute equivalence.
Compute exact or certified radii, run interference-derived and generic attacks, and test whether predicted feature pairs leak as expected.
Train paired L1 and TopK SAEs, implement presence/activation/ablation/steering and collision audits, and preregister the full held-out and image-transfer protocol.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Gorton and Lewis already intervene on superposition and robustness in toy models and alter robustness through adversarial training in ResNet-18. The proposed contribution is therefore not causal sufficiency; it is the matched factorial separating dictionary geometry, activation entropy, margins, sensitivity, SAE validity, and coordinate artifacts.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Stevinson et al. derive interference-aligned attacks, establish sufficiency in controlled superposition, and connect predicted structure to image attacks. This proposal tests whether that geometry retains incremental causal value after a stricter proxy, function, margin, support, and reparameterization audit.

competitive_landscape.title: Superposition as Lossy Compression: Measure with Sparse Autoencoders and Connect to Adversarial Vulnerability
competitive_landscape.difference: Bereska et al. introduce an SAE activation-entropy effective count and find capacity-dependent adversarial-training associations. The factorial independently moves support entropy and true geometry and refuses the proxy until ground-truth causal recovery passes.

competitive_landscape.title: From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features, from Superposition Geometry to Causal Inertness
competitive_landscape.difference: Bal shows that high-cosine recovered atoms can be read- or write-inert and identifies structural and competitive inertness. The proposed SAE gate adopts this distinction and then asks a different outcome question: whether validated interference geometry predicts adversarial leakage.

competitive_landscape.title: Toy Models of Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: The canonical tied toy model establishes feature overlap, capacity allocation, and polytope phases. The proposal turns geometry into a robustness treatment and adds matched functional and proxy controls rather than rediscovering its phase diagram.

competitive_landscape.title: Polysemanticity and Capacity in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Scherlis et al. study how networks allocate feature capacity and form block-semi-orthogonal structures. Capacity and bottleneck ratio become randomized factors here, not an omitted alternative explanation for robustness.

competitive_landscape.title: What Causes Polysemanticity? An Alternative Origin Story of Mixed Selectivity from Incidental Causes
competitive_landscape.difference: Initialization, regularization, and noise can create mixed selectivity even without a binding capacity constraint. The factorial blocks initialization and crosses regularization so incidental overlap cannot be mislabeled capacity-forced superposition.

competitive_landscape.title: Projecting Assumptions: The Duality Between Sparse Autoencoders and Concept Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: SAE architecture succeeds or fails according to assumed concept geometry. This motivates the known-factor oracle, multiple SAE families, multidimensional ablation, and refusal to equate one decoder dictionary with ground truth.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
competitive_landscape.difference: Low feature overlap across SAE seeds undermines literal feature counts. The proposal measures seed alignment, splitting, merging, collisions, and aggregate-proxy stability before any robustness analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. provide TopK training, dead-latent controls, feature recovery, explainability, and downstream-effect metrics at large scale. The proposal borrows those evaluation dimensions but adds exact factor ground truth and adversarial causal outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
competitive_landscape.difference: Irreducible multidimensional features make a column-count ontology incomplete. One registered circular factor tests whether the claimed geometry-robustness relation survives beyond one-dimensional atoms.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. derive causal representation and intervention notions with a language-relevant inner product. The proposal's function-preserving controls test whether ordinary Euclidean frame geometry is causally meaningful or merely a coordinate convention.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Complexity of Neural Computation in Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Adler and Shavit bound resources for logical computation over superposed features. Their accessible computation criterion prevents the proposal from treating stored or probeable directions as automatically used by the classifier.

competitive_landscape.title: From Superposition to Sparse Codes: Interpretable Representations in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Klindt et al. emphasize sparse-code identifiability as the bridge from mixed neurons to concepts. The factorial supplies the privileged synthetic ontology and explicitly measures when each SAE does or does not recover it.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Features
competitive_landscape.difference: Ilyas et al. attribute adversarial examples to predictive but brittle features in the data. Non-robust-feature scores and attacks are therefore registered competing explanations that true interference geometry must beat incrementally.

competitive_landscape.title: Robustness May Be at Odds with Accuracy
competitive_landscape.difference: Tsipras et al. prove and observe robustness-accuracy tradeoffs tied to different learned features. The proposal explicitly matches clean performance and reports total versus controlled effects so a standard tradeoff is not mislabeled superposition.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned readings spanning 116 pages, 38 findings, 125 page anchors, and 40 competitor inspections covering 19 unique primary papers, plus a current primary-source audit of causal SAE inertness and non-robust-feature alternatives: controlled superposition can already cause adversarial vulnerability, and interference can already predict attacks. The nonredundant project is a falsification-grade boundary study, not another first-cause claim: independently randomize true Gram geometry and activation-support entropy; match margins, sensitivity, loss, width, and compute; require read/write-valid SAE atoms; and include exact function-preserving coordinate nulls. It is distinct from the compositional-geometry brief because its outcome is robust radius and cross-feature leakage, not zero-mass recombination or continual retention.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four complete full-text readings totaling 116 pages, with 38 page-attributed findings, 125 anchors, and 19 unique directly inspected primary competitors; the root novelty check added current official arXiv records including the July 2026 causal-inertness audit.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
The causal tournament uses a fully enumerated synthetic world and small models, so ten-seed factorial tests are practical before one larger natural-split confirmation.
Exact zero-mass cells, analytic score residuals, measured factor-gradient covariance, matched inference correction, and paired continual metrics give direct causal falsifiers.

Compositional diffusion, factor alignment, orthogonal heads, object-centric generation, sparsity, replay, and structural abstractions are crowded; novelty depends on the intervention tournament, not the ingredients.
A reduced two-factor world can distinguish true alignment from random orthogonality and score correction in days; natural transfer is a later claim gate.

assumptions: The synthetic world exposes the complete factor table, so held-out cells have exactly zero training mass and factor labels are unavailable to the unconstrained baselines.
Architecture, parameter count, optimizer, training tokens, FLOPs, achieved in-distribution fit, diffusion sampler, and particle count can be matched tightly enough to isolate representation geometry.
Factor-gradient covariance and representation metrics are computed by cross-fitting on held-out examples rather than by training and evaluating the same probe on the same states.
A larger natural split is required before claiming that a synthetic factor intervention generalizes to realistic composition.

brief.title: Factor-aligned gradient geometry: a causal test for compositional generation and continual abstraction
brief.thesis: Hold architecture and training budget fixed while intervening on whether factor changes are additive, orthogonal, correctly aligned, randomly aligned, or paired with shuffled abstractions. If factor-aligned gradient geometry is causal, only the correctly aligned intervention should improve exact zero-mass recombination and selective continual retention; score correction, replay, extra depth, random orthogonality, and fluent but wrong abstractions should not reproduce the full effect.
brief.motivation: Recent work finds that naive diffusion-score addition can fail even for Gaussians, that compositional robustness peaks at intermediate sparse depth in one evolved-image setting, that orthogonal additive representations correlate with recombination, and that generated abstractions may reduce continual interference. Yet the evidence mixes nonzero-mass 'OOD' cells, opposite prompt semantics, unproved posterior stability, label-informed probes, generator artifacts, pretraining leakage, mismatched compute, and mostly single-seed results. A common controlled world can test the proposed causal primitive rather than stacking four correlational stories.
brief.research_question: Does correctly factor-aligned additive and orthogonal gradient geometry causally improve unseen factor recombination and continual retention after data support, in-distribution fit, compute, inference correction, replay, depth, sparsity, and abstraction fluency are matched?
non_claims: The project does not claim compositional diffusion, score correction, object slots, additive representations, orthogonal heads, sparse subnetworks, replay, or abstraction-augmented training as new.
Orthogonal linear decodability is not by itself a causal or necessary explanation of compositional behavior.
Intermediate sparse depth is treated as a secondary optimization condition, not the universal source of composition.
A synthetic zero-mass result does not establish natural-image, language, or web-scale continual generalization without the registered transfer gate.
subquestions: Does true factor alignment beat additive-only and random-orthogonal controls after in-distribution loss, margin, tokens, FLOPs, and representation dimension are matched?
Does alignment reduce directly measured cross-factor per-example gradient covariance in the same runs where held-out cells improve?
Can corrected diffusion sampling remove the generative gap without changing learned geometry, showing that the failure was inference-time rather than representational?
Do true abstractions help beyond equally fluent relation-shuffled and label-shuffled texts, replay, and duplicate-instance auxiliaries?
Does the shallow/intermediate/deep by dense/sparse peak remain after compute and achieved-fit matching?
method: Build a fully enumerated visual world with two to four independently controlled factors, exact factor interventions, zero-mass held-out Cartesian cells, and a registered nonstationary stream that changes factor frequencies and combinations.

Use one frozen or small encoder plus one small conditional diffusion architecture. Hold the architecture fixed for the primary geometry intervention and compare unconstrained, additive-only, random-orthogonal, true-factor-aligned orthogonal, and true alignment paired with shuffled abstraction targets.

Match parameters, optimizer, tokens, FLOPs, in-distribution loss and margin, diffusion schedule, sampler, and particle count. Reweight or extend training only through a prespecified matching protocol, never by selectively tuning the proposed arm.

Measure per-example gradients for each controlled factor and their cross-covariance, along with cross-fitted full-space additivity, orthogonality, probing, and intervention metrics. Test whether geometry changes precede and mediate behavior.
Run a matched score-correction sampler, replay, duplicate-instance auxiliary, true abstractions, fluent relation-shuffled abstractions, and label-shuffled abstractions as mechanism controls.
After the fixed-architecture causal test, cross a reduced shallow, intermediate, and deep by dense and sparse grid under matched parameters, FLOPs, and achieved fit.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The enumerated world identifies a causal mechanism in a controlled regime; it does not show natural scale transfer. Freeze the intervention, metrics, and decision thresholds before a larger natural compositional split is opened.
supporting_evidence: True factor alignment improves held-out-cell accuracy and generative fit beyond random orthogonality and additive-only controls at matched in-distribution fit
The same intervention selectively reduces cross-factor gradient covariance, and mediation remains after simple probe metrics are controlled
Fluent shuffled abstractions fail while correct abstractions reproduce the aligned geometry and behavior
Corrected sampling cannot erase the residual gap when training geometry remains entangled
The frozen intervention improves a larger natural split without factor-specific retuning
claim_blockers: Random orthogonality or additive-only matches true factor alignment
Geometry metrics can be changed without any corresponding behavior change
Score correction removes the full generative gap
Fluent shuffled abstractions match semantically correct abstractions
No selective reduction in cross-factor gradient conflict is observed
The depth or sparsity peak vanishes after compute and fit matching
The effect fails on the preregistered natural compositional split
prospective_design: Develop the factor world, alignment losses, and diagnostics on two-factor cells
Freeze hyperparameter budgets and open held-out three- and four-factor cells plus nonstationary streams
Freeze the resulting intervention and test one larger natural split without per-factor labels at training time
Publish leakage hashes, all seeds, failed cells, inference budgets, and full-space metrics
why_small_models_fail: Synthetic factors are exactly identified while natural concepts are correlated, incomplete, and label-ambiguous
A small conditional score network may expose analytic residuals that are inaccessible in a large latent diffusion model
Pretraining can already encode held-out combinations, turning a nominal split into retrieval rather than recombination
Natural continual streams introduce generator, tokenizer, and schema channels absent from the controlled world
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only the controlled world passes, claim a causal factor-geometry result in that world. Claim broader compositional transfer only if the frozen natural-split gate passes without leakage or factor-label tuning.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: True factor-aligned orthogonal training will improve zero-mass held-out-cell accuracy or NLL and generated-cell score fit beyond additive-only and random-orthogonal controls while selectively reducing cross-factor gradient covariance at matched in-distribution fit and compute.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: On the nonstationary stream, correct factor alignment or correct abstractions will improve unknown-factor acquisition without worsening known-factor retention, whereas replay, duplicate-instance auxiliaries, and fluent shuffled abstractions will not match both outcomes.
experiment.primary_outcome: Zero-mass held-out-cell accuracy or NLL and generated-cell score fit under true factor alignment versus additive-only and random-orthogonal controls, with matched in-distribution fit and the registered cross-factor gradient-covariance change as the mechanism gate.
domains: Fully enumerated two- to four-factor synthetic visual worlds with exact interventions
Conditional pixel or small latent diffusion on zero-mass Cartesian cells
Registered nonstationary factor streams with known and unknown combinations
One held-out natural compositional image split with duplicate and near-duplicate auditing
baselines: Unconstrained, additive-only, random-orthogonal, true-factor-aligned, and factor-aligned with shuffled targets
Naive score composition, matched Feynman-Kac or drift correction, MCMC or energy correction, and object-centric diffusion
No replay, byte- and token-matched replay, duplicate-instance auxiliary, correct abstraction, relation-shuffled abstraction, and label-shuffled abstraction
Shallow, intermediate, and deep dense models plus parameter- and FLOP-matched sparse variants
Probe-only linear geometry, cross-fitted full-space geometry, and direct intervention metrics
ablations: Remove additivity or orthogonality while retaining the same factor labels
Rotate the orthogonal basis randomly while preserving dimension and norm
Shuffle factor-to-direction assignment across examples
Hold training fixed and change only the inference corrector and particle count
Hold abstraction fluency and length fixed while shuffling relations or labels
Match versus mismatch in-distribution loss, margin, parameters, tokens, and FLOPs
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if true factor alignment beats both random orthogonality and additive-only on preregistered held-out behavior, reduces cross-factor gradient covariance in the predicted pairs, survives the inference-correction and leakage controls, and transfers directionally to the natural split. If geometry changes without behavior, corrected sampling closes the gap, or shuffled abstractions match, reject the claimed causal primitive.

evaluation: Held-out-cell classification accuracy, conditional NLL, calibration, and exact zero-mass recombination rate
Analytic score residual where available, generated-cell MMD or energy distance, precision-recall, and factor consistency
Known-factor retention, unknown-factor acquisition, average forgetting, backward transfer, and forward transfer
Per-example cross-factor gradient covariance, cosine conflict, and selective intervention response
Cross-fitted additivity, orthogonality, subspace overlap, full-space predictivity, and causal mediation
In-distribution loss and margin, parameters, training tokens, FLOPs, wall-clock, sampler evaluations, and particle count
Duplicate and near-duplicate leakage, pretraining exposure, seed confidence intervals, and paired effect sizes
risks: True factor labels make the proposed arm privileged. Treat the experiment as a causal mechanism test and require the natural transfer arm to learn or approximate factors without privileged labels.
Matching achieved fit can change training duration and itself alter geometry. Register both equal-compute and equal-fit estimands and report them separately.
Linear metrics can miss nonlinear factor structure. Use full-space cross-fitted metrics and direct interventions, not only probes.
A diffusion sampler may dominate training geometry. Match score evaluations and include corrected-sampler arms before attributing generation failures to representation.
Generated abstractions can leak labels or generator style. Include semantically wrong but fluent controls and a human-blinded semantic audit on a small sample.
The factorial study is large. Use the fixed-architecture geometry test as the primary experiment and run the depth-sparsity grid only after it passes.
first_week: Generate and hash a complete two-factor image table, reserve exact zero-mass cells, and implement duplicate and near-duplicate audits.
Train one small encoder and conditional diffusion baseline and verify matched in-distribution fit across ten seeds.
Implement additive-only, random-orthogonal, and true-factor-aligned losses with identical dimensions and coefficient norms.
Log per-example factor gradients and cross-fitted representation metrics, then test whether the intervention changes both geometry and held-out behavior.
Add naive and corrected score samplers plus correct, relation-shuffled, and label-shuffled abstraction targets; preregister the full falsifier table.

competitive_landscape.title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts
competitive_landscape.difference: Feynman-Kac particle correction already targets products and guided distributions. The proposal makes matched correction a falsifier for any learned-geometry explanation.

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work characterizes when linear score composition works or fails. The experiment separates those inference conditions from learned factor-gradient geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Locality interventions restore one compositional failure mode and provide stronger causal evidence than representation correlations. Local score behavior is therefore a direct baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Composable diffusion introduced product-style score composition for new scenes. The proposal tests whether its failures come from inference correction or entangled training geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle: Compositional Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models and MCMC
competitive_landscape.difference: This work attributes composition failures partly to sampling and improves them with MCMC and energy parameterization. It is a required matched-compute alternative.

competitive_landscape.title: Object-Centric Slot Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Object slots build factorization into the architecture rather than imposing labeled orthogonal directions. The experiment tests it as a non-linear structural route.

competitive_landscape.title: SlotDiffusion: Object-Centric Generative Modeling with Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: SlotDiffusion tests object-centric generation across multiple datasets. It challenges any claim that linear factor alignment is the only useful compositional geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
competitive_landscape.difference: This theory derives support and architecture conditions for held-out composition. Exact zero-mass support and architecture matching in the proposal follow that stricter standard.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Compositional Generalization via Compositional Feature Alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: CFA already intervenes with compositional feature alignment and orthogonalized heads. The proposed novelty is the causal control suite across generation and continual retention.

competitive_landscape.title: Deciphering the Role of Representation Disentanglement: Investigating Compositional Generalization in CLIP Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work relates disentanglement and sparsity to unusual visual compositions without claiming exact orthogonality is universally necessary. It supplies a correlation baseline the intervention must exceed.

competitive_landscape.title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
competitive_landscape.difference: Kernel inductive bias and training dynamics can explain transfer without additive orthogonal embeddings. Matched architecture and fit controls test this alternative.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Object-Centric Representations Better At Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: This work finds conditional object-centric advantages under controlled diversity and compute. It is a key discriminator between universal necessity and regime-specific geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Data Scaling Lead to Visual Compositional Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: Persistent recombination gaps under data and model scaling show that exposure alone may not solve the problem. The proposal holds exposure fixed while intervening on geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: This predecessor establishes the evolved-image versus SGD setup behind the depth-sparsity claim. The proposal treats that axis as secondary and compute-matches it.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Lifelong Learning with A-GEM
competitive_landscape.difference: A-GEM directly constrains current gradients with episodic-memory gradients. It is the priority causal baseline for claims that abstractions help through reduced gradient interference.

competitive_landscape.title: Experience Replay for Continual Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Simple experience replay is a strong continual method. Token-, byte-, and FLOP-matched replay must lose before abstractions receive mechanism credit.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and a 44-paper focused panel: compositional score correction, projective composition theory, object-centric diffusion, additive and orthogonal feature alignment, representation disentanglement, kernel and support theories, depth and sparsity accounts, continual replay, gradient projection, and structural abstractions are established. The narrow contribution is a fixed-architecture intervention tournament that distinguishes correct factor alignment from random orthogonality, inference correction, replay, fluent semantic controls, and compute-matched depth or sparsity while measuring the proposed gradient mechanism directly.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 180 pages, with 27 page-anchored findings, 86 anchors, 20 evaluation audits, and 41 checked competitor entries spanning 40 unique primary papers.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
The models are small and data are synthetic, but censored survival estimates, 24-seed cells, width sweeps, and factorial learning-rate by batch-size controls create a meaningful compute budget.
Past-only forecasting, held-out AUPRC, survival calibration, matched trigger controls, finite-size tests, and same-checkpoint interventions provide direct pass/fail criteria.
Many criticality signals and grokking mechanisms already exist; the defensible novelty is their prospective, causally controlled tournament rather than another proposed observable.
Null forecasting and randomized-trigger results arrive quickly, while reliable transition-order and held-out transfer conclusions require the full replicated sweep.

assumptions: Every transition signal can be computed from a strictly past-only window without using the future grokking epoch for alignment or threshold choice.
Width populations can be synchronized on identical task, data, and checkpoint rules so the fitted avalanche exponent is not confounded by support changes.
Checkpoint clones can separate trigger information from dose, schedule, optimizer state, and update-covariance effects.
Finite-size and held-out-task gates are required before using phase-transition or early-warning language beyond the tested regimes.

brief.title: Prospective criticality or retrospective alignment? A causal transition tournament
brief.thesis: Freeze a past-only transition certificate on development tasks, compare it with loss, norm, mechanistic, information, spectral, avalanche, and stochastic-escape baselines on held-out runs, then intervene from identical checkpoints. A signal counts only if it improves transition-horizon forecasting and its true trigger beats dose-matched replayed and randomized schedules.
brief.motivation: Recent papers call attention-logit variance, gradient-avalanche dimension, stochastic barrier escape, and Bayesian attention order parameters evidence of critical transitions. The strongest claims currently depend on future-selected peaks, grokking-aligned trajectories, prepared checkpoints, width-mismatched controls, untested finite-size extrapolation, filtered optimizer failures, or a sign-inconsistent loss derivation. A single prospective tournament can distinguish an operational early warning from an attractive retrospective description.
brief.research_question: Can any frozen, past-only criticality certificate predict and causally advance held-out grokking or attention transitions after simpler training-state baselines, dose matching, finite-size scaling, and competing stochastic-escape laws are controlled?
non_claims: The project does not claim grokking, induction heads, neural avalanches, thermodynamic attention observables, stochastic metastability, or finite-size scaling as new.
A peak near a transition after future alignment is not an early-warning signal.
A useful controller does not establish a thermodynamic phase transition unless size sharpening, bimodality or hysteresis, and a coherent order parameter also pass.
A prepared deep-linear metastable checkpoint is a mechanism probe, not evidence that ordinary Transformer training follows the same escape path.
subquestions: Does a combined certificate add at least 0.10 held-out transition-horizon AUPRC beyond elapsed compute, loss derivatives, norms, and the strongest single observable?
Do true-signal interventions shorten transition time beyond fixed-dose, cross-seed replayed, randomized-trigger, and update-covariance-matched controls?
Does stochastic escape follow an Arrhenius law or the multiplicative-noise power-law alternative when learning rate and batch size are varied factorially?
Do avalanche-dimension and softmax-transition claims survive matched width support, past-only synchronization, factorized causal attention, and finite-size scaling?
method: Use modular addition across held-out moduli, widths, split fractions, and 24 independent seeds per cell, plus fused versus factorized and cyclic versus causal copy-head variants.
Predefine grokking as sustained training accuracy above 0.99 followed by validation accuracy above 0.95 for five checkpoints; treat runs without a transition as censored rather than dropping them.

Compute only past-window features: attention-logit variance and susceptibility, synchronized TDU-OFC avalanche dimension, barrier and noise-response probes, 2RDM spectra, mechanistic and information progress measures, loss derivatives, norms, and optimizer-state statistics.
Freeze feature definitions, thresholds, and a sparse hazard model on one development task, then test without recalibration on held-out moduli, split fractions, and attention variants.
Clone identical checkpoints into no-intervention, true-trigger weight decay, fixed-dose, cross-seed replayed, randomized-trigger, and update-covariance-matched noise arms.
Factorially vary learning rate and batch size while matching deterministic drift, then compare registered Arrhenius and multiplicative-noise power-law escape models out of sample.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: Small tasks may reject confounded signals but cannot certify universality. Freeze the complete forecast and intervention protocol before held-out moduli, widths, and factorized causal attention are opened.
supporting_evidence: The frozen certificate adds at least 0.10 transition-horizon AUPRC with a positive confidence interval on every held-out family
Calibration and coefficient signs remain stable across widths, moduli, split fractions, and attention parameterizations
True-trigger interventions outperform dose-matched replayed and randomized schedules from identical checkpoints
Finite-size curves sharpen consistently and the inferred transition order survives factorized causal attention
Registered noise-scale interventions distinguish the Arrhenius and multiplicative-noise power-law models out of sample
claim_blockers: Incremental AUPRC is below 0.10 or its confidence interval crosses zero
Performance requires future alignment or task-specific threshold recalibration
True triggers do not beat replayed, randomized, or fixed-dose schedules
The avalanche crossing disappears under identical width support or past-only synchronization
Softmax lacks size sharpening, bimodality, or hysteresis, or factorized causal attention changes the inferred order
The preferred stochastic-escape law reverses outside the fitted learning-rate range
prospective_design: Develop on one registered modular-addition family and one fused copy task
Freeze all windows, thresholds, features, exclusions, intervention doses, and statistical models
Open held-out moduli, data fractions, widths, and a factorized causal attention implementation only after freezing
Publish censored failures, optimizer instabilities, and null interventions alongside successful transitions
why_small_models_fail: Transition timing and even the existence of grokking depend on data fraction, regularization, width, and optimizer state
An exponent fit across six widths can be high leverage and need not extrapolate
A fused one-layer Bayesian attention model changes the implicit regularization and causal structure of practical Transformers
Prepared low-rank linear checkpoints can manufacture metastability absent from standard initialization
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If forecasting alone passes, claim a prospective predictor in the tested families. Use causal early-warning language only if identical-checkpoint interventions pass, and phase-transition language only when the registered finite-size and order tests also pass.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A frozen sparse certificate combining attention susceptibility with an independently measured stochastic-escape hazard will improve held-out transition-horizon AUPRC by at least 0.10 over elapsed compute, loss, norm, and every single-observable baseline.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: At checkpoints selected without future information, a true-signal intervention will reduce median transition time by at least 15% relative to every dose-matched replayed or randomized schedule without increasing failure incidence.
experiment.primary_outcome: Past-only transition-horizon AUPRC improvement over the strongest registered baseline on held-out task families; median transition time under true versus dose-matched triggers is the confirmatory causal outcome.
domains: Modular addition with held-out moduli, widths, train fractions, and seeds
Prepared and standard-initialization L2 deep-linear mode-learning controls
Fused cyclic copy attention as a theorem-aligned positive control
Factorized causal softmax and linear attention as held-out structural tests
baselines: Elapsed steps, tokens, wall time, training and validation loss, loss derivatives, weight and gradient norms
Mechanistic progress, information progress, 2RDM spectra, attention susceptibility, and avalanche dimension individually
No intervention, tuned fixed high decay, fixed-dose schedule, cross-seed replayed trigger, randomized trigger, and covariance-matched noise
Arrhenius linear-barrier and multiplicative-noise power-law escape models
Past-only sparse hazard model without criticality features
ablations: Remove each certificate coordinate and each registered interaction
Use future alignment versus past-only synchronization to quantify retrospective leakage
Match versus mismatch width support in the avalanche regression
Prepared low-rank checkpoints versus standard initialization
Vary learning rate only versus the full learning-rate by batch-size factorial
Fused versus factorized Q/K and cyclic versus causal attention
experiment.decision_rule: Pass forecasting only if the frozen certificate exceeds every baseline by at least 0.10 AUPRC with a positive cluster-bootstrap confidence interval on all held-out task families. Pass causal early warning only if true triggers also shorten transition time by at least 15% versus every dose-matched control. Otherwise report which observables are retrospective descriptions and reject the general certificate.

evaluation: Transition-horizon AUPRC, time-dependent concordance, calibration, Brier score, and lead time under censoring
Incremental value beyond compute, loss, norms, and single-observable baselines
Median transition-time ratio, failure incidence, final generalization, and matched intervention dose
Cross-task threshold stability and coefficient-sign stability
Finite-size sharpening, bimodality, hysteresis, susceptibility scaling, and order-parameter consistency
Arrhenius versus power-law held-out likelihood, calibration, and collapse under matched noise scale
Sensitivity to width support, future alignment, optimizer-failure inclusion, and factorized causal attention
risks: Grokking-time variance may make 24 seeds insufficient. Use sequential precision stopping and report censored confidence intervals rather than selectively excluding slow runs.
The candidate signals may be highly collinear with loss derivatives. Limit the certificate before held-out evaluation and require incremental, not marginal, value.
Trigger arms can differ in effective update magnitude. Match cumulative decay dose and update covariance and publish residual imbalances.
