experiment.primary_hypothesis: After an exactly balanced conditional-transition switch, preregistered probability-signature deltas will predict held-out embedding and unembedding Gram movement and subsequent contextual-region transport better than marginal, position, loss, norm, and shuffled-signature controls.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: The predicted geometry is functionally mediating: clamping it will reduce the switch-induced gain on sealed native behavior, while imposing it without the switch will recover part of that gain and norm-, rank-, and loss-matched random transports will not.
domains: Stationary finite-state Markov corpora with degree-preserving transition rewires and exact marginal audits
Semantically matched synthetic proposition corpora with counterbalanced templates and token codebooks
Tied- and untied-embedding 20M-50M decoder-only transformers across early and late training switches
One untouched transition family and one preregistered larger-decoder confirmation
baselines: No switch, byte-identical loader restart, marginal-only change, position-only change, and signature-shuffled switch
Unigram, PMI, elapsed tokens, train loss, gradient norm, embedding norm, and rogue-coordinate predictors
Global centered cosine, covariance-spectrum isotropy, PCA, K-means, MFA, SAE or unsupervised subspace, and random-region diagnostics
No clamp, true predicted-geometry clamp, predicted-geometry rescue, and random norm-, rank-, and loss-matched transport
One intrinsic-dimension estimator versus the preregistered PHD, MLE, TLE, and TwoNN panel
ablations: Remove reverse-token, adjacent-token, position-conditioned, or longer-context signature terms one at a time
Tie versus untie embedding and unembedding matrices
Measure before and after rogue-coordinate removal and held-out recentering
Fit regions on the evaluation activations versus the required disjoint cross-fit split to quantify selection leakage
Switch early versus late while matching remaining tokens and equal-achieved-loss checkpoints
Clamp parameter geometry alone versus parameter plus selected contextual-region geometry
experiment.primary_outcome: Cross-seed held-out improvement in preregistered pairwise geometry-movement prediction over the strongest non-signature baseline, followed by the paired change in sealed native behavior under the true switch, clamp, rescue, and random-transport arms.
experiment.analysis: Estimate randomized switch effects with checkpoint-blocked mixed models and seed-clustered intervals; evaluate prediction with held-out rank correlation, calibrated slope, and top-pair precision; test temporal ordering and preregistered causal mediation without selecting layers or estimators on the final behavior outcome. Correct the fixed primary family for multiple comparisons and report every estimator and abstention.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass the mechanism only if the frozen signature predictor beats every registered baseline with a positive seed-clustered interval in both corpus families, parameter movement precedes regional and dimension movement, the true switch improves sealed behavior, the clamp attenuates that improvement, the rescue restores a nonzero portion, and random transports do neither. Otherwise report a distribution-to-geometry correlation or a corpus effect and reject the causal transport claim.

falsifiers: A shuffled signature, unigram statistic, or achieved-loss trajectory predicts geometry as well as the named conditional terms.
Held-out clustering, covariance-spectrum, and multiple local-dimension estimators do not confirm the regional movement.
The geometry trajectory is concurrent with or later than the behavioral change rather than prospectively upstream.
Clamp, rescue, and random-transport arms fail to separate functional geometry from a passive coordinate change.
The intervention effect depends on unmatched tokenizer, position, entropy, semantic, compute, or contamination differences.
The frozen direction or calibration fails in the untouched family or larger confirmation.
evaluation: Exact corpus balance: vocabulary, unigrams, sequence length, position counts, row-entropy strata, latent proposition coverage, tokenizer counts, and duplicate hashes
Held-out pairwise Gram-delta rank correlation, calibration slope, top-k precision, sign accuracy, and abstention coverage
Centered within-region covariance spectra, IsoScore or uniformity, held-out assignment stability, centroid movement, principal-angle subspace transport, and neighborhood overlap
PHD, MLE, TLE, TwoNN, PCA dimension, estimator disagreement, bootstrap stability, and sensitivity to token count and density
Held-out continuation NLL, paraphrase-invariant proposition recovery, compositional path completion, multi-hop accuracy, and calibration
Clamp attenuation, rescue recovery, random-transport null effect, temporal lead, and preregistered mediation estimates
Training tokens, FLOPs, wall time, achieved loss, gradient and parameter norms, optimizer state, all seeds, and larger-run prediction error
risks: Exact matching may make the transition manipulation too weak. Increase sample size or the number of rewired edges under the frozen balance constraints rather than relaxing the confound controls after seeing outcomes.

The corpus conditionals may change an unmeasured higher-order statistic. Publish n-gram, entropy-rate, syntax-template, and latent-proposition audits and state the treatment as the complete generator intervention rather than one scalar signature when necessary.
MFA or clustering can manufacture apparent regions. Cross-fit partitions, compare K-means and nonparametric neighborhoods, require held-out likelihood, and permit abstention.
Intrinsic-dimension estimators can disagree or respond to density and length. Preserve the full estimator panel and reject any universal-dimension conclusion if results are estimator-specific.
Geometry penalties can change optimization or loss directly. Match loss, norm, rank, coefficient magnitude, and update budget and treat residual imbalance as a failed mediation gate.

A factorial with many diagnostics can invite selective reporting. Freeze one primary parameter endpoint, one primary native-behavior family, layers, pair-selection rules, and multiplicity correction before the held-out runs.
first_week: Implement two paired doubly stochastic transition matrices with identical stationary marginals and row-entropy spectra; unit-test every balance invariant and hash the corpora.
Compute adjacent, reverse, and position-conditioned signature deltas and freeze a small set of predicted moving, stable, and abstained token pairs.
Train eight seeds of one 20M tied-embedding decoder on the two corpus arms and verify equal tokens, FLOPs, loss logging, and checkpoint reproducibility.
Measure held-out Gram movement, covariance-spectrum isotropy, cluster stability, and the four-estimator local-dimension panel without using behavioral labels.
Add one mid-run true switch, sham switch, shuffled-signature control, and pilot Gram clamp; preregister the complete scale and mediation gate before expanding.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometric Signatures of Compositionality Across a Language Model's Lifetime
competitive_landscape.difference: This work manipulates dataset compositionality and follows nonlinear and linear dimension through training. The proposal instead preserves latent propositions and matched corpus statistics while randomizing selected transitions, freezes pairwise geometry predictions before training, and requires clamp/rescue evidence on native behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: The Shape of Learning: Anisotropy and Intrinsic Dimensions in Transformer-Based Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Razzhigaev et al. document anisotropy and expansion-compression dynamics across training. The proposed randomized corpus switch asks which conditionals cause those trajectories and whether their movement mediates behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Less is More: Local Intrinsic Dimensions of Contextual Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work uses local-dimension changes to anticipate optimization phenomena. Here local dimension is one preregistered downstream measurement of a randomized corpus treatment and cannot pass the claim without independent parameter predictions and native-behavior mediation.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Tokens in Internal Representations of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Viswanathan et al. relate token-cloud dimension, neighborhood overlap, cosine, and next-token loss. The proposal matches entropy and loss strata by design, then tests conditional-transition effects prospectively rather than inferring them from pooled correlations.

competitive_landscape.title: How Contextual are Contextualized Word Representations? Comparing the Geometry of BERT, ELMo, and GPT-2 Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Ethayarajh establishes anisotropy and context specificity in pretrained models. The proposal treats raw global cosine as a confounded baseline and identifies geometry change through randomized training data and held-out regional diagnostics.

competitive_landscape.title: Representation Degeneration Problem in Training Natural Language Generation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. connect likelihood training and weight tying to a narrow cone and add a cosine regularizer. The new experiment crosses tied and untied parameters, uses region-aware covariance tests, and asks whether specific conditional transitions move functional geometry rather than optimizing isotropy itself.

competitive_landscape.title: All Bark and No Bite: Rogue Dimensions in Transformer Language Models Obscure Representational Quality
competitive_landscape.difference: Rogue coordinates can dominate cosine while contributing little behaviorally. Removing or standardizing them is therefore a mandatory negative control before interpreting any predicted geometry transport.

competitive_landscape.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
competitive_landscape.difference: Engels et al. recover and causally validate circular manifolds for calendar computation. The proposal does not claim all geometry is pairwise or linear; it tests whether corpus-condition predictions propagate into local subspaces and behavior under explicit nonlinear-region alternatives.

competitive_landscape.title: Projecting Assumptions: The Duality Between Sparse Autoencoders and Concept Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows that decomposition architecture assumes a concept geometry and can fail under heterogeneous dimension or nonlinear separability. The proposal therefore triangulates MFA, SAE, covariance, and neighborhood diagnostics rather than treating one decomposition as ground truth.

competitive_landscape.title: Decomposing Representation Space into Interpretable Subspaces with Unsupervised Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang and Hahn learn global non-axis-aligned subspaces and connect them to known circuit variables. The proposed estimand is the causal movement of regions and subspaces after a frozen corpus intervention, with no claim that one decomposition supplies the unique coordinates.

competitive_landscape.title: A Latent Variable Model Approach to PMI-based Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Arora et al. derive static embedding geometry from co-occurrence under a latent discourse model. The proposal changes matched sequence conditionals experimentally and follows learned parameter and activation trajectories rather than assuming a fixed optimum-level factorization.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Word Embedding as Implicit Matrix Factorization
competitive_landscape.difference: Levy and Goldberg establish the shifted-PMI factorization view for SGNS. It is a required static baseline, while the proposal tests multi-signature transient dynamics, contextual regions, and causal behavior in trained decoders.

competitive_landscape.title: Initialization is Critical to Whether Transformers Fit Composite Functions by Reasoning or Memorizing
competitive_landscape.difference: Initialization can select reasoning versus memorization solutions with different vector structure. The experiment blocks on initialization, repeats the switch across early and late regimes, and rejects a corpus mechanism if initialization explains the geometry and behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
competitive_landscape.difference: MIB separates basis discovery from supervised causal-variable localization and finds supervised DAS strong. The proposal uses sealed native behavior and clamp/rescue interventions so unsupervised region movement is not mistaken for causal localization.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned readings spanning 99 pages, 29 findings, 111 page anchors, and 32 direct competitor inspections covering 30 unique primary papers: co-occurrence factorization, contextual anisotropy, regional manifolds, local intrinsic dimension, multidimensional features, sparse and subspace decompositions, developmental geometry, and causal localization are established. The nonredundant contribution is a preregistered intervention that holds marginals, entropy, position, semantics, and compute fixed; predicts pairwise geometry before training; follows transport into regions and estimator-robust dimension; and requires native-behavior clamp/rescue evidence. A descriptive geometry survey, generic orthogonality intervention, or retrospective corpus correlation would duplicate existing work.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 99 pages, with 29 page-attributed findings, 111 anchors, and 30 unique directly inspected primary competitors. The audited OpenReview preservation route is disclosed in its reading rather than represented as a live official download.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

A decisive pilot fits within public sub-3B checkpoints and rank-8 LoRAs, but repeated patch-ablate-rescue branches, resource-matched active auditors, program synthesis, adversarial input search, and audit-aware target training make the complete tournament materially more expensive.

Five separately preregistered, noncompensatory gates; exact positive and negative controls; identical frozen artifacts; hidden challenge sets; native interventions; and query- and resource-matched black-box comparators give direct pass, abstain, or fail outcomes.

AuditBench, MIB, InterpBench, predictive-interpretation tests, identifiability analyses, actionability studies, and adversarial monitoring already cover individual pieces. Novelty survives only in the frozen five-gate conjunction and must not drift into another circuit benchmark, plausibility score, or causal-localization leaderboard.

A 20-organism, two-method pilot can quickly reveal whether known-good and matched-null artifacts separate and whether the active black-box comparator closes the claimed gap. Adaptive target training, untouched-family transfer, and a stable tournament ranking require longer replication.

assumptions: Program, feature, attribution, and circuit explanations can be normalized into a common artifact contract without pretending that their explanatory boundaries are identical.
Public checkpoints and existing Pando, RelP, activation-patching, attention-replacement, ICA, and SAE implementations can be reproduced at the pinned source revisions.
Native patch, ablate, and rescue interventions are computationally feasible and remain within a monitored activation-distribution envelope on the selected sub-3B models.
A black-box auditor can be matched under both target-query and total-resource ledgers without converting implementation details into an unfair advantage.
Counterexample generators and audit-aware target variants can be trained on development artifacts while keeping adversary families, prompts, models, and final challenges untouched.
Known-circuit and planted-rule controls are rich enough to calibrate gate thresholds but are not treated as evidence of large-model transfer.
A null result in which no current explanation clears all five gates remains publishable if positive controls pass and the gates diagnose distinct failures.

brief.title: Counterexample-Guided Explanation Tournaments
brief.thesis: Freeze each program, feature, attribution, or circuit explanation before any hidden challenge is opened, then require it to clear five noncompensatory gates: prospective failure prediction; native mediator patch-ablate-rescue; matched-null and equivalence-class handling under program or coordinate non-identifiability; adaptive counterexample and rationale-or-trace spoofing resistance; and actionable value beyond query-budget- and resource-matched black-box auditors. An explanation earns a certificate only when every gate passes on an untouched model family; readability, in-distribution fit, probe accuracy, patching magnitude, or one successful edit cannot compensate for a failed gate.
brief.motivation: The four full readings occupy different rungs of an evidence ladder without closing it. ICA Lens yields readable hypotheses and supervised probe utility but no native behavioral mediation or adversarial test. The TabPFN study patches and ablates native predictions, yet necessity and restorability diverge, descriptive entropy is not causal, and transfer is limited to one checkpoint and two synthetic functions. Attention programs are executable and can substitute for attention matrices, but globally reused generic programs often beat head-conditioned programs, values and OV paths remain neural, and all alignment selection is TinyStories in-distribution. Pando makes held-out behavior prediction and a budget-matched transcript central, but its output-sensitive fields are not internally patched mediators and its fixed disjoint rationales are not an auditor-adaptive adversary. Existing benchmarks separately test hidden-behavior auditing, known circuits, causal variables, prediction, identifiability, or actionability. A frozen tournament is useful only if it forces those standards to meet on the same artifact and preserves failure rather than averaging it away.
brief.research_question: Does a preregistered five-gate certificate identify explanations that prospectively support specific, low-collateral audit actions on hidden inputs and audit-aware models better than explanation plausibility, in-distribution fit, a single causal-localization score, or a resource-matched active black-box auditor?
non_claims: The project does not discover a preferred feature basis, recover a true feature geometry, compare superposition levels, or treat ICA, SAE, neuron, probe, and program coordinates as an identified ontology.
It does not learn a predictive state, a future-sufficient world-model representation, or a latent dynamics model; prospective prediction is only an evaluation gate for a frozen explanation.

It explicitly excludes the reviewed superposition-robustness causal factorial: there is no manipulation of dictionary interference or activation-support entropy and no claim that superposition causes adversarial vulnerability.
It does not propose another MIB- or InterpBench-style circuit localization score; causal localization is one necessary gate and cannot establish the full claim.

It does not require a unique mechanistic explanation when the model is non-identifiable. A valid artifact may report an equivalence class or abstain, but it may not claim uniqueness unsupported by counterfactual evidence.
It does not infer faithfulness from human readability, attention alignment, kurtosis, probe accuracy, patching magnitude, or behavior preservation under a single intervention.
It does not claim that a fixed misleading rationale is strategic deception; adaptive target and counterexample arms are reported separately from ordinary unfaithfulness.
It does not claim that passing on planted rules, known circuits, GPT-2, TabPFN, or one 2B model establishes safety for frontier models or natural hidden objectives.
Gate scores are not collapsed into a compensatory scalar leaderboard; one failed gate blocks the certificate.
subquestions: Do explanations that make calibrated signed predictions about unseen failures outperform same-fit descriptions selected only for plausibility or in-distribution alignment?
When necessity, restorability, and rescue disagree, which intervention pattern predicts whether the claimed mediator supports a specific behavior-preserving edit?

Can an explanation recognize its own equivalence class or abstain when function-preserving coordinate changes, globally reused programs, redundant heads, or alternate circuits fit the observed evidence equally well?
How much explanation validity survives counterexample-guided token, length, syntax, field, corruption, and prompt search after the artifact and all thresholds are frozen?

Do white-box artifacts add actionable information beyond an active black-box auditor when target queries, evaluator tokens, backward passes, wall time, and intervention calls are charged in separate ledgers?

Does training a target to preserve task performance while spoofing rationales, traces, or a known audit statistic change the relative ranking of program, gradient, RelP, SAE, ICA, and circuit artifacts?
Which gate failures transfer from known-circuit and planted-rule organisms to an untouched checkpoint family, and which are artifacts of the synthetic ontology?
Can a low-cost development certificate predict final actionability without tuning thresholds, adversary strength, intervention dose, or artifact budget on the held-out family?
method: Define a common explanation-artifact contract before experiments: target behavior, input scope, predicted success and failure regions with uncertainty, claimed mediator boundary, permitted equivalence class or abstention, and a concrete patch, ablation, rescue, or edit policy. Retain each method's native representation and do not force scalar attributions to masquerade as executable programs.

Calibrate the harness on known positives and negatives: InterpBench- or RAVEL-style known circuits and planted Pando or TabPFN rules as positive controls; wrong-head programs, globally generic programs, random directions matched on activation tails or probe score, redundant-head pruning, corrupted patch pairs, and sham rationales as negative or non-identifiable controls.

Create development artifacts from four families represented in the readings: synthesized attention programs; ICA and SAE feature artifacts; gradient and RelP field or token artifacts; and head or block localization from patching and ablation. Fix artifact count, complexity budget, synthesis calls, feature budget, intervention dose, and allowed post-processing per family.

Freeze every artifact, scope statement, equivalence claim, abstention rule, gate threshold, counterexample budget, evaluator prompt, target-query schedule, and statistical model before opening any hidden examples or held-out target family.

Gate 1, prospective validity: require each artifact to assign calibrated probabilities or signed ranks to model-behavior errors, attention-proxy divergence, or intervention failure on untouched inputs and domains. Score log loss, AUROC, calibration, worst-group error, and incremental value beyond current loss, confidence, probe score, IoU, and transcript-only predictors.

Gate 2, causal localization: at identical inputs run patch, ablate, and rescue interventions at the artifact's declared boundary, separating necessity from restorability and measuring native loss or behavior, specificity, collateral effects, activation-distribution shift, and dose response. Compare with random, same-magnitude, same-layer, pruning, and corrupted-pair controls.

Gate 3, non-identifiability: search for equal-observation alternatives by global program reranking, wrong-head swapping, program mutation, seed and corpus refits, matched random directions, feature permutations, and function-preserving basis changes. Pass an asserted mechanism only if hidden counterfactuals distinguish it; otherwise require an explicit equivalence-class or abstention output whose members agree on the audit action.

Gate 4, adaptive faithfulness: use a development red team to generate inputs that maximize frozen explanation-model disagreement, then evaluate on unopened attack families and target organisms trained to preserve task behavior while emitting misleading rationales, obfuscating traces, or rerouting around a known audit statistic. Keep ordinary distribution shift, fixed unfaithfulness, input-adaptive attacks, and target-adaptive evasion as separate strata.

Freeze a finite Gate-5 action ontology for each target family before hidden evaluation: declare hidden behavior present, absent, or abstain; choose the next probe from a registered menu; choose no-op, monitor, human escalation, or one target-specific patch, ablation, disablement, or edit from a registered intervention menu. Every action has an executable success predicate, collateral bound, and resource cost; artifacts may not invent or redefine actions after the holdout opens.

Gate 5, black-box actionability: give a frozen audit policy the artifact and ask it to detect hidden behavior and select among preregistered interventions. Compare with random, sample-only, prefill, hypothesis-aware, active-learning, and counterexample-search black-box auditors first at equal target-query budget and then under a resource ledger that reports backward passes, evaluator tokens, intervention calls, FLOPs, wall time, and memory as separate Pareto dimensions.

Use a strict certificate vector rather than a mean score. Thresholds come only from development positive and negative controls; the primary result is the fraction and identity of artifacts whose one-sided intervals clear every gate, with all failures and abstentions retained.

Open a staged transfer suite only after the small-model protocol is frozen: new functions and corruptions, new text domains and lengths, a checkpoint from an untouched architecture family, new explanation styles, and a held-out adaptive adversary. No artifact regeneration, threshold refitting, or method-specific extra query is allowed.

Release the artifact schemas, hidden-split commitments, resource ledgers, generated counterexamples after evaluation, intervention traces, evaluator transcripts, null artifacts, and failed certificates so later methods can enter without changing the tournament.

validation_funnel.gate: Known-circuit and planted-rule positives clear the relevant gates; matched wrong, random, generic, corrupted, and deliberately non-identifiable artifacts fail or abstain at preregistered rates. If the harness cannot separate these controls, stop.

On hidden natural inputs, artifacts predict their own failure regions and their claimed mediators pass patch-ablate-rescue specificity beyond dose-, layer-, pruning-, and corruption-matched controls without threshold adjustment.

Artifacts either distinguish equal-fit alternatives on hidden counterfactuals or correctly report an actionable equivalence class or abstention; generic programs, coordinate changes, redundant circuits, and matched random directions do not receive false unique-mechanism certificates.

Frozen artifacts retain registered worst-case validity under unopened counterexample and spoofing families and improve successful, low-collateral audit actions beyond both interaction-matched and resource-matched active black-box auditors.

The complete five-gate decision rule, artifact budget, adversary budget, and resource conversion transfer without refitting to an unopened checkpoint family; failures and abstentions are counted rather than excluded.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: Small known-circuit and planted-rule organisms can validate the measurement gates, but they cannot establish that a method is faithful or actionable on larger natural models. Freeze the artifact API, gate thresholds, intervention doses, equivalence search, red-team budget, resource ledgers, evaluator prompts, and hierarchical analysis on the development suite before opening the 2B-3B family and one untouched architecture.
supporting_evidence: Positive controls continue to pass and matched negative or non-identifiable controls continue to fail or abstain as model size, context length, and task complexity increase.
Gate-1 calibration and the signed ranking of hidden failures transfer without regenerating explanations or selecting easier inputs.

Patch-ablate-rescue effects retain target specificity and acceptable collateral damage at the declared mediator boundary, while activation-distribution-shift diagnostics stay within registered bounds.
Equivalent programs, circuits, and coordinate systems are either separated on hidden counterfactuals or mapped to the same actionable equivalence class rather than arbitrarily ranked.
Worst-case performance survives unopened counterexample generators and an audit-aware target variant that was not optimized against the evaluated artifact instance.
White-box actionability remains above an active black-box Pareto frontier under both equal target interactions and explicit compute, evaluator-token, intervention, memory, and wall-time ledgers.

The first-four-gate certificate prospectively predicts Gate-5 audit success with calibrated held-out probabilities and adds information beyond plausibility, fit, probe, patching, and model-confidence baselines.
claim_blockers: Known-good circuits or planted rules do not pass, or wrong, generic, random, corrupted, or non-identifiable controls pass at a material rate.
Any gate threshold, artifact budget, counterexample strength, intervention dose, evaluator prompt, or resource conversion must be retuned on the held-out model family.
In-distribution fit or human plausibility predicts actionability as well as the frozen multi-gate certificate.
Patch, ablation, and rescue give incompatible mediator conclusions that cannot be modeled prospectively, or effects disappear under matched pruning and corruption controls.
Function-preserving coordinate changes or equal-fit alternate programs reverse the claimed mechanism while leaving the certificate unchanged.
An active black-box auditor matches the white-box audit action at equal query budget, or dominates once tool compute and evaluator tokens are charged.
Adaptive counterexamples collapse validity to chance, or the target learns to spoof the audit statistic without a registered abstention.
Only synthetic explicit-field organisms pass, while natural text, longer context, or the untouched architecture reverses the ranking.
Reported success depends on dropping failed synthesis runs, nonconverged bases, unstable heads, unsuccessful attacks, or artifact abstentions.
prospective_design: Develop the artifact schema, gate thresholds, resource ledgers, and positive or negative controls on TabPFN functions, known-circuit transformers, GPT-2, and a small subset of Pando-style LoRAs.
Freeze methods and analysis before opening new Pando rules, TinyLlama or Gemma-2 test organisms, non-TinyStories corpora, longer contexts, and unseen corruption families.

Keep one architecture family such as Qwen or Llama-3.2, one rationale-spoofing recipe, one trace-obfuscation recipe, and one counterexample-generator family completely unopened until all four preceding gates pass.
Publish every artifact, including failed program synthesis, nonconverged ICA layers, ambiguous features, negative patching recoveries, red-team failures, and abstentions.
why_small_models_fail: Known decision trees and circuits supply exact ontology and mediator ground truth that natural language-model computations may not possess.
Head and feature redundancy, model scale, tokenizer, context length, and residual compensation can change the relation between local interventions and behavior.
ICA, SAE, gradient, and program artifacts can be stable on simple corpora yet fail on long, multilingual, code, dialogue, or compositionally novel inputs.
A small LoRA model emitting a fixed distractor rationale is not a situationally aware model that detects and strategically evades an auditor.
Black-box active learning and counterexample search scale differently from backward passes and circuit tools, making any scalar resource conversion contestable.
At larger scale an actionable explanation may be an equivalence class of distributed mechanisms rather than a unique head, feature, or short program.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only calibration and synthetic gates pass, claim a validated small-model evaluation harness. If natural hidden inputs pass but the adaptive or black-box gate fails, report the artifact as predictive or causally localized but not adversarially faithful or incrementally actionable. Claim a five-gate certificate only for the frozen model, behavior, explanation family, and resource ledger that pass. Never claim feature-geometry recovery, predictive-state learning, a causal link from superposition to vulnerability, unique mechanistic truth, or frontier-model safety.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: After artifacts and thresholds are frozen, explanations that clear prospective prediction, native causal localization, non-identifiability handling, and adaptive counterexample gates will achieve a positive paired improvement in successful low-collateral audit actions over a query-budget- and resource-matched active black-box auditor on hidden inputs; in-distribution fit, human plausibility, probe score, IoU, or patching magnitude alone will not predict that improvement as well.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: The frozen five-gate decision rule will retain calibration on an untouched checkpoint family, while several currently strong methods will change rank across gates and fixed-unfaithfulness performance will overestimate robustness to audit-aware rationale or trace spoofing.
experiment.action_ontology: For each target family, freeze the allowed decisions (present, absent, abstain), next probes, and no-op, monitor, human-escalation, patch, ablation, disablement, or edit interventions before hidden evaluation. Score an action as successful only when its executable target-family predicate passes, collateral remains below the registered bound, and its complete resource charge is recorded.
domains: Known-circuit semi-synthetic transformers and RAVEL-style causal-variable tasks for positive-control and non-identifiability calibration
TabPFN-2.5 regression checkpoints on multiplication, pairwise interactions, and unopened symbolic or piecewise functions with exact input-feature interventions
Pando-style Gemma-2-2B-Instruct rank-8 LoRAs across faithful, no-explanation, fixed-unfaithful, and separately trained audit-aware rationale or trace-spoofing conditions
GPT-2 Small and TinyLlama-1.1B attention programs synthesized on TinyStories development data and tested on hidden corpora, constructions, and context lengths
ICA, SAE, gradient, RelP, program, and patching artifacts on small Gemma, Qwen, or Llama residual and attention targets
One unopened 2B-3B architecture family, new behavior generator, new counterexample family, and non-TinyStories corpus reserved for final transfer
baselines: Sample-only and fixed-prefill black-box auditors receiving the identical labeled transcript
Active black-box decision-tree, uncertainty-sampling, disagreement-search, and counterexample-search auditors at equal target-query budget
A resource-matched black-box Pareto frontier charged the white-box method's evaluator tokens, backward passes, intervention calls, FLOPs, memory, and wall time

Human or language-model plausibility ratings, description confidence, program length, attention IoU or JSD, ICA kurtosis and ERF, SAE reconstruction and sparsity, probe score, model confidence, and current loss
Ordinary gradients, RelP, logit lens, residual-token similarity, ICA, public SAEs, program proxies, patching, ablation, and circuit-tracing families under fixed per-family budgets
Globally best wrong-head and intended attention programs, fixed local or diagonal programs, head pruning, and same-IoU program mutations
Random, PCA, ITDA, same-layer, same-norm, same-kurtosis, same-probe-score, and feature-permutation controls
Corrupted clean pairs, random heads or components, same-magnitude activation edits, pruning controls, and no-op rescue interventions
Oracle planted rule or known circuit as an upper positive control and deliberately non-identifiable equivalence classes as abstention controls
ablations: Remove each of the five gates one at a time and test the frozen reduced certificate's incremental log score and audit actionability
Compensatory average score versus strict minimum-margin and all-gates conjunction
Fixed natural challenge set versus counterexample-guided inputs and target-adaptive evasion
Patch only, ablate only, rescue only, and the complete necessity-restorability-specificity triplet
Attention-matrix replacement versus value-weighted head-output and full OV-output replacement
Head-conditioned program versus global library program, matched program mutation, and pruning
ICA seed, corpus, normalization, and component-count refits; SAE dictionary, width, and sparsity variants; function-preserving basis changes
Fixed unfaithful rationale versus input-adaptive rationale spoofing, trace obfuscation, and mediator rerouting
Equal-query versus equal-wall-time, equal-FLOP, and separate multi-resource Pareto comparisons
Generic common evaluator versus method-specific frozen parser, with evaluator errors scored separately
Synthetic exact ontology versus natural hidden inputs and explicit-field versus latent-feature targets
experiment.primary_outcome: The artifact-level five-gate certificate and its final actionability margin. For every frozen model-method-target block, report the vector of one-sided gate margins and whether all clear preregistered thresholds; Gate 5 is the paired expected utility of decisions, probes, and interventions from the frozen target-family action ontology relative to the strongest active black-box auditor under equal-query and resource-matched ledgers. The headline is the proportion of artifacts with a positive lower interval on every gate, never their mean gate score.
experiment.analysis: Treat model, seed, behavior, explanation family, artifact, and adversary family as crossed or nested effects. Estimate paired gate margins with seed- and model-clustered hierarchical bootstrap intervals; calibrate thresholds only on development positive and negative controls; use proper log scores, calibration slopes, AUROC, worst-group loss, necessity and rescue contrasts, off-target effects, attack success, abstention coverage, and Pareto dominance. Fit one preregistered sparse model that predicts Gate-5 actionability from Gates 1-4 and compare its held-out log score with plausibility, fit, probe, IoU, patching, and black-box-only predictors. Correct the fixed method-by-gate family for multiplicity, preserve unsuccessful synthesis and attack runs, model abstentions explicitly, and publish family-specific estimates before any hierarchical aggregate.
experiment.decision_rule: Promote an explanation family only if known positives pass and matched negatives do not; its frozen artifact has a positive one-sided interval on every gate; the first-four-gate certificate improves held-out prediction of Gate-5 actionability beyond all single-axis baselines; its Gate-5 policy has higher expected utility under the frozen target-family action ontology than the active black-box comparator at equal queries and beyond the resource-matched Pareto frontier; and the complete result repeats without refitting on the untouched family. If actions, success predicates, collateral bounds, or costs are changed after hidden outcomes open, Gate 5 fails. If any gate fails, label the artifact only by the evidence it earned and reject a faithfulness or actionable-explanation claim.

evaluation: Gate 1: hidden-input log loss, AUROC, sign accuracy, calibration slope and error, worst-group prediction loss, and incremental held-out log score
Gate 2: native behavior or loss change under patch, ablation, and rescue; necessity-restorability asymmetry; dose response; specificity; collateral behavior; and activation-distribution shift
Gate 3: counterfactual separation of equal-fit programs, circuits, and coordinate systems; false-uniqueness rate; equivalence-class action agreement; abstention coverage and risk
Gate 4: attack success, worst-case metric retention, rationale or trace spoof rate, mediator-rerouting rate, and transfer across unopened counterexample and target-adversary families
Gate 5: paired hidden-behavior detection, successful intervention selection, off-target bound violations, and expected audit utility versus active black-box comparators
Control calibration: positive-control pass rate, negative-control false-pass rate, deliberately non-identifiable abstention rate, and gate-threshold stability
Resource ledgers: target queries, tokens, synthesis and evaluator calls, backward passes, patch branches, FLOPs, peak memory, wall time, and human-review minutes
Cross-model transfer: effect-sign stability, calibration drift, ranking changes, abstention rate, and no-refit certificate rate on the unopened family
Secondary plausibility: blinded human readability, semantic agreement, uncertainty communication, and their correlation or dissociation from each evidence gate
falsifiers: Known-circuit and planted-rule positive controls fail a gate, or matched wrong, random, generic, corrupted, or deliberately non-identifiable controls receive certificates.
Human plausibility, attention fit, probe performance, patching magnitude, or model confidence predicts held-out actionability as well as the frozen first-four-gate certificate.
A globally reused wrong-head program, matched random direction, feature permutation, or function-preserving coordinate change passes while making a contradictory mechanism claim.
Patch, ablation, and rescue do not agree prospectively on when the claimed mediator supports a low-collateral edit, or matched pruning and corruption controls reproduce the effect.
Counterexample search reduces Gate-1 or causal specificity to chance, and the registered artifact neither predicts the failure nor abstains.
Fixed unfaithfulness appears harmless but an audit-aware target reliably spoofs or reroutes around the same method on unopened variants.
The strongest active black-box auditor matches white-box actionability at equal queries or dominates after tool compute and evaluator cost are charged.
The all-gate conjunction adds no held-out information beyond a simpler MIB-style causal score, AuditBench-style agent result, or prediction-only benchmark.
Method rankings or gate calibration reverse on the untouched architecture, domain, context length, or adversary family without a preregistered abstention condition.

Success requires regenerating artifacts, changing gate thresholds, increasing a method-specific budget, dropping failed methods, or weakening the collateral-damage bound after hidden outcomes are opened.
Only explicit-field, shallow-rule, or known-circuit organisms pass, providing no evidence on natural text behavior.
The benchmark accidentally measures feature geometry, predictive-state quality, or the superposition-vulnerability factorial rather than the declared explanation artifact and audit action.

human_in_the_loop.answer: Humans are not part of gate optimization, target labeling, causal localization, attack search, black-box matching, or the certificate. They are useful only for a blinded secondary audit of whether artifacts are genuinely readable, whether adversarial examples preserve the intended task, and whether a reported equivalence or abstention is understandable to an auditor.
humans_not_needed_for: Planted-rule and known-circuit ground truth, target-model outputs, hidden-split assignment, artifact freezing, counterexample generation, patch-ablate-rescue execution, and resource accounting
Gate thresholds, method rankings, intervention selection, multiplicity correction, transfer decisions, or promotion language after outcomes are visible
Semantic labels for exact synthetic variables or executable unit tests for synthesized programs
humans_needed_for: Blindly rate a fixed random sample of program, feature, and circuit artifacts for readability and calibrated uncertainty without seeing gate outcomes
Audit whether natural-language counterexamples, rationale spoofs, and long-context perturbations preserve task meaning and do not reveal hidden labels
Review a preregistered sample of equivalence-class and abstention reports for whether they communicate the limits needed for safe audit action
human_in_the_loop.measurement: Report reviewer hours, sample rate, expertise strata, inter-rater agreement, task-preservation rate, readability calibration, and correlations between human plausibility and each gate. Human ratings remain a secondary diagnostic; a highly plausible artifact that fails a gate remains uncertified.

risks: A common artifact API can privilege executable programs over feature or attribution methods. Preserve native outputs, use family-specific parsers frozen before evaluation, and interpret cross-family aggregation only after within-family controls pass.

Patching can create off-manifold activations or conflate availability, necessity, and restorability. Monitor activation support, use multiple corruption schemes, and require patch-ablate-rescue plus native behavioral outcomes.
The equivalence search can never prove uniqueness. Frame Gate 3 as falsification, equivalence-class reporting, and calibrated abstention rather than proof of a true mechanism.

A red team can overfit one artifact serialization or expose hidden labels. Separate input attacks from target-adaptive evasion, hold out generator families, and blind humans to outcomes when validating semantics.

Audit-aware target training may reduce task quality or merely learn the training attack. Match clean behavior, confidence, and loss; reserve unseen audit methods and behavior generators; report strategic-awareness evidence separately.
Query and compute matching has no universally accepted scalar exchange rate. Publish interaction-matched results and a multi-resource Pareto frontier rather than one monetized score.

An external evaluator model can be the bottleneck or leak world knowledge. Freeze prompts and versions, compare generic and method-specific parsers, score extraction error separately, and include non-LLM controls where possible.
Many gates, methods, adversaries, and outcomes create multiplicity and researcher degrees of freedom. Freeze a primary vector, hierarchical model, thresholds, and all exclusions; release every cell.
No current method may pass all five gates. The project remains informative only if controls validate each gate and the failure taxonomy is stable and prospective.
Synthetic ground truth can make the tournament clean but unrepresentative. Treat it as calibration, reserve natural text and an untouched family, and limit claims when transfer fails.

Competitor overlap is substantial. If the project becomes a causal-variable leaderboard, known-circuit benchmark, prediction-only test, audit-agent bakeoff, or actionability case study without the frozen conjunction, reject it as redundant.
first_week: Write the versioned explanation-artifact schema and exact five gate definitions, including the finite target-family action ontology, executable action-success predicates, equivalence and abstention semantics, collateral-damage bounds, and the two black-box resource ledgers.

Reproduce one Pando no-explanation and unfaithful model with sample-only, gradient, and RelP agents; reproduce one GPT-2 attention-program replacement and one TabPFN patch-ablate result from the pinned papers.

Implement three positive controls and at least six negative or non-identifiable controls: oracle rule, known circuit, exact program; wrong-head program, matched pruning, random direction, corrupted patch pair, coordinate transform, and sham rationale.
Build the active black-box auditor with uncertainty sampling and disagreement or counterexample queries, and log target calls, tokens, wall time, FLOPs, and intervention calls separately.
Implement a bounded counterexample search over TabPFN fields and text tokens or constructions, with a hidden semantic-validity split and no target-adaptive training yet.
Run at least 20 model-method-target blocks to estimate gate variance, control error rates, abstention behavior, intervention collateral, and the cost of the resource-matched comparator.

Preregister thresholds, artifact budgets, evaluator prompts, method parsers, attack budgets, hidden domains, target-adaptive recipes, untouched family, primary hierarchical analysis, multiplicity correction, and every decisive falsifier before scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: AuditBench: Evaluating Alignment Auditing Techniques on Models with Hidden Behaviors
competitive_landscape.difference: AuditBench evaluates 56 models with 14 hidden behaviors and exposes both a strong black-box agent and a tool-to-agent utilization gap. This proposal freezes the explanation artifact itself and requires prospective, causal, non-identifiability, adaptive-counterexample, and resource-matched actionability gates; it is not another broad agent leaderboard.

competitive_landscape.title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
competitive_landscape.difference: MIB scores precise, concise recovery of causal pathways and variables across two tracks, four tasks, and five models. This proposal treats MIB-style localization as Gate 2, then blocks a certificate unless the same frozen artifact predicts hidden behavior, handles equal-fit alternatives, resists adaptive spoofing, and improves a black-box audit action.

competitive_landscape.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
competitive_landscape.difference: InterpBench uses Strict Interchange Intervention Training to produce realistic transformers with known circuits and evaluates circuit discovery. The tournament uses such models to calibrate controls but adds hidden prospective challenges, equivalence handling, adaptive adversaries, and a black-box actionability gate on natural pretrained models.

competitive_landscape.title: Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable?
competitive_landscape.difference: The paper enumerates Boolean-network explanations and shows multiple circuits, algorithms, and subspaces can satisfy standard criteria, motivating predictive and manipulability standards. Gate 3 operationalizes that warning through matched alternatives, hidden counterfactuals, equivalence classes, and abstention without claiming that the tournament proves uniqueness.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
competitive_landscape.difference: The clinical triage study shows near-perfect probe discrimination can coexist with ineffective or damaging steering. This proposal makes low-collateral audit action the fifth gate across controlled organisms and matched black-box policies; it does not generalize its small-model results to clinical safety.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
competitive_landscape.difference: Turpin et al. show that prompt biases can change answers while chain-of-thought rationalizes them without naming the influence. This proposal uses fixed unfaithfulness only as one stratum and adds input-adaptive counterexamples, audit-aware target spoofing, white-box artifacts, and native interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Interpretation Predict Behavior on Unseen Data?
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. make prediction on unseen inputs a criterion for interpretation. The tournament adopts that as Gate 1 but requires the same frozen artifact also to pass native causal, equivalence, adaptive-faithfulness, and black-box-actionability gates.

competitive_landscape.title: Attention is not Explanation
competitive_landscape.difference: Jain and Wallace show that different attention distributions can support similar predictions and attention can diverge from feature importance. The tournament turns alternate explanations into matched Gate-3 nulls and adds full head-output interventions and adversarial counterexamples rather than treating attention replacement alone as proof.

competitive_landscape.title: RelP: Faithful and Efficient Circuit Discovery in Language Models via Relevance Patching
competitive_landscape.difference: RelP is validated against activation patching on IOI and improves circuit discovery efficiency. The tournament evaluates whether a frozen RelP artifact predicts unseen failures, survives matched corruption and adaptive evasion, and improves audit action beyond black-box access; approximation to patching alone clears only part of Gate 2.

competitive_landscape.title: RAVEL: Evaluating Interpretability Methods on Disentangling Language Model Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: RAVEL supplies controlled attribute-value interventions and causal criteria for distributed representations. This proposal can reuse that setting as a calibration domain but does not search for a better representation; it tests a frozen explanation's full evidence and actionability chain.

competitive_landscape.title: Auditing language models for hidden objectives
competitive_landscape.difference: Marks et al. run a realistic blind multi-team audit of a model with a hidden reward-related objective and then study eight techniques. The tournament trades realism for repeated paired artifacts, exact controls, frozen gates, and scalable adversarial evaluation, while retaining an untouched-family audit as a transfer requirement.

competitive_landscape.title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
competitive_landscape.difference: Baker et al. show that optimizing against chain-of-thought monitors can promote obfuscated reasoning. This proposal treats monitor-aware pressure as Gate 4, compares internal and black-box artifacts, and requires held-out adversary families rather than inferring adaptive faithfulness from fixed misleading text.

competitive_landscape.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Sleeper Agents demonstrates persistent conditional backdoors and strategic reasoning through safety and adversarial training. The tournament uses narrower audit-aware organisms to attack frozen explanation statistics and measure abstention or actionability; it does not claim to remove deceptive objectives.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. learn sparse residual features and include a native circuit case study. The tournament accepts SAEs as one artifact family but neither discovers feature geometry nor treats interpretability or one causal example as a certificate; SAE artifacts face all five gates and function-preserving nulls.

competitive_landscape.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
competitive_landscape.difference: Heimersheim and Nanda distinguish corruption, restoration, metric, and causal-interpretation choices in activation patching. The proposal turns those cautions into the Gate-2 patch-ablate-rescue protocol and then tests whether localized effects predict hidden actionability.

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing Multi-Head Self-Attention: Specialized Heads Do the Heavy Lifting, the Rest Can Be Pruned
competitive_landscape.difference: Voita et al. show that many attention heads can be pruned while specialized heads carry task behavior. The tournament uses matched pruning and redundancy as nulls so behavior preservation after program replacement is not automatically counted as faithful explanation.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and direct inspection of the closest primary benchmarks: individual ingredients are established. AuditBench covers hidden-behavior audit agents and the tool-to-agent gap; MIB and InterpBench score causal variables and known circuits; RAVEL tests causal representation criteria; predictive-interpretation work tests unseen behavior; non-identifiability work shows multiple circuits, algorithms, and subspaces can fit; the actionability study shows excellent internal prediction need not enable safe correction; unfaithful-CoT, sleeper-agent, and monitor-obfuscation work cover increasingly adversarial rationales or targets. The defensible novelty is therefore only the frozen, noncompensatory five-gate tournament on the same artifact, ending in a resource-accounted black-box actionability comparison and transferring to an unopened adversary and model family. The 21-flagship audit is clean but only at this boundary: four briefs generate or validate RL environments; reliability-gated skill transfer evaluates research-agent skills; causal-maturity diffusion search and finite-noise score-norm gap study diffusion signals; gradient-viability certificates and activation-aware basis garbage collection study continual updates or representation maintenance; causal predictive-state studies future-sufficient video state and is explicitly excluded; Muon crossover, prospective criticality, search-versus-gradient, learning-rate-controller, and curvature-clamp briefs study optimizer choice, transitions, or subgroup allocation; factor-aligned geometry and causal representation transport study learned geometry; symmetry-breaking localization studies world-model breakers; causal data-value surfaces studies training examples; and the superposition-robustness factorial manipulates interference to explain vulnerability and is explicitly excluded. Shared prospective and falsifier discipline is a design pattern, not the research object. If the proposal loses the all-five-gates boundary, omits adaptive counterexamples, or drops the query- and resource-matched black-box comparator, it becomes redundant with those external benchmarks and should be rejected.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 103 pages, with 48 page-anchored findings, 157 anchors, and 38 checked competitor entries spanning 37 unique primary records. The closest-work audit additionally checked current primary pages for AuditBench, MIB, InterpBench, mechanistic-interpretability non-identifiability, interpretation without actionability, and unfaithful chain-of-thought.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
Formal finite POMDPs need no collected data and support multi-fidelity search, but training several architectures, sizes, and seeds remains the dominant cost.
Oracle state, exact transitions, sequence correctness, held-out return, intervention response, and exploit checks make the central mechanism-discrimination claim unusually falsifiable.
Environment evolution, formal-language benchmarks, feature provenance, and head compression already exist. Novelty depends on the closed adaptive loop and prospective mechanism predictions.
A small automaton suite can test whether evolution finds held-out mechanism splits quickly, while cross-scale and compression claims need longer runs.

assumptions: Finite POMDP genomes can expose transition semigroup, aliasing, and reward structure to an oracle while hiding latent state from agents.
Training compute can be matched closely enough that return differences are not simple budget artifacts.
Mechanistic measurements are collected on held-out mutations rather than used both as search fitness and final evidence.
Scaling is claimed only if environment rankings and effect directions remain stable with uncertainty across at least three sizes.

brief.title: Evolutionary mechanism-discriminating RL environments
brief.thesis: Evolve formal, partially observed environments in which models reach matched training return but diverge under controlled shifts and causal interventions. Use those environments to distinguish brittle parallel Transformer shortcuts from robust recurrence or correctly keyed external memory, then test whether gradient provenance and inter-head predictability forecast which solution will generalize or compress safely.
brief.motivation: Fixed automata already reveal that Transformers can solve training lengths through parallel shortcuts that fail out of distribution. Separately, next-token training can create features through direct, pre-cached, or shared gradients, and attention heads can be linearly predictable without being causally replaceable. Formal memory analogies can also be wrong: one reviewed paper's claimed Transformer-to-DNC equivalence omits the query projection and addresses stored values rather than stored keys. An adaptive environment loop can turn these disconnected diagnostics into prospective tests of algorithm choice instead of post hoc stories.
brief.research_question: Can evolutionary search generate finite-state and partially observed RL environments that discriminate learned algorithms under shift, and can gradient provenance plus causal head reconstruction predict which matched-performing agents will remain robust or safely compressible?
non_claims: The project does not claim new automaton expressivity theory or generic environment evolution.
High in-distribution return does not identify the algorithm used by an agent.
High linear head-reconstruction R² does not establish causal redundancy or safe cache removal.
Ordinary Transformer attention is not treated as an exact DNC: the memory baseline stores separate keys and values and reads stored keys with projected queries.
subquestions: Which transition-semigroup, aliasing, reset, delay, and distractor properties create reproducible architecture or mechanism splits after difficulty is controlled?
Do direct, pre-cached, and shared gradient provenance measured during training predict held-out state tracking better than linear decodability alone?
Does causal key-only or value-only head reconstruction predict compression sensitivity better than observational Q/K/V R²?
method: Represent mutable finite POMDPs with known transition semigroups, observation aliasing, boundary resets, delayed rewards, distractors, and explicit length and symbol-frequency shifts.
Require every mutation to pass oracle reachability, reward determinism, hidden-state consistency, exploit resistance, and nontrivial random and heuristic baseline tests.
Train small Transformers, LSTMs or GRUs, and a corrected external-memory baseline that stores separate key-value pairs and addresses stored keys with projected queries.
Evolve for matched in-distribution return but maximal held-out disagreement in return, exact latent-state recovery, sequence correctness, and causal intervention response.
Across checkpoints, measure direct, pre-cached, and shared gradient influence; Q/K/V predictability; projection overlap; and key-only versus value-only causal reconstruction.
Freeze a mechanism-risk predictor and environment archive before testing unseen mutation families, three model sizes, and new seeds.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The evolved-environment result and the mechanism-risk predictor are separate claims. Only the secondary predictor may receive cross-scale language, and only within the tested POMDP families, architectures, and three registered sizes.
prospective_design: First freeze and validate the mechanism-discriminating environment archive on unseen mutation families and seeds at development scale.
Only after that primary gate passes, freeze predictor features, coefficients, thresholds, and compression interventions before opening the larger sizes and held-out architecture.
Keep environment search fitness and final scale outcomes disjoint so the archive cannot adapt to the held-out ranking.
supporting_evidence: Evolved environments preserve matched-return mechanism splits on unseen mutation families
The frozen predictor improves OOD and compression-failure ranking over return, decodability, and observational R-squared at every registered size
Causal key/value reconstruction interventions preserve their registered ordering across sizes
claim_blockers: The primary environment-discovery gate fails before scale testing begins
Predictor rank, calibration, or intervention ordering reverses across registered sizes or architecture
A scale result requires environment reselection, predictor refitting, or target-aware compression thresholds
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Report the environment-discovery result independently. Say 'the secondary mechanism-risk predictor transferred across the tested sizes and architecture' only if its untouched gates pass.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: Quality-diversity evolution will find oracle-valid environments that produce larger and more reproducible held-out mechanism splits than random generation, regret-only evolution, or prioritized replay at matched training difficulty and compute.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: A frozen predictor using gradient provenance and causal head reconstruction will rank OOD and compression failures better than return, state decodability, or observational R² alone across held-out mutations and scale.
experiment.primary_outcome: The matched-difficulty and matched-compute architecture or mechanism split in held-out return, exact latent-state recovery, sequence correctness, and causal intervention response on unseen mutation families and seeds.
experiment.claim_hierarchy: Environment discovery is the primary claim. The cross-scale mechanism-risk and compression predictor is a secondary claim tested only after the primary environment gate passes; failure of the secondary claim does not erase a successful primary result.
domains: Finite semiautomata with solvable and non-solvable transition structure
Partially observed keyed-memory tasks with observation aliases and delayed reads
Boundary-reset and distractor environments with controlled length and symbol-frequency shifts
baselines: Uniform random valid environment generation
POET-style mutation and transfer
PAIRED regret-based generation
PLR adaptive replay without mutation
ACCEL regret-guided environment editing
Fixed automata and formal-language benchmark suites
Return-only and linear-decodability-only mechanism predictors
ablations: Remove transition-semigroup descriptors from the genome and predictor
Remove partial observability, resets, delays, or distractors one at a time
Replace quality-diversity with a single disagreement objective
Use observational Q/K/V R² without causal reconstruction
Remove gradient provenance features
Use an incorrectly value-addressed memory baseline instead of separate stored keys and values
experiment.decision_rule: Stage 1 passes only if evolved environments retain larger architecture or mechanism splits on unseen mutation families and seeds after matching difficulty, return, and compute; reward bugs or generic difficulty fail this primary claim. Only if Stage 1 passes, Stage 2 tests the frozen predictor, which requires stable held-out ranking across three scales and better calibration than return, decodability, and R². A Stage-2 scale reversal rejects the predictor claim but does not retroactively invalidate a passed Stage-1 environment result.

evaluation: In-distribution return balance and held-out return disagreement with bootstrap uncertainty
Exact latent-state recovery, full-sequence correctness, and length or symbol-frequency generalization
Causal state, key, value, and head-reconstruction intervention effects
Gradient-provenance attribution and observational Q/K/V predictability across checkpoints
Predictive calibration and rank stability for OOD and compression failures across three sizes
Archive coverage over semigroup structure, aliasing, delay, reset, distractor, and memory demands
Oracle-test failure, reward exploit, training FLOPs, environment evaluations, and wall-clock cost
risks: Evolution may discover reward bugs or generic difficulty. Enforce oracle checks, match success and compute, and keep invalidity out of the fitness reward.
Mechanism labels may rely on probes that are not causal. Require intervention and counterfactual behavior, not state decodability alone.
Semigroup structure may add no value after surface difficulty controls. Test its incremental held-out prediction explicitly.
Head R² can remain high while key or value replacement breaks behavior. Use causal reconstruction and report latency as well as memory savings.
The corrected memory baseline may behave like ordinary attention on small tasks. Include delayed overwrite, aliasing, and key-value dissociation tests that can separate them.
Environment rankings may reverse across scale. Treat that as evidence against a general scaling claim and report the boundary.
Humans are unnecessary for formal validity; add blinded review only if later environments use semantic or safety-sensitive reward specifications.
first_week: Implement a typed finite-POMDP genome and independent oracle for reachability, transitions, reward, and latent state.
Reproduce one fixed automaton shortcut failure with a Transformer and recurrent baseline.
Add one keyed-memory task whose correct solution requires separate query, stored key, and stored value paths.
Run random mutation with validity filters and verify that difficulty and return can be matched before optimizing disagreement.
Instrument one checkpoint for gradient provenance, Q/K/V R², and causal key-only and value-only reconstruction.
Preregister held-out mutation families, scale criteria, mechanism outcomes, and reward-bug rejection rules.

competitive_landscape.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
competitive_landscape.difference: POET co-evolves environments and specialist solutions for open-ended complexity. This project evolves finite POMDPs for reproducible mechanistic discrimination between matched-performing agents.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: PAIRED uses protagonist-antagonist regret for solvable curricula. This project targets cross-architecture OOD, state-recovery, and causal-intervention disagreement.

competitive_landscape.title: Prioritized Level Replay
competitive_landscape.difference: PLR selects existing levels by learning potential. It tests whether mutation adds value beyond intelligent replay and resampling.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolving Curricula with Regret-Based Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ACCEL edits levels toward the capability frontier using regret. This project evolves formally characterized state machines toward algorithm-identifying and compression-sensitive counterexamples.

competitive_landscape.title: Cayley Maze: Universal Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning Environment
competitive_landscape.difference: Cayley Maze parameterizes finite deterministic MDP complexity with automata and group theory. This project adds partial observability, controlled shifts, multi-architecture comparison, and causal validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
competitive_landscape.difference: This work exposes parallel Transformer shortcuts on fixed automata. The proposed loop makes construction adaptive and uses held-out failures as evolutionary fitness.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Networks and the Chomsky Hierarchy
competitive_landscape.difference: This benchmark compares architecture-dependent length generalization broadly. The proposed study narrows to oracle-auditable finite POMDPs and adds evolution plus causal interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding the Emergence of Seemingly Useless Features in Next-Token Predictors
competitive_landscape.difference: This work attributes features to direct, pre-cached, and shared gradients. The proposed study tests whether those signatures prospectively predict robustness across evolved environments.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Predictability of Attention Heads in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work measures and exploits inter-head Q/K/V predictability. The proposed study requires held-out causal reconstruction rather than equating R² with safe compression.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Attention Memory
competitive_landscape.difference: Neural Attention Memory provides readable and writable attention memory with DNC comparisons. It supplies a correctly typed query-key-value baseline for state tracking.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four page-anchored readings and primary-source review: automaton simulation and shortcut failures, formal-language generalization, evolutionary environment design, gradient-provenance attribution, inter-head reconstruction, and explicit attention memory are all established components. The defensible contribution is the closed loop that evolves held-out mechanism-discriminating POMDPs and then prospectively tests whether causal provenance and redundancy measurements predict OOD and compression failure across scale. The reviewed stateless-DNC paper is negative evidence, not a foundation: its exact-equivalence theorem omits the query projection, addresses stored values instead of stored keys, misattributes the DNC, and has invalid citations.
brief.evidence_note: This synthesis is supported by four page-anchored collection readings with seven checked primary competitors per paper. One source paper is retained as a high-confidence negative audit: its central equivalence theorem is invalid as written, so the proposal uses a corrected keyed-memory control and makes no DNC-equivalence claim.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
Thousands of candidate updates at 100M and 300M scale are tractable; the frozen 1B and second-architecture holdouts are the main compute cost.
Immediate learning, long-horizon retention, mode mass, policy behavior, instability, calibration, and intervention ordering can all be measured with sealed checkers.
Each proposed coordinate has close prior work. The defensible contribution is their frozen prospective joint certificate across retention, utility, stability, and unseen scale.
A reduced checker-verifiable benchmark can quickly reject weak diagnostics before the longer continual and cross-scale runs.

assumptions: Old and new skills can be evaluated with independent checkers and state-shifted policy rollouts.
Candidate updates can be logged before optimizer state is changed and replayed under controlled interventions.
The certificate form and limited interactions are specified before the 1B-scale holdout.
A cross-scale claim requires stable direction, calibration, and intervention ordering, not merely a positive small-model result.

brief.title: Gradient viability certificates for continual post-training
brief.thesis: Before accepting an LM update, measure whether it can reach useful task directions, preserve old support, avoid pathological attention routing, and remain inside a proposal-specific step-risk radius. Fit a small prespecified certificate on cheap updates, freeze it, and test whether it predicts retained learning at a held-out scale and architecture.
brief.motivation: Gradient norm and immediate loss do not say whether an update teaches useful behavior, removes old support, is attenuated through the output head, concentrates through sink paths, or crosses a dangerous softmax step scale. Recent work analyzes these mechanisms separately: output-head gradient compression, support-conditioned forgetting, complex softmax radii, and gradient sinks. A joint measurement is valuable only if it forecasts downstream retained learning before the update and adds value beyond ordinary optimizer statistics.
brief.research_question: Can four pre-update measurements prospectively predict whether a language-model update will learn new behavior, retain old behavior, and remain stable across model scale?
non_claims: The project does not claim a new divergence, output head, attention gate, or optimizer theorem.
Retained token likelihood does not establish retained policy behavior under state shift.
A large projected gradient norm does not establish task-calibrated update utility.
A diagnostic that works at 100M parameters is not a scaling result.
subquestions: Does target/reference support and replay location forecast old-mode mass separately from within-mode competence?
Does task-calibrated signal transmitted through the LM head add predictive value beyond total retained gradient norm?
Do realized attention-path concentration, RMSNorm attenuation, and complex-radius-normalized step size predict harmful updates after conventional curvature and optimizer controls?
method: Create checker-verifiable two-mode supervised and RL tasks with controllable old/new support, overlap, replay coverage, vocabulary, reward hacking, and state shift.

At 100M and 300M scale, log support/replay coverage, task-calibrated LM-head transmission, attention-path concentration with realized RMSNorm attenuation, and complex-radius-normalized step size before thousands of candidate updates.
Measure immediate loss change plus 100- and 1,000-step new-skill gain, old-skill retention, mode mass, within-mode drift, policy behavior, and instability.
Fit a prespecified additive certificate with only a small registered set of pairwise interactions; compare with loss, gradient norm, curvature proxies, replay count, and optimizer statistics.
Freeze the certificate before a 1B model and second architecture, then intervene with numerator replay, radius clipping, controlled head-rank widening, and value-path scaling.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The certificate is scale-valid only if a form frozen at 100M and 300M preserves calibration, ranking, effect signs, and intervention ordering on the untouched 1B model and second architecture.
prospective_design: Freeze coordinate definitions, preprocessing, coefficients, interactions, thresholds, missingness handling, and intervention policies on the development scales.
Keep the 1B checkpoint family and second architecture unavailable until the certificate and baseline comparison are committed.
Publish all candidate updates and abstentions at the held-out scale without refitting.
supporting_evidence: Improved held-out calibration and top-k retained-learning ranking over conventional diagnostics
Stable direction and standardized effect of each surviving coordinate across scale and architecture
Interventions preserve their registered new-skill gain at a fixed old-skill-retention threshold
claim_blockers: Certificate ranking, calibration, or effect signs reverse at 1B or on the second architecture
Scale transfer requires changing coordinate definitions, interactions, or thresholds
Token-likelihood retention improves while state-shifted policy behavior or checker agreement worsens
