scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'prospectively calibrated over the tested 100M-to-1B range and the registered architectures.' Do not claim an architecture- or scale-universal update certificate.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: The frozen four-coordinate certificate will improve held-out prediction of retained learning and harmful updates over conventional diagnostics at 1B scale and on a second architecture.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Interventions selected by the surviving diagnostic coordinates will improve new-skill gain at a fixed old-skill-retention threshold more reliably than generic clipping or replay alone.
experiment.primary_outcome: Held-out calibration and top-k ranking of retained-learning utility at the 1B and second-architecture holdouts, with new-skill gain at a fixed old-skill-retention threshold as the intervention outcome.
domains: Two-mode synthetic language tasks with exact old/new support and overlap controls
Checker-verifiable reasoning post-training with state-shifted policy rollouts
A held-out semantic task audited for reward/checker proxy failures
baselines: Update loss, gradient norm, cosine conflict, and optimizer moments
Lanczos or Hessian-vector curvature and edge-of-stability proxies
Replay count, old-token coverage, and target success probability alone
Norm clipping and fixed trust-region or KL constraints
Single-coordinate certificates for support, head transmission, sink routing, or complex radius
An unconstrained nonlinear predictor with matched validation data
ablations: Remove each of the four certificate coordinates in turn
Replace task-calibrated head transmission with retained gradient norm
Use attention concentration without realized RMSNorm attenuation
Use complex radius without Hessian and logit-scale controls
Remove state-shifted policy evaluation
Refit rather than freeze the certificate at the held-out scale
experiment.decision_rule: The primary claim passes only if the frozen certificate improves preregistered held-out calibration and ranking of retained-learning utility over conventional diagnostics at 1B and on the second architecture, with stable effect signs. If rankings reverse or only in-sample fit improves, report the scale boundary and reject the general certificate claim.

evaluation: Calibration error, Brier score, AUROC, and top-k precision for harmful versus retained-learning updates
New-skill gain at fixed old-skill retention after 100 and 1,000 updates
Old-mode probability mass, within-mode accuracy, state-shifted policy return, and reward-to-checker gap
Incremental predictive value over loss, gradient norm, curvature, replay count, and optimizer statistics
Effect-sign, standardized-effect, calibration, and intervention-order stability across three scales
Numerator-replay, radius-clipping, head-rank, and value-path intervention effects under matched compute
JVP/VJP, memory, wall-clock, and logging overhead per candidate update
risks: A flexible predictor could hide that no coordinate generalizes. Limit interactions, preregister them, and compare against a simple additive model.
Support coverage may preserve token distributions but not policies. Keep state-shifted behavior and reward hacking in the primary outcome.
Projected-norm loss may not reflect task directions. Calibrate with per-task influence or add-one-in utility rather than norm alone.
Complex radius can mark benign large steps as dangerous. Include successful above-radius and harmful below-radius cases and compare with catapult and curvature accounts.
Value-path interventions change the forward pass. Measure forward activation and attention changes so diagnostic improvement is not misattributed to gradient routing.
The certificate may lose calibration at 1B scale. Do not retune on the holdout; publish the boundary and the failed coordinates.

Instrument one 100M checkpoint for all four pre-update coordinates and conventional diagnostics.
Replay 200 proposed updates and measure immediate plus 100-step retained-learning outcomes.
Plot coordinate redundancy, missingness, overhead, and simple out-of-sample calibration.
Preregister the additive form, interactions, 1B holdout, primary outcome, and scale-claim blockers.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Dissent in Language Model Training and Saturation
competitive_landscape.difference: This work measures token-gradient conflict and saturation. The certificate combines transmission with support, routing, and step risk and tests retained-learning outcomes prospectively.

competitive_landscape.title: Why do small language models underperform? Studying Language Model Saturation via the Softmax Bottleneck
competitive_landscape.difference: This work connects narrow representations to late-pretraining saturation. The proposed study tests individual update viability across fixed checkpoints and scales.

competitive_landscape.title: Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: This work identifies on-policy data as a major retention factor. The certificate treats support as one coordinate and tests its incremental value with three optimization channels.

competitive_landscape.title: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Naturally Mitigates Forgetting in Continual Post-Training
competitive_landscape.difference: This work attributes retention benefits to reinforcement fine-tuning and reward-variance regularization. The certificate is objective-agnostic and prospectively separates support, transmission, routing, and step scale.

competitive_landscape.title: RL Forgets! Towards Continual Policy Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: This benchmark finds severe continual-RL forgetting. The proposed certificate must forecast its failures before long training and beat old-task regularization diagnostics.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
competitive_landscape.difference: Edge-of-stability statistics use Hessian sharpness. The certificate must show incremental value from proposal-specific output geometry and other coordinates.

competitive_landscape.title: A Loss Curvature Perspective on Training Instability in Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work explains instability through curvature and optimizer interventions. The certificate predicts retained learning and proposal-specific risk rather than curvature alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Why Gradient Clipping Accelerates Training: A Theoretical Justification for Adaptivity
competitive_landscape.difference: Norm clipping adapts to gradient magnitude under generalized smoothness. The proposed controller conditions on support, task-calibrated transmission, realized routing, and directional logit radius.

competitive_landscape.title: Value-State Gated Attention for Mitigating Extreme-Token Phenomena in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: This work already gates values and analyzes extreme-token gradients. The certificate uses realized attenuation as a predictor and controls for forward-path changes.

competitive_landscape.title: The Spike, the Sparse and the Sink: Anatomy of Massive Activations and Attention Sinks
competitive_landscape.difference: This work separates forward functions of massive activations and attention sinks. The certificate tests whether the phenomena forecast update utility rather than assuming a backward regulatory role.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four page-anchored readings and a primary-source competitor review: output-layer bottlenecks, continual-post-training retention, curvature and clipping diagnostics, attention sinks, value gating, and complex softmax step scales each have substantial prior work. The defensible contribution is a frozen, prospective joint certificate that predicts useful retained learning before an update, adds value beyond conventional diagnostics, and is tested without retuning at a larger scale and second architecture. A new diagnostic correlation at one checkpoint is not enough.
brief.evidence_note: This synthesis is supported by four page-anchored collection readings with 32 findings and seven checked primary competitors per paper. The certificate and scale transfer remain untested hypotheses.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
Synthetic simulator data are cheap; dense layer and diffusion-time extraction, causal patches, and native long-horizon rollouts dominate cost.
Exact latent simulator state, matched-prefix equivalence classes, future divergence, and independent rollout oracles provide unusually sharp falsifiers.
Physics probing, diffusion inversion, predictive-state geometry, cognitive maps, and manifold steering are crowded; exact degeneracy plus independent causal mediation is the narrow delta.
A two-law, two-backbone pilot can reject visual shortcuts quickly, while credible multi-model causal replication is slower.

assumptions: The simulator can generate prefixes matched on visible statistics and immediate futures while hidden physical state changes longer futures.
At least one evaluated model exposes internal activations and a native likelihood or rollout interface.
On-manifold state patches can be norm- and quality-matched to off-layer and random-direction controls.
A world-state claim requires raw-example predictive sufficiency and native behavioral mediation, not mean-state probes or decoder-only steering.

brief.title: Same prefix, different future: causal predictive-state tests for video world models
brief.thesis: Construct pairs of videos that are matched on pixels, tracks, optical flow, and the immediate next-step distribution but differ in hidden mass, friction, support, or occlusion state and therefore diverge later. A representation counts as a usable physical state only if it exposes the exact future-sufficient variable under weak probes, transfers across renderers or laws, and causally changes the model's native long-horizon prediction in the simulator-correct direction.
brief.motivation: Recent video encoders and diffusion transformers contain linearly decodable physical labels, often at intermediate depth, and their representations can sometimes be steered. Those results do not separate world state from visual or motion shortcuts, a powerful temporal probe, the VAE, generic quality effects, or decoder-only behavior. Predictive-state work in discrete walkers supplies a sharper construction: histories with the same immediate prediction but different full futures. Moving that idea into video creates an independent causal test rather than another probe leaderboard.
brief.research_question: Do video foundation and diffusion models internally encode a future-sufficient physical state that is invariant to visual shortcuts and causally used by their own long-horizon predictions?
non_claims: Linear label readout alone is not evidence that a model understands or uses physics.
Intermediate-depth emergence, diffusion inversion, predictive-state geometry, spatial maps, and on-manifold steering are established components, not new claims.
A patched external decoder is not a causal test of the model's native world prediction.
Success on one renderer or law does not establish a general physical world model.
subquestions: Can weak probes recover exact per-example future-sufficient state after pixels, centroids, tracks, optical flow, and VAE features are matched?
Does the state survive source-grouped splits and transfer across renderer, object identity, and held-out physical law?
Do on-manifold state transplants change native likelihoods or rollouts while appearance and generic generation quality remain stable?
Does the same causal criterion distinguish encoder representations from diffusion block-by-time trajectories?
method: Use a simulator to build short-horizon-equivalence classes for collision, support, occlusion, and latent material properties. Pair prefixes on RGB statistics, object tracks, optical flow, and immediate next-step distributions while forcing their longer futures to diverge.

Extract every encoder layer and selected diffusion block-by-time states. Evaluate activation-to-state and state-to-raw-activation fits with source-grouped train/test splits and both weak and deliberately strong probe controls.
Measure per-example reconstruction of the exact full-future sufficient vector, not only class labels or state means, then test cross-renderer and cross-law transfer without probe retuning.

Transplant an on-manifold hidden-state representation between matched prefixes and require the model's native likelihood or rollout to move toward the donor simulator future. Match patch norm and generic quality with random-direction, off-layer, appearance-only, and state-only controls.
Compare encoders, diffusion models, VAE features, random and untrained backbones, and explicit visual-motion baselines under identical probe capacity and search budgets.

validation_funnel.gate: Pixels, centroids, tracks, optical flow, VAE features, and random or untrained backbones must not match the candidate representation under identical probes.
A weak probe must recover the exact per-example future-sufficient state and distinguish immediate-prediction-matched prefixes on grouped holdouts.
The readout must preserve direction and calibration across an untouched renderer, object set, and at least one held-out law without retuning.
On-manifold patches must change the model's own long-horizon prediction toward simulator truth while appearance and generic quality controls remain stable.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A representation chosen by a development-only layer or diffusion-time selection rule will distinguish short-horizon-matched prefixes through a weakly decoded future-sufficient state and causally mediate simulator-correct native long-horizon predictions beyond every visual-motion baseline.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: The development-selected layer or diffusion-time location that maximizes cross-validated weak-probe predictive sufficiency will retain controlled native-rollout mediation and cross-renderer transfer on unopened pairs.
experiment.primary_outcome: Cross-renderer or cross-law raw-example recovery of future-sufficient simulator state under the frozen development-only layer or diffusion-time selection rule, followed by simulator-direction native-rollout mediation under norm- and quality-matched on-manifold patches.
experiment.selection_protocol: Choose one layer or diffusion-time rule using grouped cross-validation on development laws only, including its tie-break, probe family, and multiplicity correction. Freeze that rule before the renderer, physical-law, and causal-patch holdouts are opened; no 'best of all layers' target result is admissible.
domains: Two-body collision with latent mass and restitution
Support and friction with visually matched contact configurations
Occlusion and object permanence with divergent hidden trajectories
Grid-walker bridge task as an exact discrete positive control
baselines: Pixels, centroids, tracks, optical flow, and explicit short-horizon predictors
VAE latents, random features, untrained architecture, and shuffled temporal order
Weak linear probe and matched-capacity temporal probe
Published physics-label and violation-of-expectation probes
Off-layer, random-direction, decoder-only, and appearance-only interventions
State-space oracle and simulator-native sufficient statistic
ablations: Remove exact immediate-prediction matching
Replace grouped splits with random frames
Average states before decoding instead of scoring raw examples
Hold probe capacity fixed versus tune it per model
Patch off-manifold or without norm and quality matching
Evaluate an external decoder without native likelihood or rollout change
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if the frozen development-selected weak-probe representation beats every visual-motion and random or untrained control on raw-example future-state recovery, transfers to the registered renderer or law, and its norm-matched on-manifold patch changes native long-horizon predictions toward simulator truth without a generic quality or appearance shift. A result obtained only by selecting the best held-out layer or diffusion time fails. Otherwise narrow the result to correlational readout or reject the world-state claim.

evaluation: Per-example exact-state error and full-future distribution divergence within matched-prefix classes
Incremental prediction over pixels, tracks, optical flow, VAE, and immediate-next-step baselines
Cross-renderer, cross-object, and cross-law calibration and effect-sign retention
Native rollout error or likelihood shift toward the donor simulator future after intervention
Mediation effect with norm-matched random, off-layer, appearance-only, and state-only controls
Generic generation quality, perceptual identity, and artifact rates after patches
Probe capacity, search budget, seeds, activation storage, and wall-clock cost
risks: Perfectly matched visible prefixes may be impossible for some continuous laws. Quantify residual imbalance and adversarially predict the hidden state from every baseline before interpreting model activations.
A strong temporal probe can compute physics rather than read it. Make the weak probe primary and use the strong probe only as an upper-bound control.
State patches may leave the activation manifold or damage generation. Use nearest-neighbor or low-rank on-manifold transplants and predeclare quality tolerances.
Native rollout APIs differ across encoders and diffusion models. Define model-specific outcomes before looking at effects and avoid comparing incommensurate likelihoods as one score.
Cross-renderer failure may reflect low-level distribution shift rather than absent state. Include a renderer-adaptation control that cannot see target physics labels.
A positive discrete grid result may not transfer to video. Treat it as a construction check, not evidence for continuous-world claims.
first_week: Implement one collision simulator with latent mass and generate immediate-prediction-matched divergent-future pairs.
Train pixels, centroids, tracks, optical-flow, VAE, random, and untrained-backbone baselines with grouped splits.
Extract all layers from one open video encoder and test weak versus temporal probes on raw examples.
Define a native prediction outcome and prototype norm-matched on-manifold state transplants on 100 pairs.
Preregister the second law, renderer holdout, quality gate, probe budgets, and causal decision rule.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Physics in Video World Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work maps layerwise direction and preliminary interventions. It does not use exact predictive-state degeneracy or require simulator-grounded native rollout mediation.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Video Foundation Models Understand Intuitive Physics? A Layerwise Probing Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper compares probe capacity across encoders and a diffusion model, but its strongest readout can learn temporal computation and model or search budgets are unmatched.

competitive_landscape.title: The Invisible Hand of Physics: When Video Diffusion Models Know More Than They Show
competitive_landscape.difference: This work probes recovered diffusion trajectories and block-noise outcomes. The proposed study uses an independent simulator oracle and native causal rollout rather than the same probe surrogate.

competitive_landscape.title: Predictive Statistics Shape Emergent World Representations of Grid Walkers
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper supplies immediate-prediction-degenerate but full-future-distinct walker states. The proposal moves the construction to video and adds raw-activation, transfer, untrained, and causal controls.

competitive_landscape.title: Intuitive physics understanding emerges from self-supervised pretraining on natural videos
competitive_landscape.difference: This work establishes violation-of-expectation and physics readout in predictive encoders. It does not prove that the native model uses a future-sufficient physical state.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
competitive_landscape.difference: This work reconstructs full-future sufficient state in hidden Markov models. The proposal supplies continuous physical equivalence classes and native video interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Constrained Belief Updates Explain Geometric Structures in Transformer Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper derives representation geometry from constrained updates. It narrows mechanism novelty but does not test visual physics or native rollout mediation.

competitive_landscape.title: Cognitive Maps in Language Models: A Mechanistic Analysis of Spatial Planning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work already combines spatial representations, interventions, and generalization. The proposal requires exact matched-prefix physical state and simulator-scored video futures.

competitive_landscape.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
competitive_landscape.difference: Manifold steering connects geometry and behavior, including physical video dynamics. The proposed state transplants are constrained by an exact hidden-state oracle and matched-prefix future divergence.

competitive_landscape.title: Physion++: Evaluating Physical Scene Understanding that Requires Online Inference of Different Physical Properties
competitive_landscape.difference: Physion++ evaluates online inference of mass, friction, and elasticity. It lacks exact equivalence classes and internal causal mediation, but provides a strong task and negative baseline.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and a ten-paper primary-source review: physics readout, intermediate-depth emergence, diffusion inversion, belief-state geometry, spatial cognitive maps, and on-manifold behavior steering are established. The defensible contribution is the exact short-horizon-degeneracy construction for continuous video plus an independent simulator-grounded causal mediation test across encoder and diffusion representations. Another probe score, attention map, decoder-only intervention, or claim that decodable labels equal physical understanding would not be novel.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 91 pages, with 43 page-anchored findings and 38 direct-primary competitor entries spanning 26 unique IDs. The ten-paper brief landscape uses primary arXiv records.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
The small-scale tournament is tractable, but multi-scale Hessian-vector products, optimizer branching, repeated tuning budgets, and the untouched 1.5B-scale run are expensive.
Identical-checkpoint candidate updates, matched norms and function-space movement, realized loss change, and frozen cross-scale predictions give crisp causal falsifiers.

Angular decay, river-valley switching, spectral flattening, batch-noise geometry, NDS, curvature accounts, and Muon benchmarks already exist; the prospective mechanism tournament is the narrow contribution.
Short branches from shared 124M checkpoints can eliminate individual mechanisms quickly; only the scale certificate requires long runs.

assumptions: Every candidate optimizer update can be formed from the identical checkpoint and minibatch before committing a branch.
Native-recipe and counterfactual-update comparisons can be matched separately on compute, tuning budget, norm, angle, and function-space movement.
Hessian-vector and spectral measurements are accurate enough to test directional predictions at registered checkpoints.
A scale claim requires a certificate frozen before the larger model and held-out architecture, not post-hoc mechanism fitting.

brief.title: Muon mechanism crossover certificates
brief.thesis: At identical checkpoints, measure angular displacement, residual-sensitive oscillation, update-spectrum and noise geometry, and directional curvature for matched Muon and AdamW candidate updates. Freeze a low-complexity certificate at small scales and test whether it predicts the sign and magnitude of short-horizon loss-per-FLOP differences and improves phase switching on an untouched larger model.
brief.motivation: Recent Muon explanations emphasize different mechanisms: implicit angular decay from row-norm growth, river-valley overshoot and phase switching, spectrum-dependent response and batch noise, or superior normalized directional sharpness. The papers often analyze stylized variants, compare separate optimizer trajectories, use incompatible momentum or matrix-sign implementations, omit decisive figures, or confound switching with moment transfer and schedule tuning. A same-checkpoint causal tournament can say which measurements predict realized advantage rather than which story correlates with elapsed training.
brief.research_question: Can a prospective same-checkpoint mechanism certificate explain and predict when Muon beats AdamW, when the advantage crosses over, and whether that prediction survives model scale and architecture?
non_claims: The project does not claim angular decay, river-valley phase switching, spectral flattening, critical-batch theory, NDS, or matrix-sign implementations as new.
A mechanism derived for exact polar descent does not automatically describe five-step Newton-Schulz Muon with momentum, weight decay, and row rescaling.
A lower final loss on separately tuned trajectories does not isolate the causal update mechanism.
A certificate fit after seeing the larger-model ranking is not evidence of scale transfer.
subquestions: After Frobenius norm, spectral norm, mean row angle, and logit KL are matched, which directional statistic still predicts realized loss change?
Does residual-to-step ratio detect a real Muon-to-AdamW crossover better than elapsed step or a tuned fixed schedule?
Do singular-mode response and observed batch crossover agree with the proposed spectral and critical-batch formulas under the actual optimizer implementation?
How much of an apparent Muon mechanism is instead explained by Newton-Schulz approximation error, parameter grouping, weight decay, or moment transfer?
method: Train shared 124M and 500M checkpoints with a neutral recipe. At registered checkpoints, construct every optimizer candidate from the same parameters, minibatch, parameter groups, and decay configuration.

Run native recipes matched on tokens, FLOPs, wall time, tuning budget, seeds, parameter groups, and decay, alongside counterfactual updates matched on Frobenius norm, spectral norm, mean row angle, and function-space logit KL.

Measure row-norm growth, angular step, residual-to-step ratio, polar-direction persistence, oscillation, spectrum entropy, stable rank, singular-mode response, batch crossover, g-transpose-z, z-transpose-H-z, normalized directional sharpness, realized loss change, and Taylor residual.
Branch each candidate for the same short minibatch sequence and later run registered phase switches from identical checkpoints, including zeroed versus transferred AdamW moments.
Fit a prespecified sparse certificate at 124M and 500M, freeze it, then test its ranking and switching policy near 1.5B and on a held-out architecture without retuning.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: Small-checkpoint branches identify candidate mechanisms but do not establish scale. Freeze feature definitions, coefficients, thresholds, tuning budgets, and switch policy before opening the 1.5B model and held-out architecture.
supporting_evidence: Same-checkpoint certificate predicts realized Muon-minus-AdamW loss-per-FLOP sign and magnitude beyond training step and validation loss
Coefficient signs and optimizer rankings remain stable at the held-out scale and architecture
A frozen controller improves compute to target loss over native Muon, AdamW, and a tuned fixed switch schedule
Results survive exact-SVD versus Newton-Schulz, moment-transfer, parameter-group, and update-matching controls
Mechanism-specific interventions change the predicted outcome in the registered direction
claim_blockers: Same-checkpoint NDS or the combined certificate fails to predict realized advantage after update matching
Angle-matched optimizers remain substantially different, refuting angular decay as a sufficient account
Observed singular-mode response or batch crossover disagrees with registered formulas
Elapsed step or a tuned fixed schedule matches the residual detector
Random or inverted spectra match Muon after norm and direction controls
The frozen certificate reverses ranking at the held-out scale or architecture
Newton-Schulz implementation error explains more variance than the proposed optimization mechanisms
prospective_design: Develop feature definitions and sparse certificate on 124M and 500M checkpoints
Freeze the certificate, optimizer tuning budgets, and switch rule before 1.5B training
Use a different architecture as a second untouched validation and publish all checkpoint branches
why_small_models_fail: Curvature, width-depth aspect ratios, and batch-noise crossover change with scale
Row norms and angular equilibrium can be parameterization- and decay-dependent
Approximate matrix-sign error may matter differently as matrix shapes and precision change
The optimizer advantage may occur in a tail-learning phase absent from short small-model runs
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only development scales pass, claim a same-checkpoint mechanism predictor in the tested regimes. Claim cross-scale certification only if the frozen 1.5B and held-out-architecture gates pass.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A frozen certificate combining angular displacement, residual-sensitive oscillation, spectral or noise geometry, and directional curvature will predict Muon-versus-AdamW short-horizon loss-per-FLOP differences from identical checkpoints better than validation loss, training step, gradient norm, or any single proposed mechanism.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: A phase controller driven by the frozen certificate will reach a target loss with less compute than native Muon, native AdamW, and a tuned fixed Muon-to-AdamW switch at the held-out scale.
experiment.primary_outcome: Stage-1 held-out sign prediction, ranking, and loss-change error for Muon-versus-AdamW short-horizon loss per FLOP from identical checkpoints at the 1.5B and second-architecture holdouts.
experiment.claim_hierarchy: The same-checkpoint mechanism certificate is the primary claim. The phase controller is a secondary engineering claim tested only after the frozen certificate passes; controller failure does not erase a valid predictive certificate.
domains: Decoder-only language-model pretraining at approximately 124M and 500M development scales
An untouched approximately 1.5B language-model scale
A held-out architecture or matrix-shape regime
Synthetic river-valley, mixed-spiked, and matrix-factorization diagnostics as theorem-aligned positive controls
baselines: AdamW and exact-SVD Muon
Standard five-step Newton-Schulz Muon and Polar Express
Muown and AngularMuown
Residual-scaled Muon and Muon-to-AdamW with zeroed or transferred moments
Random-spectrum and inverted-spectrum controls
Validation-loss, elapsed-step, gradient-norm, single-mechanism, and tuned fixed-switch predictors
ablations: Remove each certificate coordinate and registered interaction
Match Frobenius norm only, then add spectral norm, row angle, and logit KL matching
Replace exact SVD with each Newton-Schulz implementation
Zero versus transfer optimizer moments at phase switches
Hold parameter groups and decay fixed versus use published native recipes
Refit versus freeze the certificate at the target scale
experiment.decision_rule: Stage 1 passes only if the frozen combined certificate improves preregistered held-out sign prediction, ranking, and loss-change error over every single-mechanism and elapsed-training baseline at 1.5B and the second architecture. Only after that gate passes, Stage 2 tests whether the frozen switch rule improves compute to target loss without a larger tuning budget. A Stage-2 controller failure rejects the controller claim but not a passed Stage-1 mechanism certificate; a Stage-1 failure rejects the general certificate.

evaluation: Same-checkpoint realized loss change, short-horizon loss area, and loss decrease per FLOP
Certificate sign accuracy, rank correlation, calibration, mean absolute error, and incremental value over checkpoint age
Row angle, norm growth, residual-to-step ratio, persistence, and oscillation
Spectrum entropy, stable rank, singular-mode response, noise covariance, and observed critical batch
Directional linear term, curvature term, NDS, Taylor residual, and logit KL
Compute to target loss for native and switched recipes under matched tuning budgets
Exact-SVD versus Newton-Schulz approximation error, wall time, memory, and numerical failures
risks: Matching all update statistics may be infeasible simultaneously. Predeclare a hierarchy of exact and approximate matching tolerances and report residual imbalance.
Hessian-vector estimates can be noisy and expensive. Use repeated probe vectors, held-out minibatches, and confidence intervals rather than one NDS value.
Short branches may not capture tail associative learning. Include longer registered branches at phase candidates and separate immediate from long-horizon claims.
Native recipes may require different tuning, while strict matching can make both unnatural. Report native-recipe and counterfactual causal comparisons as distinct estimands.
Optimizer switching can be confounded by moment initialization. Treat zeroed and transferred moments as separate preregistered arms.
A flexible certificate could combine noise into apparent accuracy. Limit feature count and interactions, freeze them before target scale, and compare with regularized and null predictors.
first_week: Implement exact-SVD Muon, five-step Newton-Schulz Muon, AdamW, and matched candidate-update logging on one 124M checkpoint.
Measure angle, norms, spectrum, g-transpose-z, z-transpose-H-z, NDS, logit KL, and realized one-step loss on 200 shared minibatches.
Build Frobenius-, spectral-, angle-, and KL-matched counterfactual updates plus random and inverted-spectrum controls.
Branch 20 registered checkpoints for a short common minibatch sequence and estimate variance and measurement cost.
Preregister certificate features, matching tolerances, development scales, untouched target, tuning budgets, and decisive falsifiers.

competitive_landscape.title: Muown: Row-Norm Control for Muon Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: Muown makes row-norm control explicit. The proposed tournament tests angular sufficiency with angle-matched candidate updates and native implementations.

competitive_landscape.title: Rotational Equilibrium: How Weight Decay Balances Learning Across Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Rotational equilibrium establishes norm-growth and effective angular-rate dynamics. The certificate tests their incremental predictive power for Muon versus AdamW.

competitive_landscape.title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining
competitive_landscape.difference: This work benchmarks practical Muon recipes. The proposal uses its native-efficiency standard while adding identical-checkpoint causal branches.

competitive_landscape.title: The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm
competitive_landscape.difference: Polar Express improves matrix-sign computation. The tournament isolates exact or approximate implementation error from optimizer-family mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: River-valley theory explains phase-dependent schedules without Muon. Elapsed-step and tuned fixed-switch baselines test whether residual geometry adds information.

competitive_landscape.title: Convergence Bound and Critical Batch Size of Muon Optimizer
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper predicts a Muon critical batch. The experiment measures the crossover under the actual implementation and tests it prospectively.

competitive_landscape.title: Spectral Flattening Is All Muon Needs: How Orthogonalization Controls Learning Rate and Convergence
competitive_landscape.difference: This work argues spectral flattening is sufficient. Random and inverted spectra plus norm, angle, and KL matching directly test that account.

competitive_landscape.title: Muon is Not That Special: Random or Inverted Spectra Work Just as Well
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper reports random or inverted spectral values can work similarly. Those controls become first-class falsifiers rather than afterthoughts.

competitive_landscape.title: Muon Does Not Converge on Convex Lipschitz Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: This counterexample rules out broad convergence narratives. The proposed claim is explicitly empirical, local, and regime-bounded.

competitive_landscape.title: Preconditioning Benefits of Spectral Orthogonalization in Muon
competitive_landscape.difference: This work explains Muon through structured Hessian preconditioning. Same-checkpoint directional curvature measures test its predictions alongside angle and spectrum.

competitive_landscape.title: Isotropic Curvature Model for Understanding Deep Learning Optimization: Is Gradient Orthogonalization Optimal?
competitive_landscape.difference: This analysis identifies regimes where exact orthogonalization is not optimal. The certificate must identify those crossovers rather than assume universal benefit.

competitive_landscape.title: Toward Understanding Why Adam Converges Faster Than SGD for Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper connects adaptive optimization to Transformer Hessian geometry. It supplies a non-Muon directional-curvature baseline for the tournament.

competitive_landscape.title: Muon Outperforms Adam in Tail-End Associative Memory Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work locates Muon advantage in tail associative-memory learning. Longer phase branches test whether a short certificate anticipates that delayed regime.

competitive_landscape.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them
competitive_landscape.difference: This benchmark emphasizes recipe and tuning fairness. Its controls define the native comparison, while the proposal adds causal matched-update branches.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond a Single Explanation of the Adam--SGD Gap
competitive_landscape.difference: This work argues optimizer gaps resist a single-factor account. The proposed certificate is explicitly comparative and must beat every individual coordinate.

competitive_landscape.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper shows Adam can depend on parameter basis even when the loss does not. Basis transformations become a control for parameter-space curvature interpretations.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and a 16-paper primary-source review: angular effective learning rates, row-norm control, river-valley schedules and switching, spectral flattening and negative spectral controls, critical-batch theory, curvature accounts, matrix-sign implementations, tail-learning results, and controlled Muon benchmarks are established. The defensible contribution is a prospective same-checkpoint causal tournament plus a low-complexity mechanism certificate frozen before an unseen scale and architecture. Tuning another Muon variant and reporting lower final loss would not be novel.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 122 pages, with 63 page-anchored findings, 146 anchors, and 47 checked competitor entries spanning 40 unique primary papers.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
A two-family, two-backbone pilot is manageable, but a credible cross-scale claim needs repeated agent runs and a third untouched larger backbone.
Executable outcomes, paired counterfactual arms, reliability vectors, exploit checks, and preregistered transfer gates make failure observable.
Skill generation, skill repositories, reliability profiles, compression certificates, and research-agent RL are crowded. The prospective causal acceptance protocol is narrower and defensible.
A 60-120-task pilot can reject weak selectors quickly; transfer and scale validation take longer because the held-out harness and backbone cannot be reused during selection.

assumptions: Fresh executable tasks can be authored outside the skill generator and kept hidden through selector freeze.
No-skill, candidate-skill, placebo, and raw-trace arms can be matched on tokens, tools, calls, and training compute.
Repeated runs expose reliability differences that a single success rate hides.
Cross-scale validity means stable sign, rank, calibration, exploit resistance, and transfer rather than a positive small-agent result.

brief.title: Reliability-gated skill transfer for research agents
brief.thesis: Freeze a cheap skill-acceptance selector that combines repeated-run reliability, causal uplift on independent hidden tasks, and fresh cross-model compressed reproduction. Then test whether it selects skills whose benefits survive a new task family, harness, and larger model better than intrinsic skill scores, retrieval relevance, training reward, or raw in-family success.
brief.motivation: Agent skill libraries report large average gains, yet close audits find negative tasks, large-pool degradation, harness confounds, model-generated evaluation gyms, and weak open-world transfer. Reliability frameworks expose inconsistency but can reward repeatable failure; compression bounds can detect memorized task descriptions but do not certify downstream skill utility; search-agent RL can optimize the same evaluation surface used to generate training data. A useful gate must predict causal transfer before the target backbone and task family are opened.
brief.research_question: Can a preregistered small-agent selector identify generated research skills whose compute-matched causal gains, reliability, and safety transfer prospectively across tasks, harnesses, and model scale?
non_claims: The project does not claim skill generation, skill repositories, reliability vectors, compressed reproduction, or search-agent RL as new.
A repeatable outcome is not necessarily a successful outcome, and an average success gain is not a safety result.
Passing public or generator-authored tasks is not evidence of open-world skill transfer.
A frozen selector trained on small agents is not scale-valid unless its sign, ranking, and calibration survive an untouched larger backbone.
subquestions: Which reliability coordinates add transfer information after raw task success, tokens, tool calls, and training compute are matched?
Does fresh compressed reproduction detect evaluation-specific or verbose skills that ordinary retrieval scores accept?
When do automatic executable graders disagree with blinded semantic or safety adjudication, and can disagreement route only ambiguous cases to humans?
Are skill rankings stable across task family, harness, backbone, and scale, or do apparent gains mostly encode evaluator and scaffold compatibility?
method: Create 60-120 hidden, post-cutoff executable tasks in two research families. Author outcomes and exploit checks outside the skill generator and seal one family, harness, and larger backbone until the selector is frozen.

For each candidate skill, run paired no-skill, skill, equal-token placebo, and raw-successful-trace arms with identical model, tools, token budget, calls, and training compute across powered repeated seeds.

Measure a capability-and-reliability vector: causal success uplift, run-to-run consistency conditional on correctness, recovery, calibration, cost, exploit rate, safety failures, and automatic-judge disagreement.
Ask a different model family and harness to reproduce the skill from a compressed description on fresh tasks; include shuffled, bloated, and evaluation-keyword controls.

Fit a simple registered selector on one task family and small backbone, freeze coefficients and thresholds, then evaluate candidate selection on the untouched family, harness, and larger backbone without retuning.

human_in_the_loop.answer: Humans are not required for every rollout. They are required to define ambiguous semantic and safety boundaries, adjudicate grader disagreements, and audit a random sample that can reveal shared generator-evaluator blind spots.
humans_not_needed_for: Deterministic executable outcomes, resource budgets, tool traces, and seeded repeatability
Matched-arm assignment, selector scoring, compression checks, and confidence intervals
Known exploit signatures and mechanically checkable safety constraints
humans_needed_for: Semantic partial credit or validity that the executable checker cannot represent
Novel harmful strategies, hidden evaluator leakage, and suspiciously brittle skills
A blinded random audit used to estimate automatic-grader false acceptance and rejection
human_in_the_loop.measurement: Report judge-human disagreement with confidence intervals by task family and failure type. If disagreement exceeds the preregistered tolerance or clusters around selected skills, block the transfer claim and expand human review.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: A small-agent screen is a proposal filter, not a scaling claim. The selector must be frozen before the larger backbone and must preserve causal-gain sign, rank, calibration, reliability, and exploit behavior under the held-out harness and task family.
supporting_evidence: Positive lower confidence bound for selected-skill causal uplift over no-skill and equal-token placebo arms
Positive cross-scale rank correlation with few material sign reversals and calibrated acceptance precision
Transfer across an untouched task family, different harness, and model family under matched resources
No material worsening of exploit, safety, or judge-human disagreement rates
Fresh compressed reproduction succeeds beyond public or in-family tasks
claim_blockers: Gains disappear after tokens, calls, tools, or training compute are matched
The selected-skill lower confidence bound is non-positive
Cross-scale rank correlation is at or below zero or several candidate effects reverse sign
Benefits vanish on the held-out harness, backbone, or task family
Safety, exploit, or grader-disagreement rates exceed the registered margin
prospective_design: Fit on one task family and two small/medium backbones, then freeze the selector
Open a second task family and different harness only after selector freeze
Use a third, larger backbone as the untouched scale test and publish every candidate, not only winners
why_small_models_fail: They may lack the capability to use a valid skill, creating false negatives
They may benefit from verbose procedural hints that larger models already internalize
Harness-specific recovery behavior can dominate the measured skill effect
Skill rankings can encode backbone-specific priors rather than task-general utility
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only the pilot passes, claim a validated selection procedure at the tested scale. Use cross-scale language only if the untouched larger-backbone gates pass without retuning.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: The frozen reliability-and-reproduction selector will achieve higher preregistered expected causal utility on the untouched task family, harness, and larger backbone than intrinsic skill score, training reward, retrieval relevance, or raw in-family success.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Selected skills will improve repeated-run reliability without increasing exploit, safety, or grader-disagreement rates relative to no-skill and equal-token placebo arms.
experiment.primary_outcome: Preregistered expected causal utility of the frozen selector on the untouched task family, harness, and larger backbone, defined before evaluation as compute-matched success uplift minus fixed safety, exploit, grader-disagreement, and resource penalties at a fixed acceptance budget.
domains: Executable machine-learning experimentation tasks
Research search and evidence-synthesis tasks with sealed source sets
A held-out tool-use family with independent safety and exploit checks
baselines: No skill and equal-token generic instruction placebo
Raw successful trace and top-retrieval skill
Intrinsic LLM skill score, training reward, and in-family validation success
Reliability vector without causal uplift or compressed reproduction
Compressed reproduction without repeated-run reliability
Random skill selection at the same acceptance rate
ablations: Remove each selector coordinate and each task-family reliability slice
Use the same model or harness for generator, evaluator, and reproducer
Replace fresh hidden tasks with public or generator-authored tasks
Unmatch tokens, tool calls, or training compute one at a time
Remove blinded human disagreement audits
Retune the selector after seeing the larger backbone
experiment.decision_rule: Accept the primary claim only if the frozen selector improves the single preregistered expected-utility outcome over every cheap baseline on the untouched family and larger backbone, the selected-skill uplift lower confidence bound is positive, rank correlation remains positive, and safety, exploit, grader-disagreement, and resource gates do not worsen. Report precision and recall as diagnostics, never as alternate routes to a pass. Otherwise report the failed transfer boundary and reject general skill validity.

evaluation: Paired causal success uplift and confidence intervals for selected versus rejected skills
Selection precision, recall, calibration, and utility at a fixed evaluation budget
Conditional consistency among correct runs, recovery, cost variance, and repeated-failure rate
Cross-family, cross-harness, cross-backbone, and cross-scale sign and rank stability
Exploit success, safety violations, reward-to-executable-outcome gap, and judge-human disagreement
Fresh compressed-reproduction success with shuffled, verbose, and keyword-matched controls
Tokens, calls, wall time, training compute, and total selector cost
risks: Hidden tasks can still share pretrained public priors. Use post-cutoff or privately authored tasks and distinguish contamination reduction from elimination.
All evaluators may share the same semantic blind spot. Use independent executable outcomes plus blinded disagreement audits from a different model family and humans.
Repeated runs are expensive and selector fitting can overfit. Predeclare the coordinate set, use task-grouped splits, and keep the final family and backbone sealed.
Compression can reward underspecified descriptions. Require executable reproduction, not token count alone, and include concise but wrong controls.
A selector may reject innovative but high-variance skills. Publish the precision-recall frontier and rejected-candidate outcomes rather than optimizing one threshold.
Safety is multidimensional and must not be hidden inside one overall score. Keep separate hard gates and confidence intervals.
first_week: Implement paired no-skill, candidate-skill, placebo, and raw-trace arms in one executable task family.
Select 12 candidate skills and run a pilot variance study across repeated seeds with matched token and tool budgets.
Build the capability/reliability vector and confirm that repeatable failure is separated from successful consistency.
Prototype fresh compressed reproduction with a different model and harness plus shuffled and verbose controls.
Preregister selector coordinates, task-family split, human-audit sample, scale gates, and rejection rules before fitting.

competitive_landscape.title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
competitive_landscape.difference: ReliabilityBench measures production-like consistency and recovery. The proposed study uses such coordinates prospectively to select skills and requires independent causal transfer rather than a retrospective profile.

competitive_landscape.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
competitive_landscape.difference: A holistic leaderboard aggregates capabilities; this project tests whether a frozen subset predicts skill transfer and keeps safety as a separate gate.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Large Language Model Benchmarks Test Reliability?
competitive_landscape.difference: This work questions whether standard scores measure reliability. The proposed paired repeated-run design estimates causal skill uplift conditional on correctness and transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark
competitive_landscape.difference: LiveBench refreshes objective tasks to reduce contamination. This project additionally separates generator, evaluator, harness, and held-out backbone while testing skill causality.

competitive_landscape.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: SkillsBench measures skill utility across tasks. The proposed selector is trained prospectively and must predict compute-matched transfer to untouched tasks, harnesses, and scale.

competitive_landscape.title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
competitive_landscape.difference: SWE-Skills-Bench shows realistic software skills can fail to help. Those nulls motivate the no-skill, placebo, and matched-resource causal gates here.

competitive_landscape.title: How Well Do Agentic Skills Work in the Wild: Benchmarking LLM Skill Usage in Realistic Settings
competitive_landscape.difference: This work tests open skill use in realistic settings. The new contribution is predicting which skills will transfer before the hidden setting is opened.

competitive_landscape.title: SkillLearnBench: Benchmarking Continual Learning Methods for Agent Skill Generation on Real-World Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: SkillLearnBench evaluates learning pipelines. This project evaluates a frozen acceptance rule and includes cross-harness, scale, reliability, and exploit gates.

competitive_landscape.title: SkillGenBench: Benchmarking Skill Generation Pipelines for LLM Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: SkillGenBench compares generators. The proposed protocol is generator-agnostic and asks whether cheap evidence predicts causal downstream transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: OpenSkillEval: Automatically Auditing the Open Skill Ecosystem for LLM Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: OpenSkillEval audits open skills automatically. This project measures when automated acceptance disagrees with independent executable and human outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
competitive_landscape.difference: MLAgentBench supplies experimentation tasks. The proposal adds hidden paired interventions and prospective skill selection rather than a system leaderboard.

competitive_landscape.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
competitive_landscape.difference: MLE-bench evaluates end-to-end ML engineering. The proposed pilot uses similarly executable outcomes but isolates candidate-skill causality under matched budgets.

competitive_landscape.title: Rip van Winkle's Razor: A Simple Estimate of Overfit to Test Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Compression estimates description-length overfit. Here fresh cross-model executable reproduction is one selector coordinate, not a sufficient validity certificate.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
competitive_landscape.difference: Adaptive holdout theory limits reuse of evaluation data. The proposed design seals task family, harness, and larger backbone to test one frozen selector prospectively.

competitive_landscape.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Search-R1 optimizes search behavior with RL. The proposal tests whether extracted skills from any such pipeline transfer beyond the reward and scaffold that produced them.

competitive_landscape.title: DeepResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Reinforcement Learning in Real-world Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepResearcher trains real-world research behavior. The new protocol isolates skill-level causal value and prospective cross-harness transfer rather than overall agent return.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored collection readings and a 16-paper primary-source review: agent reliability suites, holistic leaderboards, fresh benchmarks, skill-generation systems, realistic skill audits, ML-research benchmarks, compression-based overfit estimates, and search-agent RL are established. The defensible contribution is a prospective causal acceptance protocol that freezes a cheap selector on small agents and tests whether it predicts compute-matched skill transfer, conditional reliability, exploit resistance, and sign/rank stability on untouched task families, harnesses, and a larger backbone. Another skill library, average benchmark gain, or retrospective reliability score would not be novel.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 186 pages, with 42 page-anchored findings and 38 direct primary competitors. The 16-paper brief landscape was checked against primary arXiv records.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
Many treatment cells and model-scale transfers are expensive, but fractional-factorial pilots, shared checkpoints, and small randomized data blocks can reject weak proxies early.
Randomized block replacement, sealed downstream tasks, token- and compute-matched controls, semantic-equivalence audits, and prospective rank tests give direct causal outcomes.

Curation, influence, coverage, reuse, deduplication, and data scaling are mature; the narrow contribution is a frozen cross-scale causal surface over selection, timing, and reuse rather than another retrospective score.
A small-language-model block-randomization pilot can reveal proxy sign errors within a week, while semantic and larger-scale confirmation takes longer.

assumptions: Data treatments can be randomized from identical checkpoints without leaking treatment identity into evaluation or changing unrelated token budgets.
Difficulty, semantic support, quality, timing, and reuse can be defined independently enough to construct factorial or balanced treatment cells.
A development-only proxy model and semantic-equivalence policy can be frozen before the held-out task and model scale are evaluated.
Data value is an interaction among example, training stage, learner, dose, and target distribution—not an intrinsic scalar attached permanently to one example.

brief.title: Prospective causal data-value surfaces
brief.thesis: Treat data value as a causal response surface over what is selected, when it is shown, how often it is reused, which learner receives it, and which held-out behavior is measured. From identical checkpoints, randomize compute-matched data-block treatments across semantic support, difficulty, quality, timing, and exact-reuse dose; cross-fit loss, margin, influence, coverage, and reuse predictors at development scale; freeze the surface; then test causal marginal transfer, semantic-support change, memorization, and rank stability on an untouched task and model scale.
brief.motivation: Recent theories separately predict easy-versus-hard curation crossovers, stage-dependent influence, exact sequence coverage, and dataset-size-dependent reuse. Their strongest evidence uses incompatible units and assumptions: Gaussian margins, locally tuned Bayesian covariance, unobservable density ratios, or loss-equivalent linear reuse. Retrospective correlations can look strong while sharing labels, checkpoints, or hyperparameters with the claimed validation. A randomized prospective surface would reveal which signals predict actual marginal learning and when their sign reverses.
brief.research_question: Can small-scale data-value signals prospectively predict the causal effect of selection, timing, and reuse on sealed semantic transfer at a new task and model scale?
non_claims: No example has a context-free scalar value; effects are conditional on learner, checkpoint, dose, optimizer, and target distribution.
Lower training loss, exact sequence probability, or correlation with leave-one-out labels is not semantic downstream value by itself.
Token-matched repetition is not compute equivalence when examples receive different optimizer steps, sequence lengths, or wall time.
A proxy selected on the same retraining trace it predicts does not demonstrate generalization.
subquestions: Which proxies retain effect sign and rank after lineage-grouped cross-fitting and an untouched task, checkpoint stage, architecture, and scale?
When do easy versus hard selection, early versus late exposure, and fresh versus repeated data interact rather than add independently?
Does exact sequence coverage predict semantic answer or behavior coverage after equivalence classes and reward validity are predeclared?
Can positive loss transfer coexist with worse memorization, rare-mode coverage, calibration, or downstream behavior?
method: Partition a source corpus into lineage-grouped blocks with preregistered semantic-support, difficulty, quality, contamination, and frequency strata. Define semantic equivalence with task-specific canonicalizers and human adjudication only for unresolved boundary cases.

Save common checkpoints at early, transition, and late stages. Randomize equal-token and separately equal-compute replacement treatments that vary selection stratum, exposure time, fresh-versus-exact-reuse dose, and clean-versus-synthetic source while keeping optimizer, batch order outside the block, and evaluation sealed.

Estimate development-only predictors: loss and margin, static influence, TracIn or SOURCE, stagewise BIF, exact sequence density ratio where observable, semantic-support coverage, diversity, gradient agreement, and fitted reuse saturation. Cross-fit every hyperparameter and feature without using the target treatment outcomes.

Fit a hierarchical response surface with treatment, stage, learner, dose, lineage, and seed effects. Freeze the proxy ensemble, interaction terms, semantic policy, and promotion thresholds before evaluating a held-out task family and larger model.

Measure causal marginal transfer on sealed behavioral tasks alongside training loss, semantic support, calibration, rare-mode performance, contamination, verbatim memorization, and compute. Publish the full treatment distribution rather than only the selected top bucket.

validation_funnel.gate: Lineage, token, compute, optimizer-step, contamination, and semantic-stratum balances must pass before any data-value comparison is interpreted.
Randomized block replacements from identical checkpoints must produce reproducible marginal effects beyond seed and batch-order variation.
The frozen proxy surface must predict effect sign, rank, and uncertainty on held-out lineages and a sealed task without tuning to the intervention outcomes.
Predictions must survive the untouched larger model and semantic-support audit under both token- and compute-matched controls without worsening memorization or rare-mode gates.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The data-value surface is scale-valid only within the registered treatment, learner, task, dose, and target-distribution range and only if a surface frozen on development checkpoints predicts an untouched larger model and task family.
prospective_design: Freeze treatment definitions, lineage splits, semantic-equivalence policy, proxy ensemble, interaction terms, promotion threshold, and compute estimands before the larger model or sealed task is evaluated.
Keep one task family and one larger model fully untouched; do not use their loss curves to choose feature transforms or surface complexity.
Carry promoted, rejected, and randomly sampled treatments to the holdout so selection bias and false negatives remain estimable.
supporting_evidence: Improved held-out causal-effect sign, rank, and calibration over every registered single proxy
Positive compute-matched semantic transfer on the untouched task and larger model
No material worsening of memorization, contamination, calibration, semantic support, or rare-mode outcomes
claim_blockers: The frozen surface loses useful sign, rank, or calibration at the larger model or new task
Scale transfer requires target-aware refitting, a changed semantic policy, or a different treatment definition
Loss improves while sealed semantic behavior, support, memorization, contamination, calibration, or rare-mode gates fail
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'the conditional data-value surface transferred within the tested learner, task, treatment, dose, and scale range.' Never assign a context-free scalable value to an example.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A cross-fitted interaction surface using stage, semantic support, difficulty, source, and reuse dose will predict held-out causal marginal transfer more accurately than loss, margin, static influence, exact coverage, or a global repetition discount alone.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Proxy rankings will reverse across training stage and model scale, but a prospectively frozen interaction model will retain useful sign and rank accuracy while exposing treatments whose loss gains come from memorization or support collapse.
domains: Controlled graph or algorithmic sequences with exact semantic equivalence and support
Small language-model pretraining with lineage-controlled web and synthetic blocks
Reasoning post-training with verifier-audited solution equivalence
An untouched larger model and sealed downstream task family
baselines: Uniform random selection and equal-compute fresh replacement
Loss, margin, perplexity, confidence, and difficulty ranking
Static influence functions, TracIn, TRAK, and SOURCE-style attribution
Stagewise Bayesian influence with hyperparameters fit only on development folds
Exact sequence coverage and semantic-equivalence coverage
Diversity, deduplication, gradient-similarity, and data-pruning scores
Global and dataset-size-dependent repetition-discount fits
ablations: Remove stage, learner, dose, semantic support, or source interactions one at a time
Use random instance splits instead of lineage-grouped cross-fitting as an optimism diagnostic
Tune attribution hyperparameters on the target intervention trace as an explicitly invalid upper bound
Compare token matching, optimizer-step matching, FLOP matching, and wall-time matching
Replace semantic equivalence with exact-string support
Omit memorization, contamination, calibration, or rare-mode outcomes
Fit on one model scale and inspect only after freezing the larger-scale prediction
experiment.primary_outcome: Causal marginal area-under-learning-curve improvement on a sealed downstream suite per matched training FLOP, with semantic-support gain and memorization rate as co-primary gates.
experiment.analysis: Estimate paired treatment effects from common checkpoints, hierarchical seed and lineage intervals, held-out sign and rank accuracy, calibration, top-bucket regret, interaction variance, proxy residuals, and disagreement between loss, semantic transfer, and memorization outcomes.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if the frozen interaction surface beats every single proxy on held-out causal effect sign, rank, and calibration; transfers to the untouched model and task under token- and compute-matched controls; and promoted treatments improve sealed semantic behavior without crossing contamination, memorization, calibration, or rare-mode thresholds. Otherwise reject a general data-value claim and report only the registered conditional effects.

evaluation: Paired causal marginal transfer and area under learning curves from identical checkpoints
Held-out Kendall tau-b, pairwise sign accuracy, top-bucket overlap, calibration, selection regret, and ranking reversals
Exact-string support versus preregistered semantic-equivalence support and diversity
Verbatim memorization, contamination, rare-mode recall, calibration, and reward-to-hidden-evaluator divergence
Training loss, validation loss, downstream accuracy or reward, and forgetting of untouched capabilities
Tokens, examples, optimizer steps, FLOPs, accelerator-hours, wall time, attribution queries, and human-adjudication minutes
Treatment, stage, learner, dose, lineage, source, and seed variance components
risks: Semantic equivalence can import subjective labels. Use exact solvers where possible, preregister canonicalizers, blind adjudicators to treatment, and report unresolved rates.
Randomized small blocks may underestimate long-range curriculum or distribution effects. Vary dose and block length and include a cumulative multi-block confirmation.
Attribution methods are expensive and hyperparameter-sensitive. Cross-fit them by lineage and charge every model, sampler, Hessian, and query cost.
Equal tokens can hide extra epochs or optimizer steps, while equal FLOPs can change exposure. Publish both estimands instead of collapsing them.
A downstream gain can come from benchmark contamination or memorized templates. Seal tasks, audit nearest neighbors and verbatim output, and require rare-mode and contamination gates.
A larger model may use the same data differently. Treat scale interactions and ranking reversal as primary results rather than noise.
first_week: Define four lineage-safe semantic strata and build token-, step-, and FLOP-accounting checks for randomized block replacement.
Save three checkpoints of one small transformer and run fresh-versus-reuse, easy-versus-hard, and early-versus-late pilot treatments from identical states.
Compute loss, margin, TracIn, a cross-fitted influence baseline, exact support, and semantic-support coverage without seeing the sealed outcomes.
Measure paired downstream transfer, calibration, rare-mode behavior, and verbatim memorization across at least five seeds.
Preregister the held-out lineage, larger scale, semantic policy, proxy ensemble, compute estimands, and claim-blocking thresholds.

competitive_landscape.title: Why Less is More (Sometimes): A Theory of Data Curation
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper derives a generator-quality-dependent easy/hard crossover in Gaussian ridge classification. The proposal tests causal neural effects while separating semantic support, reuse, and compute.

competitive_landscape.title: Influence Dynamics and Stagewise Data Attribution
competitive_landscape.difference: Stagewise BIF predicts transition-dependent influence but tunes key sampler settings against the same intervention label family. The proposal cross-fits every proxy and seals the treatment outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: The Coverage Principle: How Pre-Training Enables Post-Training
competitive_landscape.difference: The coverage profile formalizes exact sequence density ratios under realizability. The proposal distinguishes that statistic from preregistered semantic support and directly tests downstream interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Larger Datasets Can Be Repeated More: A Theoretical Analysis of Multi-Epoch Scaling in Linear Regression
competitive_landscape.difference: This work defines loss-equivalent fresh-data reuse in linear regression and one small LLM. The proposal crosses reuse with timing and selection and adds compute, semantic, and memorization equivalence.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Neural Scaling Laws: Beating Power Law Scaling via Data Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: Sorscher et al. compare pruning metrics and derive scaling predictions. Their scores become baselines inside randomized treatment cells rather than assumed intrinsic values.

competitive_landscape.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
competitive_landscape.difference: TRAK approximates retraining-based attribution at large scale. The proposal tests whether it predicts stage-, dose-, and scale-conditional causal transfer prospectively.

competitive_landscape.title: Training Data Attribution via Approximate Unrolled Differentiation
competitive_landscape.difference: SOURCE models non-converged optimizer trajectories and counterfactual retraining. It is a strong cumulative-effect comparator to local stagewise covariance.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This large study estimates repetition discounts across model and token scales. The proposal asks whether a global discount predicts causal semantic value once selection and stage interact.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Repeated examples can consume capacity and damage induction behavior. This makes memorization and untouched-capability gates mandatory alongside loss equivalence.

competitive_landscape.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better
competitive_landscape.difference: Near duplicates alter memorization, learning, and evaluation overlap. The proposal preserves exact lineage and audits duplicate-mediated gains explicitly.

competitive_landscape.title: Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? Coverage, Scaling, and Optimality in Inference-Time Alignment
competitive_landscape.difference: This work already makes policy coverage central to Best-of-N and reward hacking. The proposal tests whether pretraining support measures predict later causal semantic transfer under independent reward checks.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Model Collapse: Scaling Up with Synthesized Data Requires Verification
competitive_landscape.difference: Verification mitigates recursive synthetic-data collapse in theory and language experiments. The proposal crosses verifier quality with difficulty, timing, and reuse rather than treating source quality alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Estimating Training Data Influence by Tracing Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: TracIn accumulates gradient interactions at checkpoints with modest machinery. It tests whether expensive posterior attribution adds prospective value beyond simple trajectory signals.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and a 36-paper primary-source audit: data pruning, difficulty curation, static and trajectory attribution, Bayesian influence, exact coverage, semantic sampling coverage, repetition scaling, deduplication, synthetic-data verification, and memorization effects are established. The defensible contribution is a prospective randomized response surface that crosses selection, timing, exact-reuse dose, learner, and target; freezes all proxy fitting before a new task and scale; and makes semantic transfer, compute, contamination, and memorization co-primary gates. Another retrospective data score would not be novel.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 209 pages, with 35 attributed findings, 108 page anchors, and 36 unique directly inspected primary competitors. The unit of study is a randomized data treatment, so this does not duplicate environment validity, optimizer crossover, or continual-update safety briefs.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

Markov-mixture and nested-regression corpora are fully synthetic, labels are exact, and the primary study can use repeated 10M-100M-parameter models. Credible boundary estimates still require many seeds, dense checkpointing, factorial context and diversity grids, causal branches, and an unopened deeper-model confirmation.

Executable candidate algorithms, a categorical four-route-plus-unknown target, a full-cohort abstention-penalized log score, an exact boundary metric, simultaneous 95% baseline comparisons, answer-matched causal gates, and explicit kill criteria yield a sharp accept-or-reject test. Mixtures and partially identified routes map to the unknown class, while predictor abstention remains penalized and visible through selective risk.

Algorithm selection, phase diagrams, strategy competition, causal task vectors, schema-binding double dissociation, learned relevance-conditioned ICL-IWL switching, behavioral switch-and-recovery surfaces, induction-head formation, contextualize-then-aggregate circuits, and 2026 test-versus-readout and task-vector sufficiency studies already occupy the component ideas. Novelty survives only in their conjunction: an independently frozen executable route basis, source-only fitted prospective switch forecast, answer-matched route-specific causal labeling, and zero-calibration transfer to a completely untouched target family.

A two-route, one-family pilot can expose collinearity, unstable labels, generic competence effects, or failure against loss-only baselines within weeks. A defensible paper needs the four-route dictionaries, both task families, sealed larger-depth cohort, and no-refit transfer, which makes the decisive result materially slower.

assumptions: Each family admits at least two executable candidate algorithms whose predictions separate on a preregistered diagnostic set and jointly leave a small enough oracle residual for a route claim to be meaningful.
Route identities can be defined functionally from candidate predictions and targeted prompt evidence, without assuming a universal neuron, layer, task vector, or discrete router.

Answer-matched donor and counterfactual constructions can selectively remove and restore retrieval, inference, or order evidence while holding ordinary answer difficulty, confidence, and token statistics within registered tolerances.
A sparse switch surface fitted from pre-intervention observables can be frozen before the confirmation cohort and evaluated without relabeling routes, refitting coefficients, or changing thresholds.

Markov-mixture and nested-regression families share enough normalized evidence, complexity, ambiguity, and training-progress variables for a no-refit transfer test to be meaningful, while family-specific executable algorithms remain explicit.
Seed and architecture variation can be covered with sufficient replication to distinguish a stable functional route from per-seed label permutation or a probe artifact.
A negative result remains publishable if positive controls pass and it identifies where candidate algorithms become collinear, mixtures cease to be identifiable, or prospective transfer fails.

brief.title: Prospective Causal Switch Surfaces for In-Context Algorithms
