brief.thesis: For two controlled task families, define every candidate in-context algorithm, oracle, diagnostic, and semantic intervention analytically before inspecting either family's trained-model outcomes, and reject dictionaries with collinear fingerprints or large oracle residuals. Fit a sparse switch surface only on source-family Markov trained-model outcomes, freeze route identities, labels, features, coefficients, thresholds, interventions, target filters, matchers, and exclusions, and evaluate sealed same-family cells before opening any target-family regression outcome. The claim passes only if the source-fitted surface beats every registered baseline, route-specific answer-matched remove-and-rescue tests clear the causal gate, and the frozen surface transfers with zero target-family calibration to completely untouched regression outcomes and one larger model without route reidentification or refitting. The one-larger-model result is transfer evidence, not a scaling claim.
brief.motivation: The supporting readings establish complementary but incomplete pieces. In-Context Learning Strategies Emerge Rationally fits a compact loss-complexity account of memorizing versus generalizing behavior across training and diversity, but supplies the strategies, fits from outputs, repairs a complexity proxy post hoc in three conditions, and offers no causal route test. In-Context Occam’s Razor: How Transformers Prefer Simpler Hypotheses on the Fly makes nested-class ambiguity explicit across Markov and regression tasks, but selection depends on classes represented during pretraining and does not identify a switch mechanism. Decomposing Prediction Mechanisms for In-Context Recall separates label-driven recall from observation-driven continuation using tokenwise trajectories and OOD recombinations, yet its zero-overlap pruning result is fragile and the later route is not Bayes-optimal. The transformer-k-means reading contributes only a structural boundary: executable algorithms can be compiled into modular attention blocks, but that is not evidence that a trained model selects among them. Closest prior work already individually occupies four-algorithm phase diagrams, strategy coopetition, provable in-context algorithm selection, a causal task-schema-versus-binding double dissociation, learned ICL-IWL switching conditioned on context relevance, and behavioral task-switch-and-recovery surfaces conditioned on curriculum. Two August 2026 near-blockers add matched counterfactual tests of static versus query-specific task-vector realizations and Test, then Route's asymmetric causal test-versus-readout dissociation across models and languages; the latter is not a double dissociation. The remaining question is therefore only the registered conjunction: can a surface fitted on source-family trained-model outcomes forecast answer-matched causal route labels on sealed source cells, then transfer with analytic route construction and zero calibration to a completely untouched target family and one larger model?
brief.research_question: Can an independently specified multi-algorithm dictionary and a frozen low-complexity switch surface prospectively predict answer-matched causal route changes on sealed in-context-learning models and task regimes, then transfer without route reidentification or coefficient refitting?
non_claims: The project does not identify all algorithms a transformer can use, and the registered dictionaries are neither exhaustive nor assumed to span every model output.
It does not claim that in-context learning uses one universal discrete router; mixtures, superposition, continuous interpolation, unidentified alternatives, and abstention are allowed outcomes.
Behavioral proximity, convex-mixture weights, probes, attribution, attention maps, task vectors, or edge-pruned graphs alone are not treated as causal route identification.
A behavioral match to a Bayesian, ridge, retrieval, or memorizing predictor is not evidence that the network implements Bayesian inference or that named algorithm internally.
No task vector is assumed to be globally necessary or sufficient; local, query-conditioned, distributed, and task-dependent representations are explicit alternatives.
The study does not assert neuron-, head-, direction-, or layer-level correspondence across seeds, widths, architectures, or task families.
It does not generalize from small synthetic models to unrestricted natural-language ICL, multimodal ICL, closed frontier systems, or all context lengths.

It does not call a result prospective if route fingerprints, label assignments, coefficients, thresholds, donor matching, exclusions, or intervention doses change after any confirmation outcome is inspected.
A successful surface predicts a registered functional route under the tested interventions; it does not prove that no behaviorally equivalent implementation exists.
The k-means transformer reading is a modular algorithm-compilation blueprint and boundary control only, not substantive evidence for learned ICL route switching.
subquestions: When do four executable route fingerprints remain identifiable rather than collapsing into a collinear or high-residual behavioral basis?

Can pre-intervention loss gaps, complexity gaps, context identifiability, diversity, and normalized training progress forecast a causal route label rather than merely reconstruct a retrospective phase diagram?
Do retrieval-evidence and structural-order interventions create an answer-matched double dissociation, with route-specific removal and rescue but no generic competence loss?
Are switch boundaries stable across seeds and harmless diagnostic reweightings, or do route labels permute whenever the probe, metric, or checkpoint grid changes?

Does a surface fitted only on source-family Markov trained-model outcomes retain its proper-score and boundary-location advantages on sealed same-family configurations and one larger model without coefficient, threshold, or route refitting?

Does that source-fitted surface transfer to completely untouched target-family regression outcomes when both families' route code and interventions were constructed analytically in advance, target filtering and matching were prespecified, and no target-family outcome was used for calibration?
Do internal task-vector or circuit diagnostics add predictive value after the functional causal label is fixed, or do they merely track confidence, loss, or elapsed training?

reading_roles.use: Supplies the loss-complexity, training-time, and task-diversity variables and motivates turning a retrospective two-strategy fit into a frozen prospective causal forecast.
Supplies nested-class ambiguity tests in Markov and regression settings and the important boundary that simpler routes may not appear when their class was absent from pretraining.
Supplies token-position-resolved route dissociation and label-observation counterfactuals while warning that post-hoc edge-pruning overlap is not a stable causal identity.
Shows that transformer components can be organized as executable algorithm modules; it neither studies ICL selection nor supports the proposed causal switch claim.

shared_axes: retrieval or finite-support lookup versus inference under a generating family
lower-order or simpler sufficient statistic versus higher-order or more expressive statistic
markov_family: unigram retrieval from the finite pretraining chain set
bigram retrieval from the finite pretraining chain set
unigram inference under the generating prior
bigram inference under the generating prior
regression_family: finite-task posterior prediction in the registered low-dimensional class
finite-task posterior prediction in the registered full-dimensional class
route_dictionary_protocol.freeze_boundary: Before any sealed source checkpoint or target-family trained-model outcome is opened, hash both families' analytic route and oracle implementations, semantic interventions, diagnostic prompts, family-to-shared-axis mapping, output normalization, oracle-residual and collinearity tolerances, categorical target and unknown-class rule, predictor-abstention rule, surface features, source-fitted coefficients, interactions, thresholds, target-family filters and matcher, seed policy, and exclusion list.
invalidation_rules: Reject the family-level route claim if the registered candidate span leaves an oracle residual above tolerance on discovery or sealed positive controls.

Reject a discrete identity where route fingerprints are collinear, unstable under harmless diagnostic reweighting, or require per-seed label permutation; report a mixture, equivalence class, or abstention instead.
Treat any new candidate algorithm discovered after freeze as an out-of-dictionary failure for the current test, not as permission to refit and preserve the headline claim.

method: Before inspecting any trained-model outcome, designate Markov sequence modeling as the source family and nested noisy regression as the target family; implement and unit-test both four-route dictionaries, oracles, diagnostic panels, and semantic interventions from the analytic generators alone. Include prompts where candidates agree, disagree on one axis, disagree jointly, become deliberately collinear, or fall out of dictionary.

Train source-family discovery cohorts of small decoder-only transformers across a preregistered factorial of task diversity, context length, observation noise, class-mixture prior, ambiguity, depth, and checkpoints. Keep source-family seeds and configuration cells, one larger source model, one architecture variant, and every target-family trained-model outcome sealed; target jobs may run under a blinded manifest, but their outputs and outcome-dependent summaries remain unopened.

Estimate route weights only from source-family discovery outcomes with a constrained simplex fit plus an explicit residual channel. Assign one categorical target from the four registered routes plus unknown: mixtures, unstable winners, collinear fingerprints, and high-residual cases are unknown. Predictor abstention is a separate action and never removes a unit from scoring.

Construct both families' answer-matched route interventions from task semantics and analytic oracle behavior, not a learned probe or any target-model outcome. For Markov prompts, independently disrupt or restore finite-chain identity evidence and higher-order transition evidence while matching unigram counts, prompt length, final answer, and difficulty. For regression prompts, independently disrupt or restore finite-task identity and low- versus full-dimensional sufficient evidence while matching query answer, covariance, norm, noise, and margin.

Require a causal double dissociation: removing retrieval evidence must selectively reduce retrieval-route diagnostics and its registered counterfactual behavior while an inference-evidence intervention has the complementary effect; restoring only the removed statistic must rescue the corresponding route. Repeat for simple-versus-complex or unigram-versus-bigram evidence, with sham and equal-distance controls.

Use answer-matched donor and recipient pairs whose unpatched target answer, confidence, loss, token frequency, and context difficulty are within fixed tolerances but whose registered causal route labels differ. Internal patching, ablation, or task-vector measurements are secondary diagnostics and cannot rescue a failed semantic intervention.

Fit one prespecified sparse multinomial surface from normalized training progress, task diversity, context evidence, candidate loss gaps, candidate complexity gaps, and ambiguity margins to source-family discovery causal labels only. Limit interactions before fitting and expose equal-probability boundaries with uncertainty rather than drawing a heatmap by eye.

Compare with elapsed-step and diversity thresholds, loss-only selection, the hierarchical loss-complexity account, differential-kinetics forecasts, behavioral interpolation, static task-vector scores, current validation loss, model confidence, and a per-seed reidentified upper diagnostic that is explicitly ineligible as a prospective baseline.

Freeze the complete registry and make every confirmation outcome inaccessible to model selection. Evaluate first on sealed source-family seeds and configuration cells, then on the one larger source model and architecture variant, and only then open target-family trained-model outcomes using unchanged shared-axis labels, coefficients, thresholds, interventions, filters, matcher, and exclusions.

Prespecify target-family filtering and matching from generator metadata and analytic oracle outputs alone. Use no target-family trained-model answer, loss, confidence, route label, intervention effect, or aggregate outcome for feature selection, coefficient fitting, threshold choice, dose tuning, filtering, matching, or calibration. A target-family refit may be shown only after the frozen test as an ineligible diagnostic upper bound and counts as failure of the no-refit transfer claim.

Test robustness to harmless changes in diagnostic-query weighting, equivalent route implementations, prompt serialization, label permutations, donor order, metric choice, and bootstrap resampling. Route identity must remain fixed or correctly abstain.

Publish every route implementation, hash, discovery and sealed commitment, failed seed, residual, condition number, abstention, causal branch, matcher tolerance, fitted coefficient, boundary interval, and negative transfer result.

validation_funnel.gate: Unit tests recover every route oracle and planted mixture; collinear and out-of-dictionary controls abstain.
Source-family route labels remain stable across seeds, bootstrap samples, equivalent implementations, and harmless diagnostic reweightings.
Answer-matched remove-and-rescue interventions produce the preregistered route-by-intervention double dissociation without generic loss or confidence damage.
The switch surface beats every registered noncausal and single-mechanism baseline on sealed proper score and boundary location.

Analytic target routes, interventions, filters, and matching were committed before target training outcomes; the source-fitted labels, coefficients, and thresholds pass on completely untouched target outcomes with zero target-family calibration.
The frozen source registry passes unchanged on one larger model and one architecture variant; this supports only those transfer claims, not a scaling law.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: Small synthetic models can establish identifiability and causal selectivity but cannot establish scale. In the scoped experiment, an unopened larger model evaluated after every route definition, feature, coefficient, threshold, intervention, matcher tolerance, and exclusion is frozen is only a larger-model transfer test, not scale evidence. A scale claim requires at least three prespecified capacities, a capacity trend fit without the largest-capacity outcomes, and a frozen extrapolation to an unopened largest capacity; post-hoc relabeling or a single small-to-larger comparison is never scaling evidence.
supporting_evidence: The frozen surface improves the registered primary score and switch-boundary error over every eligible baseline on sealed source cells, the one larger source model, and completely untouched target-family outcomes.
Answer-matched causal effect signs and the route-by-intervention interaction retain their direction and minimum effect without route reidentification or dose tuning.
Oracle residual, route-margin calibration, condition number, abstention coverage, and label stability remain within preregistered bounds.
The result survives prompt serialization, label permutation, equivalent route code, diagnostic reweighting, and seed changes without a per-seed permutation of route names.
Any larger-model or architecture-variant success is stated as functional route transfer, not a scaling law or neuron-, layer-, direction-, or task-vector correspondence.
A future scale extension must prespecify at least three capacities, fit its capacity relationship on the smaller capacities only, and score a frozen extrapolation on the unopened largest capacity.
claim_blockers: Candidate predictions are collinear or their span leaves a large oracle residual on sealed data.
Route identity changes under harmless diagnostic reweighting, metric choice, equivalent implementations, or seed resampling.
A route assignment requires rediscovery, per-seed label permutation, confirmation-set inspection, or family-specific coefficient or threshold refitting.
Causal interventions mainly change generic competence, loss, confidence, length, or difficulty rather than the targeted solver diagnostic.
There is no answer-matched causal double dissociation or the registered rescue fails.
The frozen switch predictor loses to loss-only, Occam, differential-kinetics, elapsed-step, or behavioral-mixture baselines.
The larger model, target family, or architecture variant requires route reidentification, coefficient refitting, new features, target-outcome calibration, or changed exclusions.
prospective_design: Develop and unit-test both families' route code, planted mixtures, causal prompts, filters, and donor matching from analytic generators; fit the surface on source-family discovery outcomes only.
Commit hashes and a split manifest before producing any sealed source route plot, causal table, target-family trained-model summary, or fitted diagnostic.
Open sealed source-family configuration cells and seeds first, the one larger source model and architecture variant second, and completely untouched target-family trained-model outcomes last.
Keep target-family refits, new routes, alternate thresholds, and any target-outcome-dependent filtering or matching in a clearly labeled post-failure appendix only.
why_small_models_fail: Candidate algorithm support can change with capacity, optimization, context length, and task mixture, invalidating a route basis that fit a small model.
Training checkpoints and task diversity can correlate with ordinary loss and confidence, making an apparent switch surface a generic competence curve.
Causal prompt interventions can be exact in synthetic generators but lose selectivity when several sufficient statistics co-vary.
Seed-dependent superposition or continuous mixtures can destroy discrete route identity even when average behavior is stable.
Natural language and multimodal tasks need not admit the same executable algorithms or answer-matched interventions.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only Gates 1-3 pass, claim a validated causal route assay for the named small synthetic source family. If the frozen forecast passes sealed source-family cells but not the untouched target family, claim a source-family-specific switch surface. Claim no-refit transfer only for the exact target family, larger model, and architecture gates that pass unchanged and without target calibration. Do not use the word scaling unless a separate prespecified study covers at least three capacities and passes a frozen extrapolation to its unopened largest capacity. Never claim all ICL algorithms, a universal discrete router, Bayesian implementation from behavioral match, or cross-architecture neuron correspondence.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: On sealed source-family configuration cells and then completely untouched target-family outcomes, a sparse switch surface fitted only on source-family causal labels will improve the preregistered abstention-penalized categorical log score and exact switch-boundary metric over every eligible baseline under simultaneous comparison, while each admitted route clears the answer-matched remove-and-rescue causal gate.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: The frozen route names, algorithm implementations, features, coefficients, thresholds, interventions, target filters, and matcher will retain calibrated causal-route prediction on one unopened larger source transformer, one architecture variant, and the target family without per-seed label permutation, route reidentification, refitting, or target-outcome calibration; the larger-model result is transfer evidence, not scale evidence.
domains: Finite mixtures of Markov chains with retrieval versus inference and unigram versus bigram route oracles
Nested noisy linear regression with finite-task versus continuous-prior prediction and low- versus full-dimensional route oracles
Source-family discovery models across registered diversity, context, ambiguity, noise, depth, and training-time grids
Sealed source-family seeds and factorial cells, one larger source model, one architecture variant, and completely untouched target-family trained-model outcomes
Planted single-route, mixture, collinear, and out-of-dictionary positive and negative controls
baselines: Always-most-common route, nearest executable algorithm, and unconstrained behavioral simplex interpolation
Current training or validation loss, model confidence, context length, task diversity, elapsed step, and normalized pretraining loss
Loss-only candidate selection and the registered hierarchical loss-complexity or Occam predictor
Differential learning-kinetics and strategy-coopetition transition predictors
Retrospective four-phase behavioral classification from output proximity

Reproduction-style occupied-component comparators: task-schema-versus-binding activation-patching double dissociation; Contrastive-Context relevance-conditioned ICL-IWL switching; context-stickiness task-switch/recovery surfaces over pre/post example counts and curricula; and Test, then Route's asymmetric test-versus-readout dissociation, which is not treated as a double dissociation
Static global task-vector, local task-vector, probe, attribution, and edge-pruning diagnostics
Random, sham, answer-mismatched, same-length, same-norm, equal-distance, corrupted-pair, and generic-difficulty causal controls
A per-seed or target-family route reidentification, refit, target-outcome-dependent filter, or calibration as an ineligible post-test diagnostic upper bound
ablations: Two routes versus the complete four-route family dictionary and the explicit unknown residual channel
Remove loss gap, complexity gap, ambiguity, context evidence, diversity, or normalized training progress from the surface
Source-family discovery-only causal labels versus behavioral-proximity labels and probe-derived labels
Answer-matched versus unmatched donors and complete remove-ablate-rescue versus removal alone
Retrieval-evidence, inference-evidence, simple-statistic, and higher-order-statistic interventions separately and jointly
Fixed diagnostic weighting versus harmless reweightings and equivalent executable implementations
Frozen source-to-target coefficients with zero target calibration versus a target-family post-hoc refit
Sealed same-capacity source cells versus one larger source model and architecture-variant transfer
experiment.primary_outcome: Use one categorical target with five mutually exclusive classes: the four registered routes plus unknown; do not use soft targets. Mixtures, collinear or unstable winners, excessive oracle residuals, and failed causal identity gates are labeled unknown, which is distinct from predictor abstention. Every predictor must emit a five-class probability vector even when it abstains. The primary score is S = mean_i log(max(p_i[y_i], 1e-6)) - 0.25 * A/N, in nats per evaluated unit, where A is the number of predictor abstentions and all unknown targets and abstentions remain in N; higher is better. Also report misclassification risk at the preregistered 80% coverage point. Boundary error is the equal-weighted mean absolute difference in normalized sweep coordinate between the predicted first equal-probability crossing for each registered adjacent route pair and the first midpoint between adjacent sealed grid cells whose categorical causal target changes for that pair; assign error 1.0 for a missing or spurious crossing. Score-eligible means every registered baseline that emits a five-class probability vector under the identical source-only fitting budget; freeze that set before sealed outcomes, and never declare a baseline ineligible after seeing its result. Pass the score gate only if the simultaneous one-sided 95% seed-clustered max-t lower confidence bound for S uplift is at least 0.02 nats per unit against every score-eligible baseline and boundary error is at least 10% lower than every such baseline.
experiment.analysis: Fit one sparse multinomial logistic surface or fixed low-degree generalized additive surface on source-family discovery outcomes only, with seed and model as clustered effects and interactions fixed in advance. Evaluate the registered primary score, five-class log score and Brier score, calibration slope, categorical accuracy, abstention coverage, risk at 80% coverage, exact boundary error, oracle residual, and condition number on every unit. Estimate route-by-intervention double dissociations with matched-pair contrasts and seed-clustered hierarchical bootstrap intervals; require selective route movement after matching ordinary answer, loss, confidence, length, and difficulty. Use a seed-clustered max-t bootstrap to form simultaneous one-sided 95% lower bounds against all eligible baselines, correct the fixed route-by-family causal family for multiplicity, and report all seeds and failures. Apply the frozen source fit first to sealed source cells, then the larger source model and architecture variant, and finally untouched target-family outcomes; forbid target-outcome filtering, matching, label alignment, calibration, coefficient refitting, or threshold changes before the target test is scored.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass the narrow claim only if positive controls are recovered and collinear, mixed, or out-of-dictionary controls map to unknown; every claimed route clears the answer-matched remove-and-rescue double dissociation; the frozen surface clears the registered 0.02-nat simultaneous uplift, 10% boundary-error, and 80%-coverage selective-risk gates against every score-eligible baseline on sealed source cells; route identities survive harmless reweighting and equivalent implementations; and the source-fitted registry clears the same frozen gates on the larger source model, architecture variant, and completely untouched target-family outcomes with prespecified analytic filtering and matching and zero target-family calibration. If any condition fails, report the passed lower rung and reject prospective transferable causal switch surfaces. Passing one larger-model cohort supports only a larger-model transfer claim, never a scaling claim.

evaluation: Candidate-span oracle residual, fingerprint condition number, winning-route margin, bootstrap label stability, and unknown or abstention rate
Full-cohort five-class abstention-penalized log score, Brier score, calibration, categorical accuracy, and misclassification risk at 80% coverage

Registered first-crossing boundary mean absolute error across task diversity, context evidence, ambiguity, normalized training progress, and loss-complexity gaps, with unit penalty for missing or spurious crossings
Answer-matched route-by-intervention interaction, selective effect size, removal necessity, restoration rescue, off-route effect, and generic-competence collateral
Sensitivity to prompt serialization, label permutation, equivalent route implementation, diagnostic weighting, metric choice, donor order, and seed
Incremental performance over loss-only, Occam, kinetics, coopetition, elapsed-step, confidence, task-vector, and behavioral-mixture baselines

No-refit effect-sign, calibration, boundary, label-stability, and abstention transfer from source discovery to sealed source cells, one larger model, one architecture variant, and completely untouched target-family outcomes
Tokens, training FLOPs, checkpoint storage, causal branches, route-oracle calls, wall time, and failed or excluded runs
falsifiers: The executable route basis is collinear or leaves an oracle residual above the registered tolerance.
Harmless probe reweighting, equivalent code, metric choice, seed, or bootstrap sample changes route identity.
Stable labels require route rediscovery, a per-seed permutation, or target-outcome calibration after confirmation inspection.
Matched interventions reduce general competence, confidence, or answer quality but do not selectively move the targeted route diagnostic.
Retrieval and inference, or simple and complex, interventions do not form an answer-matched double dissociation and route-specific rescue.
A loss-only, Occam, differential-kinetics, elapsed-step, or behavioral-mixture baseline matches or beats the frozen surface.
The surface predicts retrospective proximity labels but not intervention-defined causal labels.
Sealed boundary orientation reverses across seeds or configuration cells without a preregistered abstention.

Target-family, larger-model, or architecture transfer needs new routes, new features, coefficient refitting, threshold tuning, outcome-dependent filtering or matching, changed exclusions, or label reassignment.
A task-vector, patching, or edge-pruning statistic appears causal only under one corruption, donor, metric, or answer-mismatched comparison.
risks: The candidate algorithms may be useful descriptions but not an identifiable basis; the residual and collinearity gates can therefore reject most configurations.
Route-specific semantic interventions can accidentally alter difficulty, entropy, or ordinary competence despite answer matching; multiple matching diagnostics and sham controls are mandatory.
The shared route axes may be too coarse for zero-calibration transfer from Markov chains to completely untouched regression outcomes, leaving only valid family-specific studies.
Dense checkpoint grids and many seeds create researcher degrees of freedom unless the split, smoothing, boundary definition, and multiplicity correction are frozen.
A continuous mixture can be scientifically correct while a discrete route label is unstable; the protocol must abstain rather than force a clean phase diagram.
Task-vector or circuit correlates may tempt an internal-mechanism claim that the functional interventions do not support.

The larger or alternate-architecture models may add routes absent from the source discovery dictionary; that is a prospective transfer failure, not a reason to revise the confirmation analysis or make a scale claim.
Synthetic answer matching and exact route code may not translate to natural tasks, so external-validity language must remain narrow.

milestones.name: Executable-basis audit
milestones.deliverable: Hash-pinned route code, planted single-route and mixture tests, oracle-residual and condition-number report for both families.
milestones.pass_condition: Every planted route is recovered; collinear and out-of-dictionary controls abstain at the frozen thresholds.

milestones.name: Answer-matched causal pilot
milestones.deliverable: At least 12 seed-checkpoint matched blocks for one route pair with removal, sham, rescue, and generic-difficulty controls.
milestones.pass_condition: The preregistered route-by-intervention contrast is selective, its clustered interval excludes zero, and ordinary answer collateral stays within tolerance.

milestones.name: Source-family discovery freeze
milestones.deliverable: Both analytically constructed four-route dictionaries and interventions plus the source-fitted sparse surface, coefficients, thresholds, diagnostic weights, target filter, matcher, exclusions, and sealed split committed by content hash.
milestones.pass_condition: Source discovery cross-validation beats every baseline without unstable route permutations and no sealed source or target-family trained-model outcome has been opened.

milestones.name: Sealed same-family forecast
milestones.deliverable: Proper-score, boundary, causal, stability, and abstention report for unopened seeds and factorial cells.
milestones.pass_condition: The complete noncompensatory primary decision rule passes on sealed source-family cells without refit.

milestones.name: No-refit larger-model, architecture, and target-family transfer
milestones.deliverable: Unchanged-registry results on one larger source model and architecture variant, followed by completely untouched target-family trained-model outcomes, including every negative transfer.
milestones.pass_condition: Calibration, boundary, and causal effect gates pass with no route reidentification, coefficient or threshold change, target-outcome calibration, or post-hoc exclusion; describe the larger-model result as transfer, not scaling.

first_week: Implement and unit-test the four Markov route oracles and four nested-regression route oracles, including planted mixtures, collinear pairs, and an explicit unknown residual.
Generate a small factorial corpus and train at least four seeds of one 10M-30M-parameter model with dense checkpoints around the expected retrieval-to-inference transition.
Write the route registry schema and content-hash commitment covering code, fingerprints, diagnostic weights, label rule, condition-number and residual thresholds, and abstention semantics.
Build one answer-matched retrieval-versus-inference removal, sham, and rescue intervention per family and verify matching of answer, loss, confidence, prompt length, entropy, norm, and difficulty.

Fit only the prespecified loss, Occam, kinetics, elapsed-step, behavioral-mixture, occupied-component, and sparse combined baselines on source-family discovery outcomes; estimate whether a sealed study is powered.

Reserve source seed IDs, factorial cells, larger-model configuration, architecture variant, and every target-family trained-model outcome in a machine-readable sealed manifest before producing a final route heatmap or causal result.

competitive_landscape.title: Competition Dynamics Shape Algorithmic Phases of In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It decomposes behavior into fuzzy retrieval versus inference crossed with unigram versus bigram statistics and tracks phase changes. This proposal reuses that as a baseline and contributes only a sealed causal-route forecast, answer-matched interventions, and no-refit transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It identifies coexistence, competition, cooperation, and shared subcircuits between ICL and context-constrained in-weights learning. The proposed delta is independently fixed route identities plus prospective switch prediction on unseen settings, not another coopetition narrative.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers as Statisticians: Provable In-Context Learning with In-Context Algorithm Selection
competitive_landscape.difference: It constructs and observes adaptive selection among least squares, ridge, Lasso, generalized linear models, and other procedures using pre-tests or post-validation. It does not test a learned route's causal identity or freeze a longitudinal switch forecast before unseen cohorts.

competitive_landscape.title: When Is a Task Vector Enough? An Empirical Theory of Implicit Multimodal ICL
competitive_landscape.relationship: 2026 near-blocker on intervention selection and realization
competitive_landscape.difference: It contrasts static task-vector interventions with query-specific or distributed realization using matched counterfactuals and predicts when extra intervention complexity is useful. This proposal must therefore avoid a universal task vector and adds only a frozen multi-algorithm switch surface with causal route labels and sealed no-refit transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Test, then Route: How Language Models Execute In-Context Conditional Rules Across Models and Languages
competitive_landscape.difference: It reports an asymmetric causal test-versus-readout dissociation with a four-donor patching design across models, families, languages, and predicates, and finds the router token-bound rather than abstract; this is not a double dissociation. The surviving delta here is prospective selection among independently executable algorithms, not rediscovery of a test-and-route circuit.

competitive_landscape.title: Task Schema and Binding: A Double Dissociation Study of In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: near-blocker on causal schema–binding double dissociation and architecture breadth
competitive_landscape.difference: It reports an activation-patching double dissociation between task schema and binding across nine models spanning seven Transformer families plus Mamba, so double dissociation and broad architecture coverage are not themselves novel. It does not register executable solver alternatives, forecast a training-time switch boundary on sealed cohorts, or transfer a frozen no-refit surface between task families.

competitive_landscape.title: Training In-Context and In-Weights Mixtures Via Contrastive Context Sampling
competitive_landscape.relationship: near-blocker on learned ICL–IWL switching by context relevance
competitive_landscape.difference: It teaches stable ICL–IWL mixtures that change with target–context similarity using Contrastive-Context, with a minimal-model analysis, diagnostic probes, four LLMs, and several real and synthetic tasks. It does not identify an intervention-defined causal solver route, register an executable multi-algorithm dictionary, make a sealed prospective switch forecast, or test no-refit family/scale transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: When Context Sticks: Studying Interference in In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: near-blocker on task-switch/recovery surfaces and curriculum dependence
competitive_landscape.difference: It sweeps abrupt linear↔quadratic in-prompt switches over structured pre/post context counts and training curricula to map behavioral interference and recovery surfaces. It does not arbitrate among competing internal solver routes, supply answer-matched remove/rescue causal labels, freeze a prospective route boundary, or test cross-family no-refit transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Differential learning kinetics govern the transition from memorization to generalization during in-context learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It models memorizing and generalizing subcircuits as largely independent learners and explains transition scaling through their rates. The proposed surface must beat this kinetics baseline and adds sealed multi-route causal labels rather than another transition fit.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamics of Transient Structure in In-Context Linear Regression Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: It tracks transient ridge-like structure, specialization, trajectory geometry, and Bayesian local complexity. It does not freeze a functional route dictionary, forecast causal switches on sealed cohorts, or require an answer-matched double dissociation.

competitive_landscape.title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
competitive_landscape.difference: It matches trained transformers to gradient descent, ridge, least squares, and Bayesian-like predictors as depth and noise vary and probes internal representations. Algorithm matching and transitions are not prospective causal arbitration forecasts.

competitive_landscape.title: Dual Operating Modes of In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives task retrieval and task learning regimes in Bayesian multi-group regression. Its binary modes do not establish independently separable routes across two families or a frozen causal switch boundary.

competitive_landscape.title: In-Context Learning through the Bayesian Prism
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies Bayesian prediction over unions of linear and nonlinear task families and transformer deviations from that norm. Those normative alternatives do not identify causal route identities or predict sealed transitions.

competitive_landscape.title: The Evolution of Statistical Induction Heads: In-Context Learning Markov Chains
competitive_landscape.difference: It traces uniform-to-unigram-to-bigram phases and interference from simpler strategies in Markov tasks. It neither independently forecasts a multi-route causal boundary nor transfers a frozen route registry.

competitive_landscape.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses training-time activation clamping to isolate additive subcircuits that enable induction-head formation. That is a causal account of one mechanism, not a frozen selector among solver families or a sealed switch-surface test.

competitive_landscape.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
competitive_landscape.difference: It links induction-head formation to an ICL phase change and gives causal evidence for match-and-copy behavior. It does not cover multi-algorithm support, ambiguous route identity, or prospective route boundaries.

competitive_landscape.title: In-Context Learning Creates Task Vectors
competitive_landscape.difference: It compresses demonstrations into patchable task vectors that can drive query-only inference. A task vector is not a discrete algorithm router, and the proposal treats it as a baseline rather than a route definition.

competitive_landscape.title: Label Words as Local Task Vectors in In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It finds that some tasks use local label-word task vectors rather than one global vector, especially when rules require multiple demonstrations. This directly blocks any universal compact-state claim and motivates functional route definitions and abstention.

competitive_landscape.title: Task Vectors in In-Context Learning: Emergence, Formation, and Benefit
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies task-vector emergence in models trained from scratch and can force stronger localization with an auxiliary loss. It does not prospectively predict naturally learned route switches or arbitrate among fixed algorithms.

competitive_landscape.title: Contextualize-then-Aggregate: Circuits for In-Context Learning in Gemma-2 2B
competitive_landscape.difference: It causally identifies contextualize-then-aggregate information flow across five Gemma-2 tasks and shows contextualization varies with ambiguity. It occupies causal ambiguous-context analysis but not competing-solver kinetics or a sealed switch forecast.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Sparse Feature Circuits for Studying In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It identifies causal task-detection and task-execution SAE features alongside competing task-specific features at scale. It does not make a prospective, support-controlled arbitration forecast with a frozen executable route basis.

competitive_landscape.title: Measuring Inductive Biases of In-Context Learning with Underspecified Demonstrations
competitive_landscape.difference: It constructs demonstrations compatible with two NLP rules and measures which behavioral inductive bias wins under prompting interventions. It does not identify causal routes or forecast longitudinal algorithm switches.

competitive_landscape.title: In-Context Learning with Long-Context Models: An In-Depth Exploration
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows thousands-shot gains, contrasts retrieval with full-context ICL, and finds mechanism balance changes with context length and dataset. It supplies an important axis and baseline but no causal solver switch or frozen forecast.

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Transformer Circuits with Edge Pruning
competitive_landscape.difference: It scales edge-pruning circuit discovery and compares overlap among prompting and ICL circuits. Pruned edges are a discovery artifact rather than a functional route identity, so edge overlap remains secondary here.

competitive_landscape.title: AtP*: An efficient and scalable method for localizing LLM behaviour to components
competitive_landscape.difference: AtP* improves scalable component localization and diagnoses false negatives. It is a method for finding candidate components, not evidence of route-specific necessity, double dissociation, or prospective selection.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows that patching conclusions depend on corruption and metric choices. The proposed protocol therefore requires answer-matched donors, multiple registered metrics, removal plus rescue, and negative controls; one patching map cannot define a route.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after three substantive hash-pinned full-text readings, one explicitly boundary-only reading, and a 26-record current primary-source audit: the broad idea of causal arbitration among in-context algorithms is not novel. Competition Dynamics already supplies a four-algorithm phase diagram; Strategy Coopetition supplies interacting strategy dynamics and shared subcircuits; Transformers as Statisticians supplies provable and empirical algorithm selection; Task Schema and Binding supplies a causal double dissociation across broad architecture coverage; Contrastive Context Sampling supplies learned relevance-conditioned ICL-IWL switching; and When Context Sticks supplies behavioral task-switch and recovery surfaces with curriculum dependence. Kinetics, Bayesian, nested-class, induction-head, task-vector, sparse-circuit, long-context, and ambiguity studies cover most remaining component claims. The August 2026 near-blockers are also constraining: When Is a Task Vector Enough? uses matched counterfactuals to choose between static and query-specific or distributed interventions, while Test, then Route reports an asymmetric causal test-versus-readout dissociation across models and languages and finds the router token-bound; it is not a double dissociation. The defensible contribution is therefore only the conjunction of an analytically frozen executable multi-algorithm basis for both families, a source-family-only fitted prospective route-switch boundary, answer-matched route-specific remove-and-rescue causal labels, sealed same-family confirmation, and zero-calibration transfer to completely untouched target-family outcomes. This is a reviewer inference from a bounded current audit, not an exhaustive priority proof. If routes are relabeled after inspection, target outcomes affect filtering, matching, calibration, or coefficients, causal selectivity is replaced by generic competence effects, or transfer requires refitting, reject the novelty claim. A successful one-larger-model test supports transfer only, not scaling.
brief.evidence_note: Substantive support comes only from arxiv:2506.17859v2 (2025-06-26), arxiv:2506.19351v1 (2025-06-24), and arxiv:2507.01414v2 (2026-06-16): 125 fully read pages, 30 page-attributed findings, 70 anchors, and 31 competitor entries spanning 21 unique primary records. Arxiv:2506.19125v2 (2026-08-07) was also read in full but is counted only as a boundary and structural algorithm-compilation blueprint, never as evidence for ICL route selection. The independent promotion audit directly compared 26 exact-version primary records, including arxiv:2512.17325v1 (2025-12-19), arxiv:2604.01601v1 (2026-04-02), arxiv:2604.23371v1 (2026-04-25), and both August 2026 near-blockers. Those additions establish that causal double dissociation, learned ICL-IWL switching, and behavioral switch/recovery surfaces are individually occupied; they support only the narrower conjunction stated here.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
A credible crossover needs multiple horizons, model scales, and controller-tuning budgets, although checkpoint replay and aggressive low-fidelity pruning keep the pilot manageable.
Gradient calls, loss queries, future information, tuning FLOPs, parallelism, wall time, untouched-scale rank, and final loss are directly measurable and yield crisp rejection rules.

Tuning-free optimization, online schedule search, schedule-free training, and hypergradients are crowded; the defensible delta is a prospective information-and-resource crossover certificate rather than a new controller.
A small transformer and convex stress suite can expose hidden query or oracle costs within a week, while a convincing untouched-scale test takes longer.

assumptions: Each controller can be applied to identical checkpoints, minibatches, parameter groups, and base-optimizer update geometry.
Proposal losses, gradient calls, future horizon, lower bounds, terminal-performance estimates, tuning runs, and available parallel workers can be recorded as separate currencies.
A development-scale controller and its features can be frozen before any target-scale loss curve is inspected.
A scheduler advantage must survive both serial-resource and realistically parallelized accounting rather than relying on unmeasured concurrency.

brief.title: Oracle-budgeted learning-rate controller crossover certificates
brief.thesis: Hold minibatches, checkpoints, parameterization, and base-optimizer update geometry fixed, then compare adaptive learning-rate controllers under an explicit ledger of gradient calls, proposal-loss queries, horizon knowledge, lower-bound or terminal-performance oracles, tuning FLOPs, parallel workers, and wall time. A controller earns a scaling claim only if a rule frozen on small workloads predicts its advantage over tuned cosine, WSD, and schedule-free baselines at an untouched horizon, architecture, data order, and scale after every information and resource cost is charged.
brief.motivation: Recent learning-rate papers answer different questions with different information budgets: AutoGD evaluates three deterministic proposals per step, adaptive Polyak methods use optimum-loss or lower-bound signals, an optimal-control rule assumes terminal performance, and near-optimal shape search consumes millions of offline trials plus a known horizon. Comparing their reported steps or best losses treats queries, oracles, parallelism, and tuning as free. A common prospective crossover protocol would show when adaptivity is genuinely useful and when it only relocates tuning or future information.
brief.research_question: Which learning-rate controllers remain better than strong fixed and schedule-free baselines after their information, query, tuning, parallelism, and transfer costs are normalized?
non_claims: The project does not propose a new optimizer or learning-rate controller.
A reduction in nominal training steps is not an efficiency gain when extra proposal losses, tuning runs, or serial latency erase it.
A controller selected after inspecting the target scale does not demonstrate scale transfer.
One scalar ranking is not valid across mutually incompatible resource budgets; the result is a Pareto frontier and registered crossover rule.
subquestions: How do controller rankings change under gradient-call, scored-example, serial wall-time, parallel wall-time, peak-memory, and total-tuning-FLOP budgets?
Which advantages survive removal or misspecification of optimum loss, lower bound, horizon, terminal performance, or validation-forecast signals?
Can small-scale curve shape, query efficiency, and controller stability prospectively predict untouched-scale crossover without target retuning?
Do batch size, data order, nonstationarity, architecture, and horizon cause ranking reversals large enough to block universal scheduler claims?
method: Create a checkpoint-replay harness that applies each candidate rate to the same weights, minibatch, random state, weight decay, momentum or preconditioner, and parameter groups. Separate the rate controller from update geometry so only the control policy changes.

Instrument a resource ledger for backward passes, full and sampled loss queries, examples scored, future horizon, lower-bound and terminal-gap information, validation forecasts, tuning trials, accelerator hours, serial critical path, parallel workers, memory, and synchronization.

Evaluate AutoGD, oracle and safeguarded SF-SPS, terminal-gap feedback, AutoLRS or AdaLRS, hypergradient descent, D-Adaptation, tuned cosine and WSD, schedule-free training, and a low-dimensional offline shape search. Give every method the same registered tuning and early-stopping budget.

Fit a small development-only crossover rule from early loss curvature, gradient noise, proposal disagreement, oracle error, query overhead, and horizon. Freeze controller configurations, features, thresholds, and claim language before opening the target scale and held-out data order.

Report separate Pareto frontiers for serial and parallel execution, then ablate each privileged signal and inject registered oracle error, horizon mismatch, interruption, batch shift, and nonstationarity.

validation_funnel.gate: Every controller must receive identical checkpoints, batches, gradients, update geometry, and numerical precision; a fixed-rate replay must reproduce the reference trajectory within tolerance.
Every proposal loss, gradient, future signal, bound, validation forecast, tuning run, worker, and synchronization point must appear in the ledger before a step-efficiency result is reported.
An adaptive controller must beat tuned cosine, WSD, or schedule-free training on at least one preregistered resource frontier without worsening the co-primary final-loss and stability gates.
The frozen crossover rule must retain its predicted sign and useful rank on the untouched horizon, architecture, data order, and largest scale without retuning.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: A controller comparison supports scale transfer only when the complete information ledger, controller configurations, and crossover rule are frozen before the untouched horizon, architecture, data order, and larger model are opened.
prospective_design: Develop and tune controllers only on the registered small workloads, then freeze their budgets, features, thresholds, oracle-error model, and serial-versus-parallel accounting.
Reserve one larger model, horizon, architecture, and data-order shift as a joint untouched test rather than treating them as tuning axes.
Publish every target controller run and retain failed or unstable trials in the resource ledger.
supporting_evidence: The frozen crossover rule predicts the sign of at least one preregistered target-region advantage
Final validation loss and area under the loss curve improve under matched total tuning-plus-training resources
The advantage persists under both serial critical-path and registered parallel-resource accounting without worse instability
claim_blockers: Target-scale rank or effect sign reverses after full information and resource charging
The result requires retuning controller features, budgets, oracle assumptions, or parallelism after the holdout is opened
An apparent gain disappears against tuned cosine, WSD, or schedule-free baselines under the registered ledger
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'the frozen controller crossover transferred within the tested horizons, architectures, data orders, and scale interval.' Do not claim a universally superior scheduler.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: Once all information and resource currencies are charged, adaptive controllers will occupy different Pareto regions rather than dominate universally, and a development-only rule will correctly predict at least one untouched-scale crossover against tuned cosine, WSD, and schedule-free baselines.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Proposal-query controllers will retain value on smooth deterministic or low-noise workloads with parallel evaluation, while lower-bound and terminal-gap controllers will lose most of their advantage under realistic oracle error, nonstationarity, or serial latency.
domains: Deterministic convex, nonconvex, and rapidly changing directional-curvature stress tests
Small language-model pretraining with controlled batch, token, and horizon sweeps
Image classification as a cross-architecture transfer check
An untouched larger language model and sealed data-order shift
baselines: Tuned constant, cosine, warmup-stable-decay, and one-cycle schedules
Schedule-Free SGD or AdamW with a matched base-rate search
AutoGD with serial and three-way parallel proposal accounting
Oracle and safeguarded Schedule-Free Polyak controllers
Terminal-performance feedback with oracle and forecasted terminal gaps
AutoLRS, AdaLRS, hypergradient descent, and D-Adaptation
Low-dimensional offline schedule-shape search at the same tuning budget
ablations: Remove optimum-loss, lower-bound, horizon, terminal-performance, and validation-forecast signals one at a time
Vary oracle error and register optimistic, conservative, and adversarial misspecification
Charge nominal steps only versus gradient calls, loss queries, tokens, accelerator time, and serial critical path
Allow three-way proposal parallelism versus one-worker execution
Freeze the development policy versus retune at each target as an invalid upper bound
Shift batch size, data order, horizon, architecture, and loss nonstationarity independently
experiment.primary_outcome: Final validation loss and area under the validation-loss curve at matched total tuning plus training accelerator-hours, with serial wall time and scored tokens reported as co-primary resource views.
experiment.analysis: Report per-budget Pareto dominance, paired checkpoint effects, seed intervals, target-scale rank and sign accuracy, calibration of the crossover rule, ranking reversals, oracle-sensitivity curves, and the fraction of apparent gains erased by query or tuning overhead.
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if at least one preregistered adaptive region beats all fixed and schedule-free baselines at matched resources, the frozen crossover rule predicts the sign at the untouched scale and shift, co-primary final loss and instability do not worsen, and removal of privileged signals does not reveal that the claim depended on an uncounted oracle. Otherwise narrow the result to the measured development regime.

evaluation: Validation loss, final loss, and area under the loss curve at matched tokens and optimizer updates
Backward passes, proposal losses, examples scored, validation queries, and total tuning trials
Training and tuning FLOPs, accelerator-hours, serial critical path, parallel workers, peak memory, and communication
Untouched-scale rank correlation, sign accuracy, top-controller regret, calibration, and ranking-reversal rate
Sensitivity to optimum-loss, lower-bound, terminal-gap, horizon, and forecast error
Loss spikes, divergence, update norms, gradient noise, and seed uncertainty
Performance under interruption, horizon extension, batch shift, data reorder, and nonstationarity
risks: Controller implementations can differ subtly in momentum, averaging, warmup, clipping, or weight decay. Use one update kernel and golden checkpoint-replay tests before comparing outcomes.
Parallel proposal evaluation may be realistic on idle hardware but wasteful at saturation. Publish both serial and measured parallel frontiers and the exact worker allocation.

A large baseline sweep can make fixed schedules look artificially expensive while controller hyperparameters remain hidden. Register symmetric search spaces and include all development trials in total cost.

Terminal performance and sample-optimum losses may be unavailable rather than merely noisy. Include no-oracle variants and treat oracle methods as upper bounds when the signal cannot be obtained causally.
Small workloads may not predict larger-scale scheduler rankings. Seal the target scale and make reversal a claim blocker rather than explaining it away after inspection.
One workload can favor a controller because its loss units or batch variance match an implicit assumption. Repeat across loss rescaling, batch, architecture, and nonstationarity shifts.
first_week: Implement the shared rate-controller interface and golden replay test for constant, cosine, schedule-free, AutoGD, and safeguarded Polyak policies.
Add the explicit information and resource ledger, including serial critical path and hypothetical versus measured proposal parallelism.
Run deterministic quadratic, saddle, and directional-curvature stress tests with lower-bound and horizon misspecification.
Launch a small transformer pilot from shared checkpoints and compare nominal-step rankings with token, query, and wall-time rankings.
Preregister development tasks, target scale, controller budgets, crossover features, and the scale-transfer decision rule.

competitive_landscape.title: AutoGD: Automatic Learning Rate Selection for Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: AutoGD chooses among three deterministic proposals and offers strong local analysis, but reported runtime parity assumes unmeasured parallel proposal evaluation and supplies no stochastic or deep-scale transfer test.

competitive_landscape.title: Taking the Road Less Scheduled with Adaptive Polyak Steps
competitive_landscape.difference: SF-SPS derives a schedule-free Polyak correction, but oracle and safe variants consume different optimum-loss or lower-bound information and the practical Adam recipe lies outside its convex theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Learning Rate Schedule for Balancing Effort and Performance
competitive_landscape.difference: The HJB controller optimizes cumulative performance minus effort and uses optimal terminal performance, not conventional final loss; the proposal audits that privileged signal and objective under matched ML outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: What Do Near-Optimal Learning Rate Schedules Look Like?
competitive_landscape.difference: This study separates scale from shape across more than eleven million small runs, but consumes a known horizon and large search budget and does not freeze a cross-scale prediction.

competitive_landscape.title: The Road Less Scheduled
competitive_landscape.difference: Schedule-free training removes decay and horizon tuning but retains a base learning rate. It is a required matched-geometry baseline for any controller claiming to remove schedules.

competitive_landscape.title: AutoLRS: Automatic Learning-Rate Schedule by Bayesian Optimization on the Fly
competitive_landscape.difference: AutoLRS branches candidate rates and forecasts validation loss with Bayesian optimization. Its branch and validation costs belong in the same query and tuning ledger.

competitive_landscape.title: AdaLRS: Loss-Guided Adaptive Learning Rate Search for Efficient Foundation Model Pretraining
competitive_landscape.difference: AdaLRS adapts from loss-descent velocity and reports cross-size pretraining evidence. It is a strong empirical comparator for prospective scale transfer rather than a free controller.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient-based Hyperparameter Optimization through Reversible Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Reversible learning can optimize thousands of schedule values through the entire trajectory. It supplies an expensive upper bound whose backward-through-training cost must be counted.

competitive_landscape.title: Online Learning Rate Adaptation with Hypergradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: Hypergradient descent updates a global rate online with little extra work and no proposal branches. It tests whether elaborate controllers beat a simple adaptive mechanism at equal geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Population Based Training of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: PBT reuses population training while evolving trajectory-specific hyperparameters. Its population and exploit-explore costs form a distinct tuning frontier rather than an ordinary training run.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning-Rate-Free Learning by D-Adaptation
competitive_landscape.difference: D-Adaptation estimates distance-to-solution without line search or extra loss proposals and includes deep-learning tests. It is a strong no-query adaptive baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Tuning-Free Stochastic Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: This work defines comparison with optimally tuned SGD and proves impossibility without some prior knowledge. It motivates reporting every oracle and hint instead of calling a controller parameter-free.

competitive_landscape.title: Stochastic Polyak Step-size for SGD: An Adaptive Learning Rate for Fast Convergence
competitive_landscape.difference: SPS provides a core loss-gap controller whose strongest story often assumes interpolation or sample optima. It anchors oracle removal and misspecification tests.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four hash-pinned, page-anchored readings and a 38-record primary-source audit: deterministic proposal search, stochastic Polyak rules, schedule-free averaging, terminal-effort control, offline schedule-shape search, validation forecasting, hypergradients, population search, and tuning-free bounds are established. The defensible contribution is not another controller; it is a prospectively frozen crossover certificate that normalizes information, queries, tuning, serial and parallel resources, and then tests ranking transfer at an untouched scale and shift.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current full-text readings totaling 106 pages, with 62 page-bounded findings, 143 anchors, and 38 directly checked primary-source competitor comparisons. The proposal deliberately holds update geometry fixed, so it does not duplicate the Muon mechanism-crossover brief.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
Forward-only methods are memory-light but query-heavy, and a prospective scale crossover needs replicated HPO budgets and at least one expensive untouched model.
Separate scored-token, accelerator-hour, peak-memory, and HPO frontiers plus retention and exploitability metrics make optimizer rankings explicitly falsifiable.
ES, low-rank ES, MeZO, curvature-aware zeroth order, GRPO, forgetting controls, and systems studies exist; the prospective resource-normalized crossover map is the narrow contribution.
Small-model frontiers can reject broad dominance claims quickly, but a credible phase boundary and scale forecast require longer matched-budget runs.

assumptions: All methods start from identical checkpoints and see identical frozen task and reward definitions; environment generation is outside this study.
Queries, scored tokens, accelerator time, peak memory, communication, and hyperparameter search can be logged independently rather than collapsed into one convenient budget.
Validation tasks used for optimizer selection remain disjoint from final evaluation and do not leak benchmark answers into checkpoint choice.
A scale claim requires a crossover surface frozen before an unseen model size and task family, not a retrospective trend line.

brief.title: Where does search beat gradients? A resource-normalized post-training phase diagram
brief.thesis: Compare dense evolution strategies, low-rank EGGROLL-style search, memory-efficient and curvature-aware zeroth-order updates, and GRPO from identical checkpoints under four separate resource ledgers. Fit a low-complexity crossover surface from model size, sequence length, reward sparsity, noise, and target headroom, freeze it, and test whether it predicts the hindsight Pareto set and a low-regret optimizer under each preregistered resource preference on an unseen scale and task family.
brief.motivation: Recent LLM evolution-strategy results match response counts rather than wall-clock, tokens, tuning effort, or hardware; select checkpoints on reported evaluation sets; extrapolate scale retrospectively; and often omit off-task retention. Follow-on low-rank work improves linear-layer throughput but sometimes spends far more queries and lacks a co-run gradient baseline at its largest scale. Theoretical random-search papers also contain gaps between stated class-wide rates and what their proofs or implemented estimators support. An optimizer ranking is therefore meaningful only after the resource and selection estimands are fixed.
brief.research_question: Across which model, task, reward, and memory regimes do evolutionary or zeroth-order methods lie on the post-training Pareto frontier, and can a small-scale crossover rule predict the Pareto set and low-regret choice under preregistered resource preferences before an unseen large run?
non_claims: The project does not propose a new optimizer or claim evolution strategies, low-rank perturbations, zeroth-order gradients, GRPO, antithetic sampling, or anchored retention as new.
A response-count win is not a wall-clock, token, energy, memory, or HPO win.
Fixed benchmark and environment definitions are held constant; this brief does not validate or evolve RL environments.
Small-model rankings do not establish scale transfer unless the preregistered unseen-scale prediction succeeds.
subquestions: Does dense or low-rank ES remain competitive after scored tokens, queries, accelerator-hours, communication, and HPO trials are charged separately?
Which regimes favor inference-like forward-only workloads because peak memory, not total compute, is the binding resource?
Do estimator variance, update rank, effective dimension, and target headroom explain crossover better than model parameter count alone?
How much target gain is purchased with off-task forgetting, dense parameter drift, reward exploitation, or unstable population selection?
Can a frozen phase boundary choose the optimizer for an unseen model and task within a registered regret tolerance?
method: Freeze a task panel spanning verifiable math, code-unit tests, noisy preference or scalar rewards, and one exploit-prone synthetic task. Vary sequence length, reward sparsity and noise, and distance from the target behavior without changing task definitions between optimizers.
At each shared checkpoint run dense antithetic ES, low-rank EGGROLL-style ES, MeZO, curvature-aware low-rank zeroth order, and GRPO with a common evaluator, checkpoint policy, and stopping interface.

Give every method the same registered HPO protocol, then publish separate Pareto frontiers for scored tokens or queries, accelerator-hours, peak memory, and total charged tuning cost instead of declaring one universal winner.

Log population or minibatch estimator variance, update norm, rank, subspace overlap, layer distribution, function-space KL, reward exploitability, and off-task retention from identical pre-update checkpoints.
Fit a sparse crossover model on two development sizes and held-in task families; freeze features, coefficients, budgets, and decision thresholds before opening the target scale and task family.
Run native optimized kernels and a hardware-portability control, reporting inference throughput, communication, and evaluation bottlenecks separately from optimizer arithmetic.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: Development-scale frontiers locate candidate regimes but do not certify scaling. Freeze the resource ledger and crossover surface before the larger model and new task family are evaluated.
supporting_evidence: The frozen model predicts the Pareto-optimal optimizer or set at the unseen scale with regret below the preregistered tolerance
Crossover directions remain stable under separate query, wall-clock, memory, and charged-HPO budgets
Estimator-geometry features add predictive value beyond parameter count, sequence length, and elapsed compute
Target gains survive retention and exploitability gates rather than merely optimizing the scalar reward
Rankings remain directionally stable on a second hardware configuration after kernels are optimized
claim_blockers: The unseen-scale winner falls outside the predicted Pareto set
Optimizer ranking reverses when HPO or evaluation tokens are charged
A claimed ES advantage disappears under wall-clock matching or a co-run memory-efficient gradient baseline
Target gains coincide with materially worse off-task retention or reward exploitation
The crossover model adds no value beyond simple model-size and memory thresholds
Performance requires choosing checkpoints on final evaluation tasks
prospective_design: Develop the ledger and crossover model on two smaller sizes and three task families
Freeze algorithms, kernels, HPO trials, stopping rules, and all cost conversions
Predict the frontier for an untouched larger model and fourth task family before training begins
Publish failed trials, selected and unselected checkpoints, and per-resource frontiers
why_small_models_fail: Forward-pass throughput, communication, and activation memory scale differently from backward computation
Useful update geometry and local expert density can change with model size and target headroom
Longer sequences change the relative price of scored trajectories and gradient backpropagation
Population size and low-rank perturbations can shift query efficiency and hardware utilization in opposite directions
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If only development regimes pass, report matched-budget frontiers for those regimes. Claim a predictive crossover law only if the frozen unseen-scale and unseen-task gates pass.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: No optimizer universally dominates: a frozen model using memory pressure, sequence length, reward noise or sparsity, target headroom, and estimator geometry will predict the hindsight Pareto set and lower per-ledger decision regret on an unseen scale than always choosing GRPO, dense ES, low-rank ES, or MeZO.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: ES advantages will concentrate in low-memory, inference-throughput-rich regimes, but will shrink after scored-token and HPO charging and after off-task retention is treated as a co-primary outcome.
experiment.primary_outcome: Per-ledger decision regret on the unseen scale and task relative to the hindsight Pareto set under preference vectors frozen before the target run, with retention and exploitability as hard feasibility gates.
experiment.resource_scalarization: Report the full nondominated set for scored tokens, accelerator hours, peak memory, and charged HPO. For each decision analysis, freeze a monotone preference vector or hard resource cap on development runs and define regret as utility loss relative to the best feasible member of the target hindsight Pareto set. No single optimizer is called 'the Pareto winner.'
domains: Two development LLM sizes and one untouched larger instruction or reasoning model
Verifier-scored math and code tasks
Noisy or sparse scalar-reward tasks with controlled corruption
One exploit-prone synthetic task plus a fixed off-task retention suite
baselines: Dense antithetic ES with fitness shaping
Low-rank EGGROLL-style ES across registered ranks and population sizes
MeZO and curvature-aware low-rank zeroth-order fine-tuning
GRPO with a matched policy-evaluation and HPO budget
Supervised full-gradient or low-rank fine-tuning where labels exist
Always-select-one-optimizer, model-size-only, and memory-threshold crossover rules
ablations: Charge responses only, then scored tokens, accelerator-hours, communication, and HPO trials cumulatively
Full-rank versus low-rank perturbations and isotropic versus curvature-aware directions
Population size, antithetic pairing, fitness shaping, and common-random-number evaluation
Zero versus anchored weight decay and explicit retention regularization
Checkpoint selection on a disjoint validation panel versus prohibited final-test selection
Fit crossover coefficients at target scale versus keep them prospectively frozen
experiment.decision_rule: Pass only if the frozen crossover model predicts the target nondominated set better than the fixed-optimizer baselines and achieves no more than 5% preregistered utility regret relative to the best feasible hindsight-Pareto member under each of at least three frozen resource preferences, while passing retention and exploitability gates. If preference vectors or resource caps were not frozen, report only the measured frontiers and reject predictive crossover.

evaluation: Target gain, success rate, calibration, best-achieved reward, and robustness across seeds
Scored sequences, scored tokens, forward queries, backward passes, and total evaluation tokens
Accelerator-hours, wall-clock, peak and persistent memory, communication volume, and energy proxy
Charged HPO trials, failed runs, checkpoint-selection cost, and compute-to-target
Estimator variance, signal-to-noise ratio, update rank, subspace overlap, layer concentration, and function-space KL
Off-task retention, catastrophic forgetting, recovery after anchoring, and reward exploitability
Crossover calibration, predicted Pareto-set coverage, unseen-regime regret, and coefficient stability
risks: Resource ledgers are hardware-dependent. Report raw counters and frontiers per machine instead of one fragile dollar conversion.
A complete factorial sweep can become unaffordable. Use sequential elimination within preregistered budgets and never drop failures from cost accounting.
GRPO and ES consume qualitatively different samples. Publish several legitimate resource views rather than asserting a single equivalence.
Reward models can hide exploitation. Use verifier checks where possible and manually audit a blinded sample of high-reward outputs.
Checkpoint headroom can dominate optimizer ranking. Measure initial success and include headroom as a prespecified crossover coordinate.
Tuning each method fairly is difficult. Use equal trial counts plus method-specific published defaults and report both estimands.
first_week: Implement one evaluator and resource ledger shared by dense ES, low-rank ES, MeZO, and GRPO on a small open model.
Run identical-checkpoint one-update probes to measure variance, rank, norm, layer distribution, logit KL, and retention cost.
Define scored-token, wall-clock, memory, and charged-HPO budgets and verify that failed trials remain in every ledger.
Build one verifier-scored task and one controlled noisy-reward task with disjoint validation and final evaluation sets.
Preregister development sizes, unseen model and task, crossover features, Pareto regret tolerance, and claim blockers.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work establishes massively parallel antithetic ES with fitness shaping. The proposal tests its modern LLM regime under complete resource and retention accounting.

competitive_landscape.title: Simple random search provides a competitive approach to reinforcement learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Augmented Random Search demonstrates competitive policy search with normalization and many rollouts. It motivates a simple-search control rather than assuming LLM-specific ES machinery is required.

competitive_landscape.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
competitive_landscape.difference: MeZO treats fine-tuning as an inference-like two-point workload. It is a direct alternative when peak memory, rather than query count, is binding.

competitive_landscape.title: Low-Rank Curvature for Zeroth-Order Optimization in LLM Fine-Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: LOREN chooses informative low-rank directions instead of isotropic populations. The phase diagram tests whether this changes the effective-dimension crossover.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolutionary Strategies lead to Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs
