competitive_landscape.difference: This follow-on finds dense larger-norm ES updates and substantial forgetting relative to GRPO. Retention is therefore co-primary rather than an optional diagnostic.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Thickets: Diverse Task Experts Are Dense Around Pretrained Weights
competitive_landscape.difference: Local expert density offers a mechanistic reason random search can work. The proposal tests whether measured effective geometry predicts resource crossover.

competitive_landscape.title: Matching Accuracy, Different Geometry: Evolution Strategies vs GRPO in LLM Post-Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Similar accuracy can hide different parameter updates. Identical-checkpoint geometry and retention measures become explanatory coordinates in the crossover model.

competitive_landscape.title: LLM Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning is an Inference Workload
competitive_landscape.difference: This work measures zeroth-order fine-tuning as an end-to-end inference workload. The proposal adopts its systems standard rather than relying on linear-layer microbenchmarks.

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming Forgetting in LLM Fine-Tuning with Evolution Strategies
competitive_landscape.difference: Anchored weight decay distinguishes recoverable drift from irreversible forgetting. The proposed ablation tests whether the ES frontier survives this correction.

competitive_landscape.title: Hyper-ES: Effective Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning via Descent Direction Merging
competitive_landscape.difference: Direction merging adds optimizer structure beyond isotropic ES. It sets a stronger search baseline if compute permits.

competitive_landscape.title: Zeroth-Order Stochastic Variance Reduction for Nonconvex Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: ZO-SVRG uses explicit snapshot control variates with analyzed bias and query cost. It is a correctness baseline for claimed snapshot-free variance reduction.

competitive_landscape.title: Minibatch Stochastic Three Points Method for Unconstrained Smooth Minimization
competitive_landscape.difference: MiSTP supplies established stochastic direct-search rates. The proposal treats theorem fidelity and actual estimator implementation as an audit dimension, not evidence of practical crossover by itself.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference over a 24-paper recorded evidence base—three directly supporting hash-pinned, page-anchored readings plus 21 unique primary competitors: scalable ES, random search, low-rank populations, memory-efficient and curvature-aware zeroth order, structured ES, variance-reduced direct search, retention failures and corrections, update-geometry comparisons, and end-to-end inference-workload studies are established. The defensible contribution is not an optimizer; it is a prospectively frozen, multi-resource phase diagram that predicts a Pareto set and per-preference crossover on an untouched scale and task while treating retention and exploitability as co-primary gates.
brief.evidence_note: Supported directly by three current full-text readings on scalable ES, hyperscale low-rank ES, and stochastic random search. arxiv:2511.03187 (Periodic Skill Discovery) was removed because its curriculum and intrinsic-signal lessons do not directly support a frozen-environment optimizer crossover. The broader primary-source panel covers memory-efficient and curvature-aware zeroth order, retention, update geometry, and resource accounting.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.
A compact simulator corpus and small checkpointed model can test the law, but credible held-out backbone and scale tests require substantial sampling compute.
Final physical validity, rank correlation, copying, diversity, calibration, and reward hacking are measurable with independent simulator and blinded-human outcomes.
Internal physics probes, world-model rewards, verifier-guided search, and evolutionary sampling already exist; novelty rests on a prospective cross-backbone reliability law and abstention rule.
A reduced study can quickly test whether maturity features predict later rank correlation, while the decisive scale and generator holdouts take longer.

assumptions: A simulator can provide physical ground truth that is independent of the learned verifier.
Moment-matched synthetic controls preserve low-order image statistics without preserving the target dynamics.
Training checkpoints, reverse-sampler states, and final samples can be retained under one fixed evaluation protocol.
The reliability law is frozen before testing a held-out generator family and larger scale.

brief.title: Causal maturity maps for trustworthy diffusion search
brief.thesis: Predict when an intermediate diffusion signal is mature enough to guide search. Combine signal remaining after a covariance-matched null, maturity across training checkpoints, and reverse-trajectory distribution shift into a preregistered reliability law. Let a calibrated lower confidence bound decide when evolutionary pruning, mutation, or gradients may act—and when they must abstain.
brief.motivation: A feature can decode physics, source identity, or future quality without remaining reliable on reverse-sampler states or under optimization pressure. Diffusion models learn low-order statistics early, can favor training examples without copying along ordinary trajectories, and expose early physics signals that already support pruning and guidance. Existing work therefore establishes both the opportunity and the confounds. The missing test is whether cheap measurements predict future verifier reliability across unseen dynamics, generators, and scale before search is allowed to optimize the signal.
brief.research_question: Can covariance-residual signal, training maturity, and sampler-state shift prospectively predict when an intermediate diffusion verifier will rank final generations reliably without inducing reward hacking?
non_claims: Decodability from a diffusion hidden state does not establish causal usefulness for generation.
Evolutionary search, verifier-guided pruning, and physics rewards are not new by themselves.
High validation AUC on forward-noised clips does not establish reliability on reverse-sampler states.
A gain under the optimized verifier is not a gain unless independent simulator or human outcomes agree.
subquestions: Does signal beyond a Wiener or moment-matched clone null predict final rank correlation better than raw probe AUC?
Does a maturity curve across checkpoints transfer across physical laws, backbones, resolution, and model scale?
Can an abstaining lower-confidence-bound gate retain search gains while reducing copying, off-support drift, and adversarial verifier gains?
method: Generate controlled simulator videos and mean-and-covariance-matched clones with higher-order dynamics deliberately broken.

Train and checkpoint a compact video diffusion model; at each checkpoint, noise level, and layer measure raw probe AUC, covariance-residual AUC, within- and cross-source transfer, and minimal-pair intervention accuracy.
Measure the shift from forward-noised training clips to reverse-sampler states and connect each intermediate score to final-video rank correlation under independent physical truth.
Fit the reliability law on selected laws and one generator, freeze it, then test held-out laws, backbone, resolution, and larger scale.
Use its calibrated lower confidence bound to gate compute-matched population selection, mutation, and optional clipped reward gradients.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: The reliability law may be described as cross-scale only within the registered physical laws, generator families, resolution range, and backbone family. A small checkpoint grid alone is screening evidence.
prospective_design: Fit the complete maturity-and-shift law, confidence rule, abstention threshold, and search policy using only the development laws and backbone.
Freeze them before opening the held-out generator family, resolution, and larger backbone or parameter scale.
Report every held-out candidate and abstention without target-scale refitting or post hoc feature selection.
supporting_evidence: Improved held-out rank-correlation prediction and calibrated confidence coverage over raw verifier AUC
Equal-FLOP physical-validity gain on independent simulator truth at the untouched scale
No material increase in copying, off-support drift, or verifier-to-truth gap
claim_blockers: The frozen rank or calibration advantage reverses on the held-out backbone, resolution, or scale
Target-scale tuning, feature selection, or threshold changes are required
Verifier improvement does not survive independent simulator or blinded-human outcomes
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'the frozen reliability law transferred within the tested laws, backbones, resolutions, and scale interval.' Do not claim universal diffusion-verifier maturity.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A frozen maturity-and-shift reliability law will predict held-out final-quality rank correlation better than raw verifier AUC and will make confidence-gated search outperform random pruning and compute-matched Best-of-N on independent physical truth.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: Abstention will reduce verifier-only gains, copying, and off-support drift compared with optimizing the same intermediate verifier without a trust gate.
experiment.primary_outcome: Held-out rank correlation between intermediate scores and final simulator truth, followed by the equal-FLOP physical-validity gain of confidence-gated search over Best-of-N, with copying and verifier-to-truth gap as hard gates.
domains: Simulator-generated object interactions with controllable gravity, collisions, support, and permanence laws
Moment-matched clone datasets that preserve mean and covariance while breaking higher-order temporal dynamics
A held-out video diffusion backbone, resolution, and larger scale reserved for prospective evaluation
baselines: One-seed generation and uniform random pruning
Compute-matched Best-of-N using the final verifier
Raw internal-verifier pruning without calibration or abstention
EvoSearch-style selection and mutation using the same reward and FLOPs
Video-T1-style verifier-guided branch search
External latent-world-model reward and ungated reward-gradient guidance
ablations: Remove the covariance or Wiener null residual
Remove checkpoint maturity features
Remove forward-to-reverse sampler shift features
Replace the lower confidence bound with the mean prediction
Remove mutation or remove gradient guidance
Train and test the reliability law on the same physical laws or backbone
experiment.decision_rule: The primary claim passes only if the frozen law improves held-out rank-correlation prediction over raw AUC and confidence-gated search beats random pruning and equal-FLOP Best-of-N on simulator truth, without a preregistered increase in copying or verifier-to-truth gap. A verifier-only win fails.

evaluation: Held-out Spearman and Kendall correlation between intermediate scores and final simulator truth
Calibration error, confidence-bound coverage, abstention rate, and risk-coverage curve
Compute-matched physical-validity gain over Best-of-N, random pruning, and direct verifier optimization
Blinded human preference on ambiguous real-world physics clips
Fidelity, temporal coherence, diversity, nearest-training-sample distance, and source-class leakage
Adversarial verifier gain, verifier-to-truth gap, and off-support reverse-trajectory distance
Wall-clock time, denoiser FLOPs, reward calls, and viable offspring recovered from initially poor populations
risks: The law may only restate probe AUC. Require incremental held-out predictive value after raw AUC, noise, layer, and checkpoint controls.
Moment-matched clones may introduce visible artifacts. Use multiple clone constructions and blinded source-classification controls.
Simulator truth may not transfer to perceptual plausibility. Separate the physical claim from the human-realism claim and report both.
Search can overfit any repeatedly queried evaluator. Keep a never-queried truth set and log the complete adaptive query trace.
Larger generators may change representation geometry enough to break the law. Treat failed cross-scale prediction as a primary negative result, not as a tuning opportunity.
All members of a population may be poor. Include mutation/recovery tests rather than irreversible pruning alone.
first_week: Select two simulator laws and build valid-invalid minimal pairs plus a covariance-matched clone diagnostic.
Reproduce one internal-physics probe at three noise levels on forward-noised and reverse-sampler states.
Measure whether covariance residual and sampler shift predict final rank correlation on a small checkpoint grid.
Implement equal-FLOP random pruning, Best-of-N, and raw-verifier pruning with complete cost logging.
Write the held-out laws, generator, scale, primary metric, confidence gate, and claim blockers before fitting the reliability law.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Generalizability of Diffusion Models Requires Rethinking the Hidden Gaussian Structure
competitive_landscape.difference: This work establishes Gaussian mean-and-covariance structure as an early learned diffusion bias. The proposed study turns it into an explicit null and asks whether residual signal forecasts verifier trustworthiness.

competitive_landscape.title: An Analytical Theory of Spectral Bias in the Learning Dynamics of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work derives inverse-variance ordering of learned covariance modes. The proposed law extends from mode-learning order to prospective reliability of intermediate rewards.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity
competitive_landscape.difference: This work introduces moment-matched distributional simplicity tests. The proposed study operationalizes statistical maturity as a search-gating predictor in diffusion sampling.

competitive_landscape.title: Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle: A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work identifies a medium-noise danger zone from training-shell geometry. The proposed study tests whether sampler-state shift predicts verifier failure and hacking there.

competitive_landscape.title: Biased Generalization in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows held-out loss can improve while samples become training-biased. The proposed evaluation therefore includes copy risk and held-out rank transfer instead of trusting loss or AUC alone.

competitive_landscape.title: LikePhys: Evaluating Intuitive Physics Understanding in Video Diffusion Models via Likelihood Preference
competitive_landscape.difference: LikePhys provides a training-free likelihood evaluator. It is a direct baseline against learned internal-feature rewards and their calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: The Invisible Hand of Physics: When Video Diffusion Models Know More Than They Show
competitive_landscape.difference: This work decodes physics from inverted diffusion trajectories but does not use the signal for generation. The proposed study asks when such decodability is causally reliable for search.

competitive_landscape.title: Inference-time Physics Alignment of Video Generative Models with Latent World Models
competitive_landscape.difference: WMReward already searches and steers trajectories with an external world-model reward. The proposed contribution is a prospective trust gate spanning internal and external rewards.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Image and Video Generation via Test-Time Evolutionary Search
competitive_landscape.difference: EvoSearch supplies selection and mutation. The proposed study predicts when that search should trust or abstain from a reward rather than claiming evolution itself.

competitive_landscape.title: Video-T1: Test-Time Scaling for Video Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: Video-T1 expands and prunes video branches using verifiers. The proposed law adds covariance residuals, sampler-shift calibration, and falsifiable cross-scale reliability forecasts.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four page-anchored readings and a primary-source competitor review: covariance-based locality, easy-to-hard statistic learning, training-versus-trajectory memorization gaps, internal physics probes, external world-model rewards, verifier-guided branching, and evolutionary test-time sampling already exist. The defensible contribution is not a new probe, reward, or search primitive. It is a preregistered reliability law that prospectively predicts held-out final rank correlation and reward-hacking risk across physical laws, generator families, and scale, then forces search to abstain when its lower confidence bound is unsafe.
brief.evidence_note: This synthesis is supported by four page-anchored collection readings with 38 findings, 107 anchors, and seven checked primary competitors per paper. The reliability law, quantitative thresholds, and cross-scale claim remain hypotheses until the prospective holdouts are run.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

Static and replay gates are cheap, but the decisive within-scale comparison still crosses candidate environments, seeds, learning rates, objectives, optimizers, on-policy reruns, and adversarial audits.

Independent shadow outcomes and matched-update interventions make the work package falsifiable, but the primary estimand, human-escalation comparison, and boundary with the separate cross-scale work package must remain fixed to avoid a compound pass rule.

Environment evolution, regret curricula, synthetic proxies, learnability filters, and hack evaluation already exist; the remaining delta is a within-scale causal-validity module inside the parent program, not an independent environment-generation program.
A typed gridworld prototype can quickly reveal whether replay, optimizer, and checker controls change environment rankings before the parent program attempts cross-scale calibration.

assumptions: Each environment exposes an intended terminal predicate and an independent hidden outcome that candidate generators and policies cannot mutate.
Policy updates can be replayed under matched effective KL or update norm across objectives, optimizers, learning rates, and checkpoints.
The registered development policy scale can support multiple objectives, optimizers, checkpoints, seeds, and sealed checkers without train-test contamination.
Human review cost and escalation decisions can be logged, blinded, and compared under a fixed audit budget.

brief.title: Within-scale causal validity for evolved RL environments
brief.thesis: This work package supplies the parent program's within-scale causal-validity stage; it is not an independently ranked environment-generation program. A candidate survives only when its hidden-outcome gain persists under trajectory, optimizer, reward/checker, initialization, learning-rate, and checkpoint interventions without widening the reward-hacking gap.
brief.motivation: The four reviewed papers show why a passing verifier and a small-model reward curve are insufficient. Prompt masking and negative-advantage choices change learning under the same verifier and rollouts; divergence effects depend on feasible optimizer geometry; feature rewards can work even when the headline whitening update is explicitly not the gradient of the defined loss; and identical data and objectives overtrain differently across learning rates and checkpoints, while the only direct learning-rate-decay intervention contradicts a simple causal account. These are signals that environment quality and training-pipeline artifacts must be separated experimentally.
brief.research_question: Within a registered policy scale and environment family, can an evolved RL environment be certified as supplying causal learning signal rather than reward leakage, feature collision, optimizer numerics, checkpoint, or effective-step artifacts?
non_claims: This work package is a within-scale validity module of flagship-evo-rl-environments, not an independent ranked research program or a cross-scale certificate.
The project does not claim the first evolutionary environment design, regret curriculum, synthetic proxy environment, learnability filter, cross-agent transfer test, or reward-hacking benchmark.
A reward increase, successful checker call, positive gradient diagnostic, or small-policy gain is not by itself evidence of valid or scalable learning signal.

Arbitrary monotone reward transformations are stress tests, not policy-equivalent controls; positive affine and potential-based transformations are controls only under their stated fixed-horizon, normalization, or policy-invariance assumptions.
Passing the certificate establishes robustness over registered interventions and domains, not universal safety or scale invariance.
Here 'certificate' means a registered empirical evidence packet. It is not a formal proof except for properties separately guaranteed by exact verifiers.
subquestions: Which cheap static, fixed-trajectory, or gradient measurements predict held-out improvement in an inaccessible shadow outcome after on-policy training?
Do environment rankings survive matched-effective-update optimizer, reward/checker, learning-rate, initialization, and checkpoint interventions?
Which validity rankings survive held-out objectives, optimizers, checkpoints, and policy families at the registered scale, and which failures should block promotion to cross-scale testing?
Can active human escalation find semantic failures more efficiently than no review, uniform review, or full review under equal cost?
method: Represent each candidate in a typed environment DSL containing transitions, observations and actions, the intended terminal predicate, observable reward or checker, a logged development shadow outcome, reference solver, invariants, seeds, trajectory provenance, and contamination canaries. The generator may mutate the environment but can access neither the independently implemented confirmation outcome nor the independently authored confirmation exploit suites.

Use MAP-Elites or NSGA-II to retain diverse lineages by robust hidden-outcome gain, optimizer and reward/checker invariance, exploit resistance, behavioral coverage, novelty, compute, and human-audit cost; compare this certificate fitness directly with reward, regret, and learnability fitness.
Gate 0 runs type, determinism, oracle-solvability, leakage, termination, invariant, independent checker-agreement, and semantics-preserving isomorphic perturbation tests before any policy training.

Gate 1 replays fixed trajectories through conditional GRPO, prompt-masked positive and negative variants, unregularized updates, and DPPO versus DRPO at equal feasible divergence limits. Match effective KL or update norm and measure gradient signal-to-noise, cross-objective alignment, and predicted held-out outcome change.

Gate 2 runs pilot-powered small-policy training across three learning rates, replay versus on-policy collection, and two checkpoints. Use frozen-policy repeated rollouts with coupled random seeds, and decompose no-update rollout drift from update-induced improvement before calling the difference learning. Small models screen candidates but never support a scale claim.

Gate 3 requires independent shadow success across optimizers and registered reward/checker controls: state and action renaming, independent checker implementations, fixed-horizon positive affine transformations with normalized optimization, and potential-based shaping under standard policy-invariance assumptions. Arbitrary monotone transforms remain adversarial stress tests only.

Gate 4 freezes the accepted candidate set, short and delayed-retention horizons, within-scale effect estimates, lineage, template, normalized-AST, and semantic-family splits, exploit thresholds, and all evaluator versions before handing them to the parent program's prospective cross-scale calibration work package. No Gate 4 result is itself a scale claim.

Keep a mutable but fully logged development verifier and development exploit suite on discovery data only. Confirmation uses an independently implemented immutable evaluator plus independently authored natural and planted exploit suites that the generator, agent, reward code, and development team cannot query or inspect. Audit implementation overlap, hashes, query budgets, timing, logs, network access, and other side channels before one-time unblinding.

Use humans only where intent is not completely formalizable. Before policy training, run blinded construct and safety review for every new semantic or high-consequence family plus random accepted/rejected sentinels. After selection freezes, run a fresh blind audit and compare no review, uniform review, active equal-budget review, and full review. Human-routing efficacy is secondary; failure selects the safer registered fallback rather than invalidating a passing causal certificate.

human_in_the_loop.answer: Humans are not required for routine execution, replay, exact-checker, update-matching, or statistical gates. They are required for construct validity and for failures whose semantics or exploitability are not completely represented by independent executable tests.
humans_not_needed_for: Static analysis, sandboxing, reset and termination checks, deterministic replay, reference-solver agreement, and invariant tests
Matched-update experiments, seeded policy reruns, confidence intervals, and mechanically specified reward or checker controls
Known exploit canaries and independently executable shadow outcomes with unambiguous semantics
humans_needed_for: Define whether the shadow outcome represents the intended capability rather than a convenient formal proxy
Blindly adjudicate semantic ambiguity, open-ended generated code, evaluator disagreement, and previously unknown exploit strategies
Audit a pilot-powered random sentinel sample of accepted and rejected candidates so confidently shared validator failures remain observable
human_in_the_loop.routing_policy: Run a pre-training construct-and-safety gate and a separate post-selection blind audit. Route every checker disagreement, reward-shadow divergence, new semantic family, high-impact candidate, and known anomaly, plus a preregistered random accepted/rejected sentinel sample powered from pilot prevalence and the desired confidence bound. Compare targeted routing with uniform review and exhaustive expert review on a powered subset under one frozen rubric; fall back to the safer registered policy if the secondary routing test fails.
human_in_the_loop.measurement: Report human minutes, stage, routing reason, inter-rater agreement, adjudication reversals, planted-exploit recall, double-blind natural-failure discoveries, sentinel false-negative intervals, and results for automation-only, targeted, uniform, and exhaustive review. Keep planted canaries and natural failures as separate estimands. Human judgments never become mutable fitness, and routing efficacy is not a core causal-validity gate.

scaling_claim_protocol.answer: This work package validates candidates only within the registered policy scale, family, optimizer, and checkpoint range. It freezes evidence for the parent cross-scale work package but makes no independent scaling claim.
prospective_design: Freeze the candidate set, lineage, template, normalized-AST, and semantic-family splits, immediate and delayed-retention horizons, within-scale effect estimates, evaluator versions, exploit thresholds, and abstentions before any target-scale outcome is opened.
Hand the frozen package to reviewed-scalefalsifier-environments, which alone owns the untouched capacity, interaction-budget, policy-family, optimizer, and lineage holdouts.
Do not retune this certificate from target-scale outcomes; a failed handoff is reported as a scale boundary.
supporting_evidence: Positive compute- and effective-update-matched hidden-outcome gain at the registered scale
Stable intervention signs across the registered objectives, optimizers, learning rates, checkpoints, seeds, and policy families
No material widening of the observable-reward versus shadow-outcome gap under the registered exploit suite
claim_blockers: Any claim that within-scale validity establishes larger-model or universal environment value
Certificate thresholds, candidate selection, or evaluator versions are changed after target-scale results are inspected
The cross-scale work package observes effect-sign, ranking, calibration, or exploit reversals outside the registered range
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'causally valid under the registered within-scale interventions.' Reserve 'predictive across scale' for the parent program only if its untouched cross-scale work package passes.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: Certificate-selected environments will cause larger immediate and delayed held-out shadow-outcome improvement than reward-, regret-, SFL-, TRACED Co-Learnability-, or one-step-learnability-selected environments after matching update size, compute, and lineage diversity.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: A cheap static, replay, and short-policy certificate will preserve candidate rankings across held-out objectives, optimizers, checkpoints, and policy families at the registered scale; exploit tests will be superior for planted-hack recall and noninferior for double-blind natural-failure detection under the frozen audit budget.
experiment.primary_outcome: Two randomized blocked effects on the inaccessible confirmation outcome, each measured immediately and at the prefrozen delayed horizon: absolute learnability versus a resource-matched no-update exposure, and allocation value versus a randomized eligible-pool replacement. Allocation value is primary; intervention-sign stability and the observable-reward versus confirmation-outcome minimum-effect test are hard validity gates.
domains: Deterministic gridworlds and typed tool-use tasks with exact transition and terminal semantics
Verifier-backed language reasoning tasks with controllable prompt masking, response length, and reward leakage
A semantic or computer-use domain whose intended outcome requires blinded human adjudication
baselines: Random procedural generation and hand-authored curricula
Prioritized Level Replay, ACCEL, PAIRED, SFL, and ADD-style regret or learning-potential selection
Learned synthetic environments and reward networks optimized for target-agent return
EnvGen, OMNI-EPIC, and trainer-agent generation with solvability or interestingness filters
Raw observable reward, regret, one-step gain, gradient signal-to-noise, and small-policy return as separate fitness functions
Value disagreement, MBeED/MBeDED, DEGen/MNA, PACE, TRACED Co-Learnability, and All Life is Problem Creation under the same frozen candidate pool and learner budget
Hack-verifiable filtering applied after training rather than inside evolutionary fitness
ablations: Hold trajectories fixed while changing optimizer and objective; then compare fixed replay with on-policy collection.

Compare conditional GRPO, prompt-masked positive and negative advantage updates, unregularized training, and DPPO versus DRPO at equal feasible divergence limits, defaults, and matched effective KL or update norm.
Apply state and action renaming, independent checker reimplementation, valid positive affine and potential-based reward controls, plus explicitly non-equivalent monotone stress transforms.
Cross prompt present versus masked, positive versus negative advantage, and response-length-matched data.
Cross clean solver/SFT/distillation traces with preregistered low-rate planted-hack contamination, then test exploit recurrence after RL, after mitigation, and on a held-out environment family.
Cross three learning rates, two checkpoints, multiple initializations, scalar verifier reward, energy-based feature reward, and feature-reward ensembles.
Remove the shadow evaluator; compare reward, regret, SFL, one-step learnability, and full certificate fitness under random, PLR, ACCEL, and LLM generation.

Within the registered scale, cross held-out policy family and optimizer while comparing no review, uniform review, active equal-budget review, and exhaustive review with sentinel sample sizes powered from the pilot.
Replace the randomized blocked add-one estimand with a post hoc Shapley approximation; report this only as an exploratory interaction analysis.
Use uncoupled rollout seeds or one rollout per frozen policy instead of the no-update versus update aleatoric decomposition.
Reuse the mutable development verifier for confirmation or expose evaluator implementation, hashes, query counts, timing, logs, or network side channels.
Measure only immediate gain and omit the prefrozen delayed-retention outcome.
experiment.selection_protocol: Freeze one deduplicated union candidate pool and blocked curriculum assignments before comparing selectors; group splits by lineage, template, normalized AST, and semantic family. Run each native generator pipeline separately as an end-to-end baseline. Randomize eligible replacements within family, difficulty, and resource blocks and state the positivity population. Permit only the logged development verifier and development exploit suite during discovery; the independent confirmation evaluator and natural plus planted confirmation exploit suites are immutable, inaccessible, side-channel audited, and opened once after every candidate, estimand, horizon, threshold, and rubric freezes.
experiment.resource_scalarization: Declare the primary constraint as learner environment interactions plus a matched effective-update bound. Publish the full Pareto vector of learner FLOPs, generator tokens, verifier calls, wall time, and human minutes; any pilot-derived scalar exchange rate is frozen and secondary.
experiment.analysis: Treat blocked curriculum runs as the inferential unit and cluster intervals by generator lineage and environment family. Estimate allocation value and absolute learnability separately; use coupled seeds and frozen-policy repeated rollouts to estimate aleatoric variance, then contrast no-update with update arms. Apply ordered familywise control: simultaneous one-sided max-t intervals against all preregistered selector baselines first, then immediate allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, optimizer/objective invariance, held-out-family robustness, and exploit resistance. Randomized add-one effects are primary and Co-Learnability and budgeted Shapley estimates are predictors or exploratory interaction summaries. Exploit analyses state opportunity unit, denominator, severity, and hierarchical interval and test reward-up plus hidden-outcome-down jointly.
experiment.claim_hierarchy: Gate the claim through executable validity, causal immediate gain, delayed retention, optimizer and objective invariance, held-out policy-family robustness, then exploit resistance. Scope every conclusion to the registered domain and semantic families; failure of a later gate cannot be compensated by a large earlier reward gain.
experiment.decision_rule: Accept the within-scale validity claim only if simultaneous intervals show allocation value beats every preregistered selector baseline at matched compute and effective update, absolute-learnability and immediate and delayed allocation lower bounds clear their registered margins, intervention signs remain stable, and the joint reward-up/hidden-down test excludes the harmful minimum effect. Target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, confirmation-evaluator or confirmation-exploit-suite changes, familywise error failure, or side-channel access are immediate blockers. Test planted-exploit superiority and natural-failure noninferiority separately; a failed human-routing subclaim selects the safer review fallback and does not erase an otherwise valid automated certificate.

evaluation: Held-out shadow-outcome improvement, sample efficiency, compute-normalized area under the learning curve, and lower confidence bounds across seeds at the registered policy scale
Observable reward minus hidden-outcome exploit gap, independent-checker agreement, hack discovery rate, time to exploit, and post-mitigation recurrence

Environment rank correlation, top-k precision, calibration, effect-sign stability, and intervention ordering across optimizers, objectives, learning rates, checkpoints, and held-out policy families within the registered scale
Gradient signal-to-noise, cross-objective alignment, effective KL, update norm, predicted versus realized hidden-outcome change, and fixed-replay versus on-policy discrepancy
Behavioral coverage, lineage novelty, solvability, transfer to held-out policies and algorithms, and diversity at fixed generation and training cost
Human minutes, escalation precision and recall, failure severity, inter-rater agreement, and discoveries per fixed audit budget

Adversarial canary suite covering checker side effects, answer leakage, premature termination, formatting shortcuts, state aliasing, feature-reward collisions, held-out generator code and seeds, planted hack-verifiable opportunities, semantics-preserving isomorphic state or action perturbations, controlled hacked-trajectory contamination, post-RL recurrence, and cross-domain persistence
risks: The search may optimize the certificate itself. Keep shadow evaluators, held-out generators, canary exploits, and some checker implementations sealed; rotate only according to a preregistered schedule.
Matching nominal optimizer settings can preserve a hidden effective-step confound. Match realized KL or update norm, log optimizer state, and report both default and matched interventions.

A feature reward may learn shortcuts or collide under whitening. Compare scalar, feature, and ensemble rewards against independent semantic outcomes and audit the actual implemented gradient rather than the intended loss alone.

Generated solver, SFT, or distillation trajectories can teach hacks that reappear under RL or transfer to another environment. Version every trajectory source, plant contamination canaries, cross clean and controlled contamination arms, and test post-mitigation recurrence on the inaccessible confirmation suites.
A candidate that is valid here may fail at a larger model or interaction budget. Freeze and hand it to the parent cross-scale work package; withhold every scaling claim from this work package.

Formal environments may make human review look unnecessary while semantic tasks reverse the result. State the domain boundary and test active review under equal budget rather than assuming HITL is universally required.

Potential shaping or affine controls may be implemented outside their invariance assumptions. Unit-test horizon, normalization, discounting, and terminal potentials; label arbitrary monotone transforms as stress tests.
Evolution may favor trivial but robust environments. Include competence ceilings, behavioral coverage, novelty, and transfer while preserving the hidden-outcome validity gate as a hard constraint.

Create five injected exploit classes: checker side effects, answer leakage, premature termination, formatting shortcuts, and state aliasing.
Instrument fixed-trajectory conditional GRPO, prompt-masked variants, DPPO, and DRPO with effective-KL, update-norm, gradient-SNR, and alignment logs.
Run random, regret, SFL, one-step-gain, and certificate ranking on 100 candidate environments with three seeds and three learning rates.
Test whether cheap rankings predict short on-policy shadow-outcome gain and whether optimizer matching changes the top-k set.

Preregister the within-scale decision rule, sealed checks, reward-transform assumptions, human-escalation thresholds, frozen cross-scale handoff, and all claim-blocking falsifiers before evolutionary search.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhanced POET: Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning through Unbounded Invention of Learning Challenges and their Solutions
competitive_landscape.difference: Enhanced POET co-evolves environments and solutions under novelty and transfer, but does not require optimizer-, reward-, checkpoint-, scale-, and hack-invariant learning-signal certificates.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: PAIRED generates curricula through relative regret and zero-shot transfer; the proposed fitness instead requires independent hidden-outcome improvement under causal pipeline interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Prioritized Level Replay
competitive_landscape.difference: PLR prioritizes replayed levels by estimated learning potential but neither synthesizes the environment semantics nor certifies hidden-objective fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolving Curricula with Regret-Based Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ACCEL evolves replay-buffer levels using regret; the proposed search uses certified independent improvement and exploit resistance as hard selection evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: No Regrets: Investigating and Improving Regret Approximations for Curriculum Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: SFL exposes failures of common regret approximations and selects intermediate-success levels; it is a key comparator, while the certificate tests causal invariance and hidden outcomes.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Environment Design via Regret-Guided Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ADD improves environment generation and diversity with regret-guided diffusion but does not audit whether gains survive optimizer, reward, and reward-hacking interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Synthetic Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Evolution Strategies
competitive_landscape.difference: This work evolves neural proxy environments and already tests some algorithm and hyperparameter transfer, so the proposed novelty is the decomposed validity certificate rather than first cross-setting transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Synthetic Environments and Reward Networks for Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This method co-learns synthetic dynamics and rewards for target return; the certificate instead separates observable reward, hidden outcome, optimizer dependence, and scale robustness.

competitive_landscape.title: EnvGen: Generating and Adapting Environments via LLMs for Training Embodied Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: EnvGen adapts environment configurations to observed weak skills but does not require reward or checker invariance, sealed hidden outcomes, or adversarial hacking tests.

competitive_landscape.title: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
competitive_landscape.difference: OMNI-EPIC generates learnable and interesting environment and reward code; the proposed work adds a causal evidence gate and independent exploit audit before selection.

competitive_landscape.title: From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: A trainer model edits configurations from policy failure summaries; the proposed certificate tests whether resulting gains persist across optimizer, reward, checkpoint, and scale interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: CUA-Gym co-generates tasks, states, and rewards and filters them with agents and rollouts; the certificate adds sealed outcome validation and causal training-pipeline invariance.

competitive_landscape.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
competitive_landscape.difference: Hack-verifiable environments make exploits detectable at scale; the proposed work uses exploit resistance inside evolutionary fitness and combines it with optimizer, reward, and scaling interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct negative evidence on reward validity
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows RL can widen the observed-versus-hidden objective gap from 1.5B to 14B parameters, directly motivating the rule that reward improvement cannot certify environment quality.

competitive_landscape.title: Automatic Curriculum Learning through Value Disagreement
competitive_landscape.difference: Value disagreement proposes goals near the policy's reachability frontier using epistemic uncertainty. It is a cheap learner-local selection signal, not an independent causal downstream effect or cross-scale predictor.

competitive_landscape.title: Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: MBeED trains a teacher on the return difference between an updated student and a slightly outdated copy, while MBeDED adds representative-state diversity. That occupies marginal-benefit scoring; the proposed gate instead requires generator-inaccessible confirmation outcomes, causal interventions, and exploit resistance.

competitive_landscape.title: All Life is Problem Creation: Learning to Generate Environments that Maximize Performance Gain
competitive_landscape.difference: The proposer already optimizes measured solver gain on held-out target-task batches. The proposed gate is narrower: freeze candidates before an inaccessible confirmation suite and require robustness across learner, optimizer, reward-checker, and exploit interventions.
competitive_landscape.source_version: SEA @ NeurIPS 2025 Poster; OpenReview record modified 2025-11-19

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Regret Approximation for Unsupervised Dynamic Environment Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: DEGen supplies denser teacher credit and Maximised Negative Advantage improves challenging-level identification. It is a mandatory generator and score baseline, but does not test generator-inaccessible causal transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Fixed Tasks: Unsupervised Environment Design for Task-Level Pairs
competitive_landscape.difference: ATLAS mutates solvable task-level pairs, including reward-machine tasks and MiniGrid levels. It is the relevant generation baseline whenever both task specifications and instances are mutable; the proposed contribution is the downstream validity gate.

competitive_landscape.title: An Optimisation Framework for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: This work supplies a nonconvex-strongly-concave UED formulation, convergence results for a zero-sum setting, and a dynamic-buffer algorithm. The empirical certificate must improve validity evidence beyond this stronger optimization baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
competitive_landscape.difference: Isomorphic Perturbation Testing distinguishes genuine rules from extensional-verifier shortcuts. The proposed gate incorporates this established test family and adds independently sealed outcomes, environment search, and prospective stronger-policy auditing.

competitive_landscape.title: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper separates reward-function from reward-input tampering and formalizes instrumental incentives with causal influence diagrams. The proposed gate operationalizes those channels in generated environments and adds independent hidden outcomes, but does not claim the tampering analysis itself.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
competitive_landscape.difference: This work measures proxy-versus-gold reward divergence across RL and best-of-n optimization, KL, policy and reward-model scale, and reward-model data. It requires the certificate to test optimizer-strength and hidden-outcome interactions rather than report one reward-hacking rate.

competitive_landscape.title: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: TRACED estimates cross-task Co-Learnability from subsequent difficulty changes and combines it with transition-aware regret. Its one-step shadow correlations are mild and its long-horizon runs oscillate, so the proposed work tests it against randomized add-one effects and delayed retention instead of treating it as causal attribution.

competitive_landscape.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
competitive_landscape.difference: Countdown-Code shows that hacked SFT traces can induce reward hacking that reappears under RL and transfers beyond the contaminated task. The certificate must therefore test trace provenance, controlled contamination, recurrence, and cross-domain persistence rather than only policy-time exploit search.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four page-anchored readings, a 25-record direct comparison, and the canonical-union 85-record field audit: environment co-evolution, heterogeneous executable generation, regret and Co-Learnability curricula, learning-potential replay, learned proxies, marginal-benefit and target-performance-gain scoring, verifier perturbations, learned-exploit contamination, causal reward-tampering analysis, and optimizer-dependent proxy overoptimization are established. This work package contributes only the parent program's within-scale causal-validity gate: separate randomized absolute-learnability and allocation-value effects on an immutable confirmation outcome, no-update versus update separation under coupled rollouts, matched-effective-update interventions, prefrozen delayed retention, and independent confirmation tamper-surface tests.
brief.evidence_note: This synthesis uses four page-anchored collection readings with 50 findings. They support optimizer-, objective-, reward-, and checkpoint-confound interventions; they are methodological and negative-control evidence rather than direct demonstrations of environment certification. Their per-reading landscapes contain 35 checked primary entries, 34 unique; the 25-record direct brief landscape additionally incorporates the canonical-union 85-record field audit at data/reviewed/audits/evo.json, checked through 2026-08-24.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

The identifiable design requires a separate 1,152-cell pilot and 1,140 learner cells for each of exactly eight promoted candidates, or 9,120 main cells before native baseline pipelines. Vectorization helps, but the untouched target contrasts, five coupled seeds, and stratified random promotions cannot be reduced after unblinding.

Causal transfer uplift, ranking, interval calibration, and exploit gates are explicit, but the work package must preserve one primary target-tier utility and avoid turning many rank thresholds into interchangeable pass criteria.

Environment generation, learnability scoring, adaptive replay, and model-size studies are established. The remaining delta is the parent program's prospective cross-agent calibration module with family, optimizer, lineage, and untouched-target holdouts, not an independent generator or research program.

A reduced vectorized MiniGrid or Craftax study can quickly falsify whether multi-agent proxy rankings beat a single small learner. Establishing target-scale calibration and cross-family transfer requires a longer confirmatory phase.

assumptions: At least one procedural domain supports immutable environment snapshots, exact replay, independent validity tests, and lineage-level train-test splitting.
Agent capacity, interaction budget, architecture family, and optimizer can be varied independently enough to expose ranking reversals rather than only aggregate compute effects.
A neutral evaluation suite can remain sealed from environment generation and selection so marginal transfer is not optimized on the test outcome.
Vectorized execution can support the fixed five-seed, eight-candidate, 9,120-cell main design after the 1,152-cell pilot; otherwise the target remains unopened and no scale claim is made.
A scaling claim is made only after a frozen predictor and candidate ranking are tested on a preregistered unseen target fidelity.

brief.title: Prospective cross-scale calibration for evolved RL environments
brief.thesis: This work package supplies the parent program's prospective cross-scale calibration stage; it is not an independently ranked environment-generation program. Freeze candidates and within-scale validity evidence before estimating capacity-by-experience response surfaces, then test ranking, causal transfer, calibration, and exploit resistance on untouched scale, architecture, optimizer, policy-family, lineage, and deployment-shift cells.
brief.motivation: An environment can compile, be solvable, resist known reward exploits, and still provide no useful learning signal. It can also improve a weak agent only because that learner discovers a shortcut whose value disappears or reverses for a larger model, different optimizer, or different architecture. Existing work already supplies strong generation and scoring mechanisms: POET evolves paired challenges and solutions; PAIRED, ACCEL, DEGen/MNA, and a dynamic-buffer UED framework optimize regret-like objectives; PLR uses temporal-difference error; value disagreement targets a reachability frontier; CENIE adds novelty; ReMiDi repairs regret stagnation; PACE measures local parameter change; MBeED/MBeDED measures updated-versus-outdated student benefit; and All Life is Problem Creation directly optimizes target-task performance gain. Realized learning benefit and held-out-task gain are therefore occupied objectives. The missing measurement layer is prospective evidence that a predictor and candidate ranking frozen before an inaccessible target fidelity generalize to causal, neutral-suite transfer for stronger and structurally different agents. Four full readings sharpen this boundary: data-mixture scaling separates capacity competition from finite exposure but validates only narrow in-family extrapolation; the proposed zeta law warns that spectral diagnostics remain hypotheses until empirically calibrated; Nexus shows equal proxy loss can conceal different transferable solutions; and learned transformer nonlinearities show task-specific inductive bias while their own 91M-162M depth-only transfer illustrates an inadequate scale test.
brief.research_question: Can a preregistered multi-fidelity validator use small-agent experiments to select evolved RL environments whose causal learning value, ordering, and exploit resistance survive larger interaction budgets and held-out agent families?
non_claims: This work package is the cross-scale calibration module of flagship-evo-rl-environments, not an independent ranked research program or a new environment generator.
The project does not claim a new environment generator, curriculum objective, or universal scalar measure of learning potential.

Mechanical validity, solvability, novelty, regret, temporal-difference error, parameter-update norm, and positive training return are screening signals rather than evidence that an environment transfers or scales.
A curve fit to scales that were also used for model selection is not prospective scaling validation.
Spectral decay, effective rank, gradient agreement, or representation change will be treated as ablatable predictors, never as standalone certificates.
Any successful scaling statement is limited to the tested environment, algorithm, architecture, optimizer, and compute range.
subquestions: Does aggregating several small learner families predict target-scale environment value better than using the strongest single small learner?

Which cheap signals add predictive value beyond complete short learning curves: regret, temporal-difference error, PACE-style update norm, CENIE-style novelty, behavior coverage, gradient agreement, or covariance spectra?
When do environment rankings change because agents move from exploration-limited to representation-, optimization-, or exploit-limited regimes?
Can a partial-pooling response surface identify likely sign reversals early enough to save target-scale compute without discarding rare scalable environments?
When do individually valuable environments become redundant or complementary in a curriculum batch, and can the frozen model predict both effects?
How much human review is needed when transition semantics are formal, and when does construct validity require domain experts despite complete executable checks?

what_counts_as_learning_signal.answer: An environment supplies useful learning signal only when adding it to a training curriculum improves an inaccessible generator-independent confirmation outcome. Estimate absolute learnability against a resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation value against a randomized eligible-pool replacement separately. Local progress is informative only insofar as it prospectively predicts those intervention effects.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Executable validity
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Transition and reward invariants, deterministic replay where required, reset independence, resource limits, solver agreement, reachability, and anti-exploit property tests pass.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: That gradient training can learn the behavior or that the behavior transfers.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Local learnability
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: A powered, multi-seed learner panel improves learning-curve area over no-update, shuffled-reward, and matched-random controls.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: Neutral-task value, cross-agent generality, or scale.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Causal utility
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Base curriculum plus candidate improves the inaccessible confirmation suite over both resource-matched no-update exposure and a randomized eligible-pool replacement, with uncertainty on the separately named effects.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: That the effect persists across policy families or target fidelity.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Cross-agent utility
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Effect direction and candidate rank remain useful across fresh seeds, at least two optimizers, and structurally different policy families.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: Prospective extrapolation to an untouched target scale.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Prospectively scalable utility
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: A frozen response model predicts candidate effects and ranks on a preregistered largest-capacity and largest-budget holdout within calibration, reversal, and exploit tolerances.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: Universal scaling beyond the tested range.

recommended_statistics: Causal neutral-suite learning-curve uplift under equal interactions and compute
Kendall tau-b and Spearman correlation between predicted and observed target effects
Pairwise selection accuracy, top-20-percent overlap, and selection regret
Fraction of environment effects whose sign reverses across target fidelity or agent family
Coverage and sharpness of frozen target prediction intervals
Environment, environment-by-family, and environment-by-optimizer variance components

method: Generate candidate environments with uniform domain randomization, PLR-style curation, PAIRED or ACCEL, DEGen/MNA, MBeED/MBeDED or performance-gain proposals, and at least one evolutionary mutation-and-archive method. Include ATLAS when task specifications and levels are both mutable. Save immutable environment snapshots, generator configuration, solver traces, evaluator version, and full mutation ancestry.

Before the main study, run a fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main candidate union: two capacities by two interaction budgets by three policy/algorithm families by two optimizers by one inference budget by two tool regimes by three coupled seeds. Freeze the minimum useful allocation effect, max-t procedure, five-seed variance model, absolute GPU-hour ceiling, and baseline costs from that pilot. Proceed only if it provides at least 80 percent power for the registered allocation effect and the ceiling covers the complete main design.

Build one deduplicated union candidate pool for every selector comparison, then partition by mutation lineage, prompt or level template, normalized program AST, and semantic capability family into discovery, calibration, and untouched confirmation sets. Discovery objectives may query only a mutable logged development outcome and development exploit suite; the independently implemented immutable confirmation evaluator, independently authored natural and planted confirmation exploit suites, target policy family, target optimizer, and target fidelity remain inaccessible until the predictor and candidate set are frozen. Merely resampling target-task instances does not satisfy this separation. Native generator pipelines are evaluated separately as end-to-end systems.

Apply executable-validity gates before learning experiments: transition and reward invariants, deterministic replay where appropriate, reset independence, solver reachability, hidden-evaluator agreement, resource bounds, metamorphic tests, and adversarial exploit probes.

For each promoted candidate, run 1,080 discovery/calibration cells: three smaller policy capacities by three interaction budgets by three policy-and-RL-algorithm families by two optimizer families by two inference budgets by two tool-access regimes by five coupled seeds. Capacity, interactions, family, optimizer, inference budget, and tool access are manipulated factors. Optimizer steps, effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs are matched diagnostics, not interchangeable budget levels.

Measure target-tier top-k selection regret as the preregistered primary ranking outcome. Gate it with neutral-suite learning-curve area at immediate and prefrozen delayed-retention horizons. Also record sample efficiency, asymptotic return, OOD return, exploit success, behavior and state-action coverage, gradient agreement, update norms, and covariance spectra. Maintain separate ledgers for generator training, candidate evaluation, solver and reward-model calls, environment interactions, learner FLOPs, generated tokens, optimizer updates, evaluator calls, wall-clock time, and human minutes.

Construct matched pairs of environments with similar small-agent return or learning-curve area but different downstream behavior, explicitly testing the Nexus-style possibility that an equal proxy hides different transferable solutions.

Fit a readable hierarchical response surface with environment and lineage effects, smooth log-capacity and log-budget terms, agent-family, algorithm, inference, tool-access, and optimizer interactions, and calibrated uncertainty. Use blocked randomized add-one effects at the curriculum-run level as primary attribution; compare TRACED Co-Learnability and report budgeted Shapley values only as exploratory interaction summaries. Permit non-monotonicity and compare against smallest-agent rank, mean small-agent rank, isotonic extrapolation, and a simple power law.

Freeze the extrapolator, union candidate pool, selected top and bottom, simple-baseline choices, matched-proxy controls, hyperparameter transfer rule, immediate and delayed horizons, and falsification thresholds before unblinding the target tier.

Run 60 untouched target cells per promoted candidate at the fourth capacity and fourth interaction budget: three contrasts—held-out policy/algorithm family with known optimizer, known family with held-out optimizer, and their joint shift—by two inference budgets by two tool regimes by five coupled seeds. Cross a held-out lineage and deployment shift within these cells. Make a scale claim only if the ordered multiplicity-controlled rank, effect, calibration, neutral-transfer, and independent exploit tests all pass.

core_design.unit_of_search: A frozen environment or curriculum addition with immutable code or parameters, mutation lineage, independent evaluator, validity record, training cost, and causal marginal effect relative to an equal-compute replacement.
core_design.generator: Begin with 128 valid candidates in vectorized MiniGrid or Craftax. Preserve candidates from random generation, PLR, PAIRED or ACCEL, and evolutionary search so prediction is not confounded with a single generator.
fitness: Policy capacity: three smaller log-spaced discovery/calibration tiers plus one untouched larger target tier

Experience: three smaller interaction budgets plus one untouched larger target interaction budget; optimizer steps, realized effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs are matched and logged rather than substituted for interactions
Policy and RL-algorithm family: three crossed discovery/calibration families plus a fourth structurally different held-out target family
Optimizer: two crossed discovery/calibration optimizer families plus a third held-out target optimizer
Inference budget: two frozen levels crossed independently of tool access
Tool access: two frozen regimes crossed independently of inference budget without changing the evaluator
Randomness: five coupled seeds, yielding 1,080 discovery/calibration cells plus 60 untouched target cells, or 1,140 learner cells per promoted candidate before native baseline pipelines
core_design.selection: Estimate the marginal neutral-suite effect with a partially pooled, non-monotone response surface over log capacity and log interaction budget, explicit agent-family, optimizer, and lineage interactions, and calibrated uncertainty. Compare it with simpler ranks and curves, then use the frozen target prediction to nominate top, bottom, and ambiguous candidates while always promoting a stratified random audit subset.
core_design.critical_control: The primary confirmation suite, target family and optimizer contrasts, largest capacity and interaction budget, held-out lineage, template, normalized-AST and semantic groups, and independently authored natural and planted confirmation exploit suites remain unavailable to generation and response-model selection until preregistration is frozen. Audit evaluator and exploit-suite code overlap, hashes, query budgets, timing, logs, network access, and other side channels before one-time unblinding.

human_in_the_loop.short_answer: Humans are not necessary for every formal or procedural environment. They are necessary when usefulness, realism, safety, semantic correctness, or unknown exploitability cannot be completely specified by independent executable tests.
humans_not_needed_for: Static analysis, sandboxing, deterministic replay, reference solvers, property tests, reachability, metamorphic checks, and mechanically specified adversarial-policy tests for routine validity
Target-tier assignment, lineage-safe splitting, response-surface fitting, uncertainty estimation, and resource accounting
Mechanically checkable outcome, solver, and invariant comparisons whose semantics are complete and independently implemented
humans_needed_for: Define whether the neutral evaluation suite represents the desired capability rather than merely a convenient formal objective.
Audit semantic realism, safety, social assumptions, and reward-evaluator mismatches that executable checks do not encode.
Adjudicate suspected exploits and create new counterexamples without feeding target-tier outcomes back into candidate selection.
Review every automated disagreement, evaluator-reward divergence, solver mismatch, new generator family, and preregistered high-impact candidate.

Blindly review a stratified sample of predicted top, bottom, ambiguous, accepted, and rejected environments, including a pilot-powered random sentinel sample, because correlated validators can be confidently wrong.
human_in_the_loop.measurement: Before training, report construct-and-safety review minutes, rubric agreement, and accepted/rejected sentinel reversals for every new semantic or high-consequence family. After selection freezes, report a fresh blind audit with routing reason, planted-exploit recall, double-blind natural-failure discoveries, false-negative intervals, and automation-only, targeted, uniform, and exhaustive-review results. Human judgments establish construct validity and routing efficacy is secondary; neither becomes mutable fitness or replaces the core causal and exploit gates.

scaling_claim_protocol.short_answer: Training one small model and showing a positive trend is screening evidence, not a scaling result. Scaling is supported only when a predictor frozen on the 1,080-cell discovery/calibration lattice succeeds on 60 untouched target cells that separately identify a held-out policy/algorithm family, a held-out optimizer, and their joint shift at a fourth capacity and interaction budget.
prospective_design: Cross three smaller log-spaced capacities with three interaction budgets, three policy/algorithm families, two optimizers, two inference budgets, two tool-access regimes, and five coupled seeds. Keep a fourth capacity and fourth interaction budget fully held out.

Treat interaction count as the manipulated experience axis; match and log optimizer steps, realized effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs so learning speed is not confused with effective update size.
At the target tier run separate held-out-family/known-optimizer, known-family/held-out-optimizer, and joint-shift contrasts so family and optimizer failures are not confounded.
Split by mutation ancestry, prompt or level template, normalized program AST, and semantic family rather than random instances to prevent structural leakage.

Promote exactly eight candidates: two predicted top, one predicted bottom, two ambiguous, and three uniformly sampled from the remaining eligible pool. Carry all eight through every target contrast so selection-induced optimism and false negatives can be estimated.
supporting_evidence: Kendall tau-b and Spearman correlation between predicted and observed target effects
Pairwise decision accuracy with uncertainty for candidate comparisons
Target-tier top-k selection regret as the primary ranking metric; top-20-percent Jaccard overlap is descriptive
Fraction of marginal effects whose confidence intervals reverse beyond the preregistered practical-equivalence margin
Binomial-uncertainty-aware coverage, weighted interval score, and sharpness of nominal 90-percent target prediction intervals
Held-out-family selection regret and conditional ranks rather than a variance-ratio pass rule
claim_blockers: The simultaneous one-sided max-t lower bound for target-tier selection-regret improvement fails the preregistered useful margin against any eligible simple or UED selector.
Predicted top candidates fail to beat random or PLR controls with a positive meaningful immediate and delayed target effect.

A candidate is called a sign reversal without its confidence interval lying beyond the preregistered practical-equivalence margin, or the registered reversal-rate limit is exceeded under that definition.
The completely held-out agent family has unacceptable selection regret; a variance-component ratio alone neither passes nor fails the claim.

Nominal interval undercoverage exceeds the binomial uncertainty tolerance or weighted interval score is worse than the registered baseline. Coverage above 95 percent is reported with sharpness and is not automatically rejected.
The delayed-retention effect misses its registered minimum-effect bound.

Exploit superiority or noninferiority fails under explicitly defined opportunity units, denominators, severity strata, and hierarchical confidence intervals. A simple zero-event one-percent upper-bound claim requires about 300 independent opportunities.
The joint confidence region permits a practically meaningful reward increase together with hidden-outcome degradation.
Any target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, confirmation-evaluator or confirmation-exploit-suite update, or failure to apply the frozen ordered familywise procedure occurs.
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: If successful, state that the validator predicted environment value within the tested domains, policy families, optimizer regimes, and scale interval. Do not say that an environment universally scales.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A cross-agent hierarchical validator trained on smaller fidelities will select environments with higher causal neutral-suite transfer at an untouched target fidelity than the smallest-agent rank, mean small-agent rank, PLR score, regret, novelty, PACE-style update norm, isotonic extrapolation, power-law extrapolation, or random selection.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: A multi-agent proxy panel will reduce target selection regret relative to one small learner; learning-curve shape, behavior coverage, and family interactions will improve calibration beyond regret or update norms; and matched-small-proxy environments will reveal different downstream transfer when learned solutions differ.
domains: Primary pilot: vectorized MiniGrid or Craftax procedural navigation and compositional tasks with exact instance lineage and independent solvers
Confirmation: a distinct partially observed or tool-use environment family with sealed state-based evaluation
baselines: Uniform valid environment generation and domain randomization
Prioritized Level Replay
PAIRED or replay-guided adversarial environment design
ACCEL regret-guided level editing
ReMiDi refined minimax regret
CENIE coverage-based novelty
PACE parameter-change scoring and TRACED Co-Learnability
Value-disagreement frontier scoring
MBeED/MBeDED updated-versus-outdated student benefit
All Life is Problem Creation target-performance-gain proposals
DEGen with Maximised Negative Advantage
Dynamic-buffer UED optimization and ATLAS task-level generation where applicable
Smallest-agent rank and mean rank across small learners
Isotonic and power-law extrapolation
Random top-k selection under the same evaluation budget
ablations: Remove agent-family and optimizer interactions from the response model
Remove lineage-level splitting and show the optimism introduced by random instance splits
Use only final environment return instead of neutral-suite marginal transfer
Remove the stratified full-fidelity audit sample and quantify pruning bias
Remove spectral, gradient, novelty, regret, or parameter-change features one at a time
Force monotonic scaling and compare its reversal and calibration errors with the non-monotone model
Select after viewing the target tier as a deliberately invalid upper-bound analysis
Compare selectors on their native, nonoverlapping candidate pools instead of the frozen union pool
Drop the prefrozen delayed-retention horizon
Reuse the development verifier or development exploit suite for confirmation, or permit evaluator or exploit-suite hash, query, timing, logging, or network side channels
Train on clean versus preregistered low-rate planted-hack solver, SFT, or distillation traces and omit post-RL recurrence or held-out-family persistence tests
experiment.primary_outcome: Target-tier top-k selection regret against the expensive oracle ranking on the frozen union pool. Gate it with separately named absolute learnability versus a resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation value versus a randomized eligible-pool replacement, each measured immediately and at the prefrozen delayed horizon on the inaccessible confirmation outcome.
experiment.selection_protocol: Freeze one deduplicated union candidate pool, the eight-candidate promotion roster, all discovery, calibration, and target groups, the 1,080 discovery/calibration cells and 60 untouched target cells per promoted candidate, horizons, response model, estimands, max-t procedure, and top-k choice before target access. Split by lineage, template, normalized AST, and semantic family. Compare native generator pipelines separately, never as if their different candidate pools were selector evidence. Permit only development outcomes and development exploits before freezing; open the independent confirmation outcome and exploit suites once.
experiment.resource_scalarization: Run the fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main candidate union. Freeze five coupled main seeds, exactly eight different promoted candidates—two top, one bottom, two ambiguous, and three uniformly random—and 1,140 cells per candidate, for 9,120 main learner cells before native baseline pipelines. Freeze an absolute GPU-hour ceiling from the pilot's 95th-percentile cell cost plus registered baseline costs. Proceed only with at least 80 percent power for the minimum useful allocation effect and resources for the full design; otherwise keep confirmation closed and make no scale claim. Disclose environment interactions, learner FLOPs, generator tokens, verifier calls, wall time, GPU-hours, and human minutes and freeze scalar exchange rates.
experiment.analysis: Treat curriculum runs as inferential units, use coupled seeds, and cluster hierarchical intervals by generator lineage and environment family. Randomize eligible replacements within family, difficulty, and resource blocks and state the positivity population; estimate allocation value and absolute learnability separately. Use an ordered familywise procedure: simultaneous one-sided max-t intervals for selection regret against every eligible selector; then allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, held-out-family regret, held-out-optimizer regret, joint-shift regret, interval calibration, and exploit resistance. Tau-b, pairwise accuracy, and Jaccard are diagnostic unless separate pilot-derived utility margins and multiplicity-adjusted thresholds are frozen. Evaluate undercoverage with binomial uncertainty, weighted interval score, and sharpness. Define sign reversal only beyond a practical-equivalence margin. Exploit tests state opportunity units, denominators, severity, and hierarchical intervals, including reward-up/hidden-down joint tests, controlled trajectory contamination, recurrence, and cross-domain persistence.
experiment.claim_hierarchy: Gate claims through no leakage; executable validity; immediate allocation value and absolute learnability; delayed retention; multiplicity-controlled target-tier selection regret; separately identified held-out-family and held-out-optimizer regret; interval calibration; then independent exploit resistance. Any earlier failure blocks later claims. Human-routing efficacy is secondary and selects the registered review policy rather than entering this core hierarchy.
experiment.decision_rule: The scale claim passes only if the simultaneous target-tier selection-regret bounds improve by the registered margin and every core gate passes. Jaccard, tau-b, and pairwise accuracy are diagnostic unless prospectively promoted into the multiplicity family; overcoverage alone is not failure. Invalid-candidate rate is a generator cost unless it contaminates selection. Human-routing failure selects the safer review fallback without erasing a passing scale result.
