Target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, familywise error failure, or confirmation evaluator or exploit-suite updates block the claim immediately.

falsifiers: The fixed pilot fails to provide at least 80 percent power for the registered minimum useful allocation effect with five coupled seeds, or the frozen GPU-hour ceiling cannot fund the complete 9,120-cell main design plus baseline costs; in either case confirmation stays closed.

The simultaneous one-sided max-t lower bound for target-tier top-k selection-regret improvement fails the registered minimum useful margin against any eligible simple or UED selector. Tau-b, pairwise accuracy, and Jaccard remain diagnostic unless separately registered in this multiplicity family.
The preregistered fraction of candidate effects has confidence intervals entirely beyond the practical-equivalence margin in the opposite direction.
Selection regret exceeds its preregistered limit on either the held-out-family/known-optimizer contrast or the known-family/held-out-optimizer contrast; report the joint-shift contrast separately.
Predicted top candidates fail to beat the random or PLR control at target scale: the 95-percent interval includes zero or the standardized gain is below 0.2.
The prefrozen delayed-retention effect misses its registered minimum-effect bound.

Nominal 90-percent target intervals under-cover beyond binomial uncertainty or have worse weighted interval score than the registered baseline; overcoverage is reported with sharpness and is not automatically rejected.

The registered planted-exploit superiority or natural-failure noninferiority test fails under explicit opportunity units, denominators, severity strata, and hierarchical confidence intervals, or controlled hacked-trajectory contamination produces material post-RL recurrence or cross-domain persistence.
The joint minimum-effect confidence region permits reward to improve while the hidden evaluator worsens materially.
Promoted environments show no positive effect on the generator-independent neutral suite.

Any target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, failure to apply the frozen ordered familywise procedure, or update to the immutable confirmation evaluator or confirmation exploit suites occurs. Invalid-candidate rate is otherwise reported as generator cost unless invalid candidates leak into selector fitting or target evaluation.
evaluation: Separate absolute-learnability uplift versus resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation-value uplift versus randomized eligible-pool replacement, immediately and at the delayed horizon
Kendall tau-b, Spearman correlation, pairwise accuracy, top-20-percent Jaccard, selection regret, and sign-reversal rate across fidelities
Prediction-interval coverage, sharpness, calibration error, and target residuals
Held-out agent-family, optimizer, environment-lineage, and deployment-shift performance
Reward-to-hidden-evaluator divergence, adversarial exploit success, solver failure, invariant-test failure, hacked-trajectory contamination response, post-RL recurrence, and cross-domain persistence
Behavior and state-action coverage, learning-curve shape, gradient agreement, update norm, and covariance effective-rank diagnostics
Environment, family-interaction, optimizer-interaction, lineage, and seed variance components
Environment interactions, learner FLOPs, evaluator calls, generated tokens, wall-clock time, and human-review minutes
risks: The response surface may be too flexible for the number of target-confirmed candidates. Predefine a compact hierarchy, compare simple baselines, and reserve an untouched calibration audit.
Successive halving can discard slow-starting but scalable environments. Carry a stratified random sample and candidates chosen for diverse learning-curve shapes to full fidelity.
A neutral suite can leak through generator features or solver design. Separate teams or processes, version and seal the evaluator, and audit indirect access paths.
Environment effects may be strongly curriculum-interactive rather than additive. Include randomized add-one-in experiments and a small batch-selection replication before assigning individual credit.
Agent-family differences can make a universal ranking impossible. Treat this as a scientific result and report conditional rankings rather than averaging away interactions.
Spectral or gradient diagnostics can become post hoc stories. Freeze feature definitions and ablations before the target tier and report when simple ranks perform equally well.

Reward hacking may emerge only at stronger optimization or after solver/SFT/distillation traces teach a shortcut. Run an independently authored target-tier exploit search, controlled contamination arms, post-mitigation recurrence, and cross-domain persistence tests.
Human audits can introduce preference leakage. Blind candidate rank and generator source, use a written rubric, and size random sentinels from the pilot's desired confidence bound.

The design is compute-heavy: the 1,152-cell pilot precedes 9,120 main learner cells across exactly eight promoted candidates before baseline pipelines. Freeze the absolute GPU-hour ceiling from pilot accounting and do not open confirmation unless it funds the entire design; never reduce target, held-out-family, held-out-optimizer, seed, or random-promotion requirements after seeing results.

Existing PACE, CENIE, ReMiDi, Procgen, and UED work may explain most gains. The project remains publishable only if prospective cross-fidelity calibration yields new positive or rigorously negative evidence.
first_week: Define a typed immutable candidate record containing environment hash, generator, lineage, solver, evaluator version, validity results, and compute accounting.
Implement one vectorized procedural domain and reproduce random generation, PLR, and ACCEL or PAIRED under a common interface and interaction budget.
Build independent reachability, replay, reward, termination, reset, resource, metamorphic, and known-exploit tests; reject failures before RL training.

Run the fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main union across two capacities, two interaction budgets, three policy/algorithm families, two optimizers, one inference budget, two tool regimes, and three coupled seeds. Freeze five main seeds, the minimum useful allocation effect, simultaneous max-t method, absolute GPU-hour ceiling, and baseline costs; stop before confirmation if power is below 80 percent or the ceiling cannot fund all 9,120 main cells.
Compute short-horizon return, learning-curve area, regret, temporal-difference error, PACE-style update norm, novelty or coverage, and one covariance-spectrum diagnostic for each valid candidate.
Implement smallest-agent rank, mean small-agent rank, isotonic extrapolation, and the initial hierarchical response model behind one deterministic evaluation API.
Create lineage-level discovery, calibration, and target splits plus a separate deployment-shift split, then freeze their hashes.

Write the preregistration containing primary outcome, target fidelity, agent-family holdout, promoted controls, falsifier thresholds, interval method, stopping rules, human routing, and claim language.

competitive_landscape.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
competitive_landscape.difference: POET co-evolves environments and specialist solutions and transfers stepping stones among them. ScaleFalsifier does not replace that generator; it asks whether cheap environment rankings predict causal value for untouched larger and structurally different agents.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: PAIRED uses protagonist-antagonist regret to produce solvable curricula and zero-shot transfer. ScaleFalsifier treats regret as a competing predictor and tests whether its candidate ordering survives scale, architecture, optimizer, and lineage shifts.

competitive_landscape.title: Prioritized Level Replay
competitive_landscape.difference: PLR prioritizes levels with signals such as temporal-difference error and improves Procgen generalization. It does not prospectively calibrate level-value rankings across learner capacities and families.

competitive_landscape.title: Replay-Guided Adversarial Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: Dual Curriculum Design unifies PLR and PAIRED and adds equilibrium robustness guarantees. ScaleFalsifier evaluates finite-training neutral transfer and target-scale rank calibration rather than optimizing one teacher-student game.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolving Curricula with Regret-Based Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ACCEL edits replayed levels toward the learner's capability frontier using regret. ScaleFalsifier freezes ACCEL outputs and tests whether their estimated value transfers across scale and learner inductive bias.

competitive_landscape.title: Leveraging Procedural Generation to Benchmark Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Procgen establishes held-out procedural generalization and reports that larger models improve sample efficiency and generalization. It does not evolve training environments or test whether candidate-environment rankings are stable across policy families and target fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: Refining Minimax Regret for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ReMiDi shows minimax-regret curricula can stagnate and refines the objective to continue learning. This motivates falsifying environment proxies rather than assuming a theoretically motivated regret score tracks scalable learning value.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Environment Novelty Quantification for Effective Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: CENIE augments regret with coverage-based environment novelty. ScaleFalsifier includes novelty as an ablatable predictor and requires prospective calibration to neutral transfer rather than treating coverage as utility.

competitive_landscape.title: PACE: Parameter Change for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: PACE scores an environment through a first-order approximation to the policy-parameter change it induces, directly targeting realized local learning progress. ScaleFalsifier tests whether that local update signal predicts neutral transfer for larger and structurally different agents.

competitive_landscape.title: DataDecide: How to Predict Best Pretraining Data with Small Experiments
competitive_landscape.difference: DataDecide finds simple rankings from small experiments can be more decision-efficient than elaborate scaling-law fits. ScaleFalsifier therefore treats smallest-agent and mean-rank rules as mandatory baselines for its multi-fidelity model.

competitive_landscape.title: Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws
competitive_landscape.difference: This work decomposes static data-mixture loss into capacity competition and finite-data effects and differentiably selects mixtures. ScaleFalsifier borrows the separation of capacity and exposure but must validate it for adaptive, agent-dependent RL environments and held-out families.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws vs Model Architectures: How does Inductive Bias Influence Scaling?
competitive_landscape.difference: This study finds that the best architecture can fluctuate across scale. ScaleFalsifier turns that warning into whole-family, interaction, and target-scale holdouts for environment rankings.

competitive_landscape.title: Same Pre-training Loss, Better Downstream: Implicit Bias Matters for Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows matched pretraining loss can conceal different downstream performance. ScaleFalsifier includes environments matched on small-agent return or learning-curve area to test whether proxy-equivalent learning signals produce different transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Nexus: Same Pretraining Loss, Better Downstream Generalization via Common Minima
competitive_landscape.difference: Nexus reports that cross-microbatch gradient agreement can change transfer at nearly fixed proxy loss, while its proofs and seed uncertainty limit certification. ScaleFalsifier uses optimizer holdouts and matched-proxy controls rather than assuming one learner reveals environment value.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Transformers Really Do It All? On the Compatibility of Inductive Biases Across Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: This work reports sharply task-specific algorithmic nonlinearities but tests scale only through 91M-162M same-codebase depth transfer and uses task-specific early checkpoints. ScaleFalsifier requires uniform outcomes, cross-family matrices, and a genuinely untouched target fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: Automatic Curriculum Learning through Value Disagreement
competitive_landscape.difference: Value disagreement uses epistemic uncertainty to propose goals near a learner's reachability frontier. ScaleFalsifier tests it as a cheap local predictor and asks whether its ordering survives unseen capacity and policy families.

competitive_landscape.title: Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: MBeED and MBeDED already score environments through updated-versus-outdated student benefit and diversity. ScaleFalsifier treats that realized benefit as a baseline, then freezes predictions before an inaccessible target scale and policy family.

competitive_landscape.title: All Life is Problem Creation: Learning to Generate Environments that Maximize Performance Gain
competitive_landscape.difference: The proposer directly optimizes solver gain on sampled target tasks, occupying performance-gain curriculum generation. ScaleFalsifier instead withholds the target fidelity and family until both the candidate set and cross-fidelity predictor are frozen.
competitive_landscape.source_version: SEA @ NeurIPS 2025 Poster; OpenReview record modified 2025-11-19

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Regret Approximation for Unsupervised Dynamic Environment Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: DEGen and Maximised Negative Advantage improve teacher credit and difficult-level identification. They are strong generation and scoring controls; the proposed work evaluates whether their candidate rankings prospectively transfer across unseen learners and scale.

competitive_landscape.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
competitive_landscape.difference: Isomorphic Perturbation Testing exposes extensional-verifier shortcuts after RLVR. ScaleFalsifier applies such perturbations at every fidelity and blocks scaling claims when stronger policies widen the reward-to-hidden-outcome gap.

competitive_landscape.title: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: This work formalizes capability-dependent incentives to tamper with reward functions and reward inputs. ScaleFalsifier turns those causal channels into stronger-policy confirmation tests but adds candidate ranking and neutral transfer across fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
competitive_landscape.difference: Reward-model overoptimization follows different empirical forms for RL and best-of-n and depends on KL, policy scale, reward-model scale, and data. ScaleFalsifier therefore crosses optimization and inference fidelity and evaluates a hidden outcome instead of assuming one exploit rate transfers.

competitive_landscape.title: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: TRACED adds Co-Learnability to transition-aware regret and reports improved zero-shot generalization, but its one-step temporal correlations are modest and long-horizon runs oscillate. It is a direct predictor baseline, not evidence that candidate rankings survive target fidelity or family shifts.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Small Training Runs Reliably Guide Data Curation? Rethinking Proxy-Model Practice
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows fixed small-run configurations can reverse data-recipe rankings and that data-specific tuning changes the relevant question. ScaleFalsifier must cross optimization fidelity and compare simple frozen ranks before claiming its response model adds predictive value.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after four complete page-anchored readings, a 24-record direct comparison, and the canonical-union 85-record field audit: heterogeneous environment generation, regret, novelty, parameter-change, marginal-benefit, target-performance-gain, Co-Learnability, and small-proxy data-selection are established. Reward tampering, learned-exploit contamination, proxy overoptimization, and architecture-dependent ranking changes make one small learner or one diagnostic untenable. This work package contributes only the parent program's prospective calibration module: freeze the union pool, response model, two causal estimands, resource rule, delayed horizon, and immutable confirmation evaluator and exploit suites before opening 60 target-tier cells that separately test family, optimizer, and joint shifts after the 1,080-cell discovery/calibration lattice.
brief.evidence_note: Supported by four current, hash-pinned full-text readings totaling 143 pages, each with page-anchored author claims, reviewer inference, contradiction audits, and at least eight checked primary competitors. They provide methodological analogies rather than direct demonstrations that evolved environment rankings transfer across scale. The 24-record brief landscape incorporates the canonical-union 85-record field audit at data/reviewed/audits/evo.json, checked through 2026-08-24. The revised 5.7 feasibility reflects the fixed 1,152-cell pilot and 9,120-cell main study required by the identifiable factorization.

factors.rationale: Requires a fresh experimental scaffold derived from public paper specifications.

Environment fitness is a bilevel problem, and the identifiable design now requires 1,080 discovery/calibration learner cells plus 60 untouched target cells per promoted candidate before baseline pipelines. Eight promoted candidates therefore require 9,120 learner cells after a separate 1,152-cell pilot, making the prospective scale test a major compute commitment.
Transfer uplift, acceptance precision, exploit gaps, cross-scale rank stability, and prediction error are measurable if sealed evaluators and matched-compute controls are defined first.

RLVE and SCALER already adapt verifiable environments to the learner; AutoEnv measures heterogeneous cross-environment learning; EnvFactory, GenEnv, RLAnything, Agent-World, and SPADE close parts of the executable agent-environment loop; and Envs-FORGE selects verified rewrites near a learning frontier across 4B-35B models. Novelty therefore depends on prospectively predicting causal marginal transfer and exploit risk at an unseen scale, not generation, adaptation, or multi-size gains alone.
A small benchmark can test whether cheap environment scores predict later transfer, but evidence that the predictor extrapolates across scale will take substantially longer.

assumptions: Start with one code-verifiable domain where success has an evaluator independent of the generated reward.
Treat an environment as a reusable instance generator plus transition system, reward, termination rule, and hidden evaluator, not as a prompt alone.

Use the registered discovery, calibration, and target factors with five coupled seeds; do not proceed to the scale claim unless the pilot gives at least 80 percent power for the registered minimum useful effect.
Treat every small-model result as screening evidence until a preregistered larger-scale holdout is run.

brief.title: Evolve RL environments whose learning value survives stronger optimizers and larger agents
brief.thesis: Build an environment-search benchmark and validator before building a larger generator. Search over executable environment families with quality-diversity, but select them using prospective estimates of marginal transfer, exploit resistance, and cross-scale stability. Keep the hidden evaluator outside the mutable genome. Use human review for semantics and blind spots, not routine execution checks.
brief.motivation: A task can compile, have a reachable goal, resist known exploits, and still add no useful training signal. Conversely, a task can improve a weak agent only because it teaches a shortcut that disappears, reverses, or becomes hackable at higher optimization power. POET, PAIRED, PLR, ACCEL, diffusion UED, and recent executable-environment systems show many ways to generate or curate tasks. AutoEnv already factorizes heterogeneous transition, observation, and reward distributions for cross-environment learning; EnvFactory and GameCWM automate executable tool or game construction; RLVE and SCALER adapt difficulty and active sets; GenEnv, RLAnything, Agent-World, and SPADE couple environment updates to learner feedback; Envs-FORGE uses frontier estimates across four Qwen sizes. MBeED selects realized marginal improvement, while All Life is Problem Creation rewards held-out target-task gain. The remaining problem is narrower: can a predictor frozen before target access forecast compute-matched causal value and exploit resistance for an untouched fidelity and policy family?
brief.research_question: Can a preregistered learning-signal validator select generated RL environments with higher held-out transfer value and lower exploit rates than regret, success-rate, novelty, or single-agent learning progress alone?
non_claims: Generating diverse valid environments is not itself novel.
A positive learning curve on the generated environment does not show useful transfer.
A gain for one small model does not show that the environment, ranking, or training recipe scales.
An automated verifier proves only the property it checks; it does not establish semantic usefulness or absence of unknown exploits.
subquestions: Which environment representation is most search-efficient: parameter vectors, editable levels, executable programs, learned proxy MDPs, reward programs, or generator-verifier packages?
Does marginal transfer uplift belong to an individual environment, or is it mainly an interaction among environments in a curriculum?

Which cheap signals predict later value: success probability near 0.5, learning-curve slope, temporal-difference error, gradient agreement, policy disagreement, regret, representation change, or solve-verify asymmetry?
When do environment rankings preserve sign and order across policy size, architecture, algorithm, training budget, and optimizer strength?
Can selective human review reduce cost without missing systematic validator failures that produce low uncertainty?

generation_routes.mechanism: Sample or adversarially choose free parameters of an underspecified environment.
generation_routes.best_when: The simulator and semantics are fixed and only level structure or dynamics vary.

generation_routes.mechanism: Mutate solved or high-value levels and retain diverse niches.
generation_routes.best_when: Local edits preserve validity and stepping stones matter.

generation_routes.mechanism: Train a policy or diffusion model to emit levels conditioned on regret or learnability.
generation_routes.best_when: The task space is structured but random search rarely reaches useful regions.

generation_routes.mechanism: Generate executable transition code, instance generators, rewards, and verifiers with a code model, then repair and mutate them.
generation_routes.examples: OMNI-EPIC, Endless Terminals, AutoEnv, EnvFactory, GameCWM, SCALER, Agent-World, AWM, ReSyn, EvoEnv, CUA-Gym, Envs-FORGE, and SPADE.
generation_routes.best_when: Broad semantic variation matters and strong sandboxing is available.

generation_routes.mechanism: Meta-optimize a compact neural or contextual-bandit environment against downstream target performance.
generation_routes.examples: Learning Synthetic Environments and Discovering Minimal RL Environments.
generation_routes.best_when: A target task is known and repeated future training can amortize the expensive outer loop.

generation_routes.mechanism: Evolve reward programs while transitions and success conditions stay fixed.
generation_routes.best_when: The task is valid but sparse or poorly shaped feedback blocks learning.

core_design.unit_of_search: An environment family has separately typed task specification, instance generator, transition system, observation and action schemas, reward, termination, reference solver, visible tests, capability tags, trajectory provenance, and contamination canaries. Discovery may use a logged development outcome and exploit suite; an independently implemented confirmation evaluator and independently authored natural and planted confirmation exploit suites remain immutable and inaccessible to the generator, policy, reward code, and outer loop until one-time opening.
core_design.generator: Begin with typed mutations over a constrained DSL. Add LLM program mutations only after the validator works. Store lineage and every evaluator interaction so adaptive overfitting can be measured. Maintain niches by required capability, horizon, observability, interaction structure, and verifier mechanism.
fitness: Mechanical validity: API determinism where expected, reset independence, invariant and metamorphic tests, resource limits, reachability, and reference-solver agreement.
Calibrated learnability: success is neither saturated nor uniformly impossible; estimate posterior learning progress across seeds rather than using one rollout or a raw success-rate heuristic.
Causal marginal value: base curriculum plus candidate beats base curriculum plus a compute- and token-matched control on sealed downstream tasks.
Cross-policy value: the transfer effect is not confined to the generator's solver, one RL algorithm, or one architecture family.

Exploit resistance: proxy reward tracks an evaluator unavailable to the agent and generator as optimization power rises; adversarial policies and counterfactual state/action interventions do not expose shortcuts.
Diversity with utility: archive distance uses behavior, causal mechanism, and capability requirements, not source-code or prompt-token novelty alone.
Efficiency: useful transfer per environment step, generated token, GPU-hour, and human-review minute.
core_design.selection: Use constrained Pareto or MAP-Elites selection. Mechanical validity and evaluator isolation are hard constraints. Optimize calibrated learnability, marginal transfer, exploit gap, diversity, and cost without collapsing them into one noisy score.
core_design.critical_control: Because environments interact, make randomized add-one-in effects within blocked curriculum runs the primary attribution design. Treat the curriculum run, not an environment rollout, as the inferential unit; cluster uncertainty by generator lineage and environment family. Report budgeted Shapley estimates only as exploratory interaction diagnostics, and compare directly with TRACED Co-Learnability.

what_counts_as_learning_signal.answer: Learning signal is an intervention effect, not a property inferred from task validity. Estimate two distinct quantities: absolute learnability against a resource-matched no-update exposure, and allocation value against a randomized eligible-pool replacement. Discovery may use a logged development shadow outcome; only the independently implemented confirmation outcome is sealed and inaccessible until every candidate, model, threshold, and estimand is frozen.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Operational
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: The environment executes, resets, terminates, and its reference solver and property tests agree.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: That an agent can learn or that the task matters.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Behavioral
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Random, scripted, known-good, known-bad, and exploit-seeking policies receive the expected ordering under both reward and hidden evaluation.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: That gradient-based training can acquire the behavior.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Learnable
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: A powered multi-seed study shows a positive learning effect against no-update and shuffled-reward controls.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Causally useful
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Adding the environment improves the inaccessible confirmation outcome over both a resource-matched no-update exposure and a randomized eligible-pool replacement curriculum, with confidence intervals on the separately named absolute-learnability and allocation-value effects.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: That the effect generalizes to other algorithms or larger agents.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Robustly useful
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: The marginal effect persists across policy families, seeds, environment families, and stronger exploit searches.

evidence_hierarchy.name: Prospectively scalable
evidence_hierarchy.evidence: A curve and environment ranking frozen using smaller runs predict a held-out larger run within preregistered calibration and error tolerances.
evidence_hierarchy.does_not_show: Universal scaling outside the tested regime.

recommended_statistics: Posterior probability and confidence interval for marginal held-out transfer uplift
Calibration error and Brier score for predicted environment value
Top-k selection regret against the expensive large-scale oracle ranking
Kendall rank correlation and pairwise sign agreement across scales
Reward-to-hidden-evaluator divergence as optimizer strength increases
Cost per accepted environment and effective sample size across environment families

validation_funnel.gate: Parse and type-check; enforce CPU, memory, time, file, and network limits; reject nondeterministic evaluators, mutable hidden state, or access from agent-visible code to the sealed evaluator.

Before any candidate trains a policy, blinded reviewers define the target capability and hazard rubric, audit every new semantic or high-consequence family, and inspect a pilot-powered random sample of automation-accepted and automation-rejected candidates. Human judgments are logged and never become mutable fitness.

Reference solutions, property tests, counterfactual action/state edits, semantics-preserving isomorphic perturbations, and metamorphic tests agree on success and failure; reward changes for the intended cause.
Random, scripted, frozen weak/strong, known-hack, and search-based adversarial policies produce a sensible difficulty ordering without reward/evaluator divergence.

A preregistered, powered comparison against no-update, shuffled-reward, and matched-random-environment controls finds learning progress across more than one algorithm. This is a screen, not a scale claim.

On logged development anchors, estimate absolute learnability against resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation value against a randomized eligible-pool replacement. Freeze both estimands before the inaccessible confirmation outcome is opened and report full effect distributions.
Freeze selection, curve family, and tolerances before the largest run. The held-out scale must meet prediction calibration, sign, rank, and reward/evaluator-gap criteria.

After selection is frozen, review all high-impact disagreements and a fresh random sentinel sample of accepted and rejected candidates to estimate systematic blind spots. This secondary routing experiment chooses automation-only, targeted, uniform, or exhaustive review for future studies; it does not replace the core causal-transfer and exploit-resistance gates.

human_in_the_loop.short_answer: No human is required in every generation or training loop when correctness and success are completely formal. Humans are required somewhere in the system when usefulness, interestingness, safety, realism, or domain coverage cannot be reduced to a trusted executable oracle.
humans_not_needed_for: API, sandbox, determinism, reachability, and property-test checks
Tasks with complete, independent formal verifiers and unambiguous semantics
Routine difficulty calibration after automated scores have been validated
humans_needed_for: Defining the target capability distribution and what counts as meaningful novelty
Auditing open-ended generated code, underspecified rewards, social tasks, and high-consequence domains
Creating and periodically refreshing a blind audit set that the generator cannot optimize against
Resolving evaluator disagreement and checking systematic low-uncertainty failures
human_in_the_loop.routing_policy: Split review into a pre-training construct-and-safety gate and a post-selection blind audit. At both stages combine disagreement routing with a pilot-powered random sentinel sample from accepted and rejected candidates. Freeze the sample size from the desired error bound, and compare targeted routing with equal-budget uniform review and exhaustive review on a powered subset. If targeted routing fails its secondary superiority or noninferiority test, fall back to the safer registered review policy without erasing an otherwise passing causal-value result.
human_in_the_loop.measurement: Report human minutes per candidate, inter-rater agreement, reversal rates for accepted and rejected candidates, sentinel-estimated false-negative intervals, and results for automation-only, targeted, uniform, and exhaustive review. Measure planted-exploit recall separately from double-blind adjudication of natural failures. Human-routing efficacy is a secondary operational claim; core promotion still requires the automated causal-transfer and independent exploit-resistance gates.

scaling_claim_protocol.short_answer: One small model cannot support a scaling claim. It can reject clearly bad environments and estimate which candidates deserve expensive tests. Small-to-large prediction is an empirical hypothesis that must be tested prospectively for a fixed algorithm and task regime.
why_small_models_fail: Larger or longer-trained agents can discover reward exploits that weak agents never reach; reward misspecification can show capability thresholds and sign reversals.
RL architecture and optimizer choices alter scaling behavior; simply increasing dense parameter count can hurt performance.
Curricula can change compute efficiency without changing the eventual performance ceiling, so early gains may disappear at convergence.
Environment rankings can change when an agent moves from exploration-limited to representation-, optimization-, or verifier-limited behavior.
prospective_design: Choose a stable training recipe and tune its scale-dependent hyperparameters without looking at the largest holdout.

Use a 1,080-cell discovery/calibration lattice per promoted candidate: three smaller policy capacities by three interaction budgets by three policy-and-RL-algorithm families by two optimizer families by two inference budgets by two tool-access regimes by five coupled seeds. Treat optimizer steps, realized effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs as matched diagnostics rather than alternative budget factors.
Split jointly by generator lineage, prompt or level template, normalized program AST, and semantic capability family, not random instances, so near-duplicates cannot leak into anchors.
Fit both monotone and saturating candidate curves and report model uncertainty. Predict marginal transfer uplift and environment rank, not training reward alone.

Freeze the union candidate pool used for every selector, the selected top-k environments, curve family, hyperparameter transfer rule, short and delayed-retention horizons, reward/evaluator thresholds, and acceptable prediction error before the larger run. Run native generator pipelines separately as end-to-end system comparisons instead of silently giving selectors different pools.

Use 60 untouched target cells per promoted candidate at the fourth capacity and fourth interaction budget: three prespecified contrasts—held-out policy/algorithm family on a known optimizer, known family on a held-out optimizer, and their joint shift—crossed with two inference budgets, two tool regimes, and five coupled seeds. Run an independently authored stronger exploit search and treat extrapolation beyond these cells as unverified.
supporting_evidence: Held-out transfer uplift is positive under equal total compute
Prediction intervals cover the observed larger-scale uplift at the preregistered rate
Top-k selection regret is lower than PLR, regret, learnability-only, novelty-only, and random selection
Environment-utility rank and pairwise signs remain sufficiently stable across scales
The hidden evaluator does not decouple from reward as policy optimization strengthens
claim_blockers: The largest held-out scale falls outside the frozen prediction interval
Transfer gain disappears under equal compute or is explained by extra generated tokens or evaluator calls
Environment ranking collapses or reverses for the second policy family
Only the generator's own solver or one algorithm benefits
Proxy reward rises while the sealed evaluator, human audit, or downstream anchors fall by more than the registered minimum-effect margin
Any target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, ordered-familywise-procedure change, or update to the immutable confirmation evaluator or confirmation exploit suites occurs
scaling_claim_protocol.claim_language: Say 'predictive within the tested scale, algorithm, and environment-family range,' never 'this environment scales' without those qualifiers.

experiment.primary_hypothesis: A cross-policy validator trained to predict compute-matched marginal transfer will select a top-k curriculum with greater sealed downstream uplift than regret, learnability, novelty, random generation, PLR-style replay, or ACCEL-style mutation using the same search and training budget.
experiment.secondary_hypothesis: At a frozen human-minute budget, disagreement plus pilot-powered random sentinels will be superior for planted-exploit recall and noninferior for double-blind natural-failure discovery relative to uniform routing; the two exploit outcomes are tested separately.
experiment.primary_outcome: Top-k selection regret against the expensive target-tier oracle ranking. Gate it with two separately reported effects on the inaccessible confirmation outcome: absolute learnability versus a resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation value versus a randomized eligible-pool replacement, each measured immediately and at the prefrozen delayed horizon, plus independent exploit resistance.
domains: Primary: executable reasoning or tool-use environments with generated instances, reference solvers, and independent database or program-state evaluation.
Replication only after the primary result: a procedurally generated simulator domain with continuous control or partial observability.
baselines: Uniform random generation and domain randomization
POET-style mutation and transfer
PAIRED or stabilized PAIRED generation
PLR and PLR-perp replay
ACCEL regret-guided editing
Direct learnability sampling from No Regrets
Value disagreement, SFL, PACE, TRACED Co-Learnability, DEGen/MNA, and the simplest small-learner rank under equal evaluation cost
MBeED/MBeDED marginal-benefit selection and the All Life is Problem Creation performance-gain proposer
CoDE and ATLAS when task specifications as well as level instances are mutable
ADD-style learned generation when the representation permits it
Adaptive verifiable-environment curricula patterned after RLVE or SCALER
Learner-coupled generation patterned after GenEnv, RLAnything, Agent-World, Envs-FORGE, or SPADE
LLM generate-filter pipelines patterned after Endless Terminals, OMNI-EPIC, EvoEnv, or CUA-Gym
ablations: Remove the sealed downstream-transfer predictor
Replace multi-policy scoring with one small solver
Remove development exploit-gap fitness or replace the independently authored one-time confirmation exploit suite with the development suite
Replace behavioral and causal diversity with source-code novelty
Use uncertainty-only human routing without random sentinel audits
Score individual environments without blocked curriculum-interaction corrections
Use post hoc Shapley values instead of the preregistered randomized add-one-in estimand
Share a mutable verifier between discovery and confirmation or expose evaluator hashes, query traces, timing, logs, or side channels to the generator
Evaluate only immediate transfer and omit the prefrozen delayed-retention horizon
experiment.selection_protocol: Freeze one deduplicated union candidate pool before selector comparison, with lineage, template, normalized-AST, and semantic-family groups fixed. All selectors receive identical candidates and evaluation ledgers. Native POET, ACCEL, learned-generator, LLM, and self-play pipelines run separately as system-level baselines. Discovery may query only a mutable, logged development outcome and development exploit suite. The independently implemented confirmation evaluator and independently authored natural and planted confirmation exploit suites are immutable, inaccessible, side-channel audited, and opened once after every selector, candidate, estimand, horizon, threshold, top-k choice, and human rubric is frozen.
experiment.resource_scalarization: Run a separate fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main candidate union: two capacities by two interaction budgets by three policy/algorithm families by two optimizers by one inference budget by two tool regimes by three coupled seeds. The main study promotes exactly eight different candidates—two predicted top, one predicted bottom, two ambiguous, and three sampled uniformly from the remaining eligible pool—and allocates 1,140 cells each, for 9,120 main learner cells before native baseline pipelines. Five coupled seeds are fixed for the main study; if the pilot does not give at least 80 percent power for the registered minimum useful allocation effect or the preregistered GPU-hour ceiling cannot cover all 9,120 cells plus frozen baseline costs, do not open confirmation and make no scale claim. Publish environment interactions, learner FLOPs, generator tokens, verifier calls, wall time, GPU-hours, and human minutes; freeze scalar exchange rates and the absolute GPU-hour ceiling from pilot accounting before main runs.
experiment.analysis: Use curriculum runs as independent experimental units with coupled seeds and hierarchical intervals clustered by generator lineage and environment family. Estimate absolute-learnability and allocation-value effects separately; randomize eligible replacements within family, difficulty, and resource blocks and state the positivity population. Estimate randomized blocked add-one effects first and report Shapley-style interactions only as exploratory. Apply an ordered familywise procedure: first target-tier selection regret against every preregistered selector using simultaneous one-sided max-t intervals; then allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, held-out-family and held-out-optimizer regret, interval calibration, and exploit resistance. Kendall tau-b and pairwise accuracy are diagnostic unless their pilot-derived utility margins and multiplicity-adjusted thresholds are separately registered. For stochastic environments, use frozen-policy repeated rollouts and paired seeds to separate aleatoric return variance from no-update versus update learning effects. Test planted exploit recall and blinded natural-failure discovery in separate families with explicit denominators, severity strata, and hierarchical confidence intervals.
experiment.claim_hierarchy: Gate claims in order: mechanical validity; within-domain causal learning value; delayed retention; cross-policy and cross-algorithm robustness; prospective target-fidelity selection; then exploit resistance. Every claim is bounded to the preregistered domain and semantic families. Quality-diversity coverage, MAP-Elites illumination, or a learned descriptor archive is not evidence of open-endedness, especially when descriptor retraining can move archive cells.
experiment.decision_rule: Success requires simultaneous-margin improvement in target-tier selection regret, positive immediate and delayed allocation value, positive absolute learnability, and independent exploit resistance under the ordered gatekeeping hierarchy. Target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, confirmation-evaluator or confirmation-exploit-suite updates, or familywise error failure are immediate blockers. Human-routing superiority or noninferiority is secondary: if it fails, use the preregistered safer review policy and report the routing claim as failed without erasing an otherwise passing causal-value result. A prettier or more diverse archive alone is a failed primary result.

evaluation: Compute-matched marginal transfer uplift on sealed family-held-out tasks
Top-k selection regret relative to an expensive post hoc oracle ranking
Cross-scale Kendall rank correlation, pairwise sign agreement, and prediction calibration
Reward-to-hidden-evaluator gap under increasingly capable exploit search
Acceptance precision and recall against blind automated and human audits
Capability, mechanism, and lineage coverage of the archive
GPU-hours, interactions, generated tokens, verifier calls, and human minutes per useful accepted environment
risks: RLVE, SCALER, GenEnv, RLAnything, Agent-World, Envs-FORGE, EvoEnv, and SPADE already cover adaptive difficulty, learner-coupled task generation, frontier-conditioned executable rewrites, staged validation, and gains across multiple model sizes. If this work only adds evolutionary search, frontier targeting, or a post hoc multi-size comparison, it is not sufficiently distinct.

The outer loop can overfit sealed anchors through repeated queries. Rate-limit access, maintain a never-touched final set, record adaptive queries, and rotate evaluator families only between preregistered studies.
A hidden evaluator can share bugs or assumptions with the generated reward. Use independently implemented evaluators, differential testing, and human sentinel audits.

Generated solver, SFT, or distillation trajectories can teach an exploit that reappears during RL or transfers to another environment. Version trace provenance, plant contamination canaries, cross clean and controlled contaminated training arms, and test post-mitigation recurrence and cross-domain persistence on the confirmation suite.
Short-horizon progress can favor shallow tasks. Preserve niches for delayed credit, exploration, memory, tool composition, and partial observability, then measure delayed transfer.
An individual environment may have no stable value outside a curriculum. Model pairwise or set-level interaction and report when the additive assumption fails.
Search noise can produce winner's curse. Use nested selection/evaluation splits, shrink noisy estimates, and publish all candidates and selection traces.

A formal simulator, temporal specification, or exact answer checker can still reward brittle templates. Require topology and backend shifts, executable temporal monitors, and hidden structural outcomes before treating verifier gains as environment validity.
Cross-scale regularity may not exist. A strong negative result is a calibrated map of which cheap signals fail, where rankings reverse, and which stronger agents uncover new exploits.
first_week: Choose one executable domain and define a candidate as generator, transition code, reward, termination rule, tests, and an inaccessible evaluator.
Build 30 hand-labeled positive, useless, impossible, trivial, leaky, and reward-hack cases to test validator recall before any evolutionary run.
Implement static, causal, reference-policy, exploit-policy, and reward/evaluator-gap checks.

Create separate development and confirmation exploit manifests, plant trace-contamination canaries, and preregister recurrence and cross-domain persistence tests before any generated solver or SFT trace trains a learner.
Freeze the pre-training construct-and-safety rubric and the separate post-selection routing experiment, including the safer fallback review policy.
Run a small randomized add-one-in experiment: base curriculum plus candidate versus a compute-matched replacement; estimate variance and power for the main study.
Compare TD error, regret, success probability, learning slope, policy disagreement, and gradient agreement as predictors of marginal transfer.
Write and timestamp the prospective scale protocol, family split, top-k decision, claim blockers, and human sentinel-audit rate.

competitive_landscape.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
competitive_landscape.difference: POET co-evolves environment-agent pairs and transfers solutions among them. It demonstrates stepping stones, not prospective prediction of an environment's causal value across policy families and scales.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhanced POET: Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning through Unbounded Invention of Learning Challenges and their Solutions
competitive_landscape.difference: Enhanced POET adds a domain-general environment characterization, improved transfer, a richer CPPN encoding, and an open-ended progress metric. The proposed work evaluates learning value and exploit risk rather than open-ended complexity alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: PAIRED trains a teacher to maximize protagonist-antagonist regret and reports zero-shot transfer. Here regret is a baseline feature, while selection targets compute-matched marginal transfer measured by independent evaluators.

competitive_landscape.title: Prioritized Level Replay
competitive_landscape.difference: PLR prioritizes levels using estimated future learning potential such as temporal-difference error. This project tests whether such cheap scores predict causal downstream value and remain calibrated across scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Replay-Guided Adversarial Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: Dual Curriculum Design unifies generation and replay, adds PLR-perp and REPAIRED, and gives minimax-regret guarantees at equilibrium. The proposed benchmark asks whether selected levels help sealed tasks under finite training and stronger policies.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolving Curricula with Regret-Based Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ACCEL edits replayed levels at the agent frontier using regret. It is the closest evolutionary baseline, but it does not make prospective cross-scale validation or independent exploit auditing the search target.

competitive_landscape.title: Grounding Aleatoric Uncertainty for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: SAMPLR shows that adaptive curricula can exploit aleatoric variables and create harmful covariate shift. Irreducible environment variables here must stay grounded to a sealed deployment distribution.

competitive_landscape.title: Stabilizing Unsupervised Environment Design with a Learned Adversary
competitive_landscape.difference: This work repairs practical PAIRED failure modes and shows learned generation can match curation or mutation. It raises the baseline for any claim that a new generator is needed.

competitive_landscape.title: Refining Minimax Regret for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: ReMiDi identifies regret stagnation and refines the objective so learning can continue. The proposed validator must beat this stronger regret baseline, not only original PAIRED.

competitive_landscape.title: No Regrets: Investigating and Improving Regret Approximations for Curriculum Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: No Regrets finds practical regret approximations correlate with success rather than regret and directly selects high-learnability binary tasks. The distinct target here is causal transfer and prospective scale fidelity, not learnability alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Environment Novelty Quantification for Effective Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: CENIE combines state-action coverage novelty with regret and already improves UED selection. Novelty here must therefore be causal, specification-stratified, and validated by transfer rather than counted as coverage alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Environment Design via Regret-Guided Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ADD guides a diffusion generator with regret and diversity for OOD generalization. It should be compared under the same generation and training budget; the proposed novelty lies in validation, not generator expressiveness.

competitive_landscape.title: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
competitive_landscape.difference: OMNI-EPIC uses foundation models to generate environment and reward code for learnable, interesting tasks. The proposed work separates mutable reward from a sealed evaluator and tests transfer and scale prospectively.

competitive_landscape.title: LLM-POET: Evolving Complex Environments using Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: LLM-POET replaces POET's environment encoding with LLM generation in Evolution Gym. It supports LLM mutations as a baseline but does not establish that generated-task utility transfers across scales.

competitive_landscape.title: BeamPERL: Parameter-Efficient RL with Verifiable Rewards Specializes Compact LLMs for Structured Beam Mechanics Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: BeamPERL finds that continued exact-reward optimization can preserve reward while robustness to moved supports deteriorates. It is direct negative evidence against certifying an environment from verifier reward or one small learner alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Eureka evolves reward code and can incorporate human feedback while holding task dynamics fixed. This project searches fuller environments and requires reward agreement with a separate hidden outcome.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Synthetic Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Evolution Strategies
competitive_landscape.difference: This work evolves neural proxy environments using target-task performance in a bilevel loop and reports limited transfer across algorithms. It is evidence that cross-agent invariance must be tested rather than assumed.

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering Minimal Reinforcement Learning Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: This work improves synthetic-environment invariance across hyperparameters and algorithms and finds contextual bandits can train agents for complex MDP evaluation. The proposed work adds open-ended executable generation, hidden-outcome audits, and prospective scale tests.

competitive_landscape.title: RLVE: Scaling Up Reinforcement Learning for Language Models with Adaptive Verifiable Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: RLVE dynamically adjusts difficulty within 400 manually engineered procedural environments and measures transfer to 50 held-out environments across several 1.5B and 7B models. It makes adaptive difficulty and environment-count scaling strong baselines; it does not automatically search new environment families or prospectively predict each candidate's marginal value at an unseen scale.

competitive_landscape.title: GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators
competitive_landscape.difference: GenEnv trains an environment policy to generate tasks near a target learner success rate while the agent learns from the resulting traces. Its success-band objective is a direct baseline, but it does not test whether that score predicts compute-matched transfer, exploit resistance, or task rankings across policy families and an unseen scale.

competitive_landscape.title: SCALER:Synthetic Scalable Adaptive Learning Environment for Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: SCALER converts programming problems into verifiable environments with controllable difficulty, adapts instance difficulty online, and retires saturated environments; ablations cover Qwen3 1.7B and 4B. The proposed delta must predict causal marginal transfer across families and a held-out scale, not merely maintain frontier difficulty or active-set freshness.

competitive_landscape.title: Endless Terminals: Scaling RL Environments for Terminal Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: Endless Terminals autonomously generates and validates 3,255 containerized tasks without human annotation and reports transfer for three model families or recipes to human-curated terminal benchmarks. It establishes a strong human-free generation baseline, but does not adapt generation to learner feedback or estimate candidate-level causal value.

competitive_landscape.title: RLAnything: Forge Environment, Policy, and Reward Model in Completely Dynamic RL System
competitive_landscape.difference: RLAnything jointly updates policy and reward models and uses critic feedback to rewrite tasks, including evaluators or unit tests, toward useful difficulty; it also tests reward-model feedback without human-labeled outcome rewards. The proposed work requires independent sealed outcomes and prospective environment-value validation rather than jointly optimizing every signal in one loop.

competitive_landscape.title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
competitive_landscape.difference: Agent-World discovers executable tool ecosystems, synthesizes verifiable tasks with controllable difficulty, and targets capability gaps through a self-evolving arena, with 8B and 14B results. It narrows autonomous discovery and co-evolution claims, but does not prospectively calibrate per-environment causal value or cross-family exploit risk.

competitive_landscape.title: Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: AWM reports 1,000 code-driven, database-backed tool environments and OOD gains from synthetic-only RL. It raises the bar for scale and reliability; this project evaluates which environments caused those gains and whether early scores predict larger agents.

competitive_landscape.title: ReSyn: Autonomously Scaling Synthetic Environments for Reasoning Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ReSyn generates reasoning environments with instance generators and verifiers and reports gains from verifier supervision and diversity. The proposed study adds counterfactual curricula, exploit auditing, and prospective cross-scale selection.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Build the Environment: Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis
competitive_landscape.difference: EvoEnv already uses staged validation, semantic self-review, solver-relative difficulty, novelty checks, and solve-verify asymmetry. A publishable delta must be a rigorous causal and cross-scale environment-value validator, not another generate-filter loop.

competitive_landscape.title: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: WebGym supplies nearly 300,000 rubric-scored real-website tasks, a high-throughput rollout stack, and transfer to held-out websites. It establishes that breadth can help one 8B visual-agent recipe; it does not estimate individual environment value or prospectively predict rankings across policy and compute scales.

competitive_landscape.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: CUA-Gym co-generates task instructions, initial and golden states, and deterministic rewards, then filters them with generator-discriminator iteration, majority voting, and rollouts. Its 32,112 tuples across 110 mock applications and two model sizes raise the generation and validation baseline, but do not test a frozen predictor of causal environment value across unrelated policy families and an unseen scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Envs-FORGE: Frontier-Optimized Reward-Grounded Environment Synthesis for Agent RL
competitive_landscape.difference: Envs-FORGE uses verifier-derived seed pass rates and a per-seed MILP to select increase, reduce, or diversify rewrites of complete verified terminal environments; one generated set improves tb-core across Qwen 3.5 4B-35B. It makes frontier targeting and post hoc multi-size gains non-novel, but does not freeze a predictor and test calibration, candidate rankings, causal marginal transfer, or exploit gaps at an unseen scale and policy family.

competitive_landscape.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: SPADE already makes executable environment design adaptive: a designer writes stateful Gym-style environments and optimizes privileged-hint regret against a learning agent, with reported gains through 30B parameters. The remaining delta is not adaptive synthesis; it is to predict compute-matched marginal transfer and exploit resistance prospectively across policy families, including when privileged-hint regret gives the wrong ranking.

competitive_landscape.title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: EurekAgent treats permissions, artifacts, budgets, and low-friction human intervention as environment-engineering primitives for autonomous science. It informs sandboxing and human routing here, but does not evolve RL environment families or validate their causal learning value and cross-scale stability.

competitive_landscape.title: AI Safety Gridworlds
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Safety Gridworlds separates observed reward from a hidden performance function. This motivates keeping a sealed evaluator outside the environment genome.

competitive_landscape.title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper shows more optimization power can increase proxy reward while reducing true reward, sometimes after capability thresholds. It directly falsifies the idea that a clean weak-agent run is enough to certify an environment.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling laws for single-agent reinforcement learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Intrinsic performance can scale smoothly with model size and interactions in studied environments. The proposed work asks a different question: whether environment-level marginal effects and rankings are predictably scalable.

competitive_landscape.title: Mixtures of Experts Unlock Parameter Scaling for Deep RL
competitive_landscape.difference: Dense parameter scaling can hurt deep RL while Soft MoE can restore positive scaling. Model size is therefore not a sufficient scale axis; architecture and optimization family must be held explicit.

competitive_landscape.title: Value-Based Deep RL Scales Predictably
competitive_landscape.difference: This work predicts data-compute frontiers and scale-dependent hyperparameters for value-based RL across several domains. Its prospective methodology is a template, but it does not predict the relative value of generated environments.

competitive_landscape.title: The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: ScaleRL fits sigmoidal compute-performance curves and distinguishes compute efficiency from asymptotic performance. This project should adopt that distinction when judging whether an environment changes learning speed or the eventual capability ceiling.

competitive_landscape.title: Automatic Curriculum Learning through Value Disagreement
competitive_landscape.difference: Value disagreement proposes goals near the policy's reachability frontier using epistemic uncertainty. It is a cheap learner-local selection signal, not a causal downstream effect or cross-scale predictor.

competitive_landscape.title: Environment Generation for Zero-Shot Compositional Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: CoDE trains a generator to build compositional tasks tailored to the student's current skill and evaluates zero-shot generalization. It occupies learner-adaptive task composition but not sealed marginal attribution or prospective scale prediction.

competitive_landscape.title: Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: MBeED trains a teacher on the return difference between an updated student and a slightly outdated copy; MBeDED adds representative-state diversity. This occupies marginal-benefit environment scoring but not a generator-inaccessible neutral-suite effect, cross-family holdout, or prospectively frozen target-scale predictor.

competitive_landscape.title: An Optimisation Framework for Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.relationship: theoretical and practical UED optimization competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: This work formulates UED as nonconvex-strongly-concave optimization and implements a dynamic-buffer algorithm. It raises the optimization baseline but does not estimate sealed candidate-level causal value across unseen learners and scale.

competitive_landscape.title: All Life is Problem Creation: Learning to Generate Environments that Maximize Performance Gain
competitive_landscape.difference: Its proposer is conditioned on solver behavior and rewarded by measured gain on repeatedly sampled held-out target tasks. It directly occupies performance-gain generation, but does not freeze a predictor for an untouched scale or family, audit exploits, or demonstrate stable candidate rankings.
competitive_landscape.source_version: SEA @ NeurIPS 2025 Poster; OpenReview record modified 2025-11-19

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Fixed Tasks: Unsupervised Environment Design for Task-Level Pairs
competitive_landscape.difference: ATLAS generates and mutates solvable task-level pairs, including reward-machine tasks and MiniGrid levels. It occupies joint task and level evolution but not sealed candidate-value measurement or cross-family rank stability.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Regret Approximation for Unsupervised Dynamic Environment Generation
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest current learned-generator and regret-objective baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: DEGen supplies denser teacher credit and Maximised Negative Advantage improves challenging-level identification. Both are mandatory generator and score baselines, but neither tests generator-inaccessible causal transfer or prospective scale ranking.

competitive_landscape.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
competitive_landscape.difference: This work finds RLVR models can exploit extensional verification and proposes Isomorphic Perturbation Testing to distinguish genuine rules from shortcuts. The program incorporates this test family and adds generated environments, sealed outcomes, and stronger-policy prospective auditing.

competitive_landscape.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
competitive_landscape.difference: MAP-Elites archives high-performing solutions across user-chosen descriptors. It supplies a search mechanism and illumination map, not evidence of open-endedness or causal learning value; the descriptor choice itself fixes what diversity can be seen.

competitive_landscape.title: Autonomous skill discovery with Quality-Diversity and Unsupervised Descriptors
competitive_landscape.difference: AURORA learns behavioral descriptors for quality-diversity archives and shows that descriptor choice changes the discovered repertoire. The validator must version learned descriptors and measure archive drift instead of treating cell movement as progress.

competitive_landscape.title: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: This work formalizes when capable agents have incentives to tamper with reward functions or reward inputs and gives causal design principles. It motivates explicit tamper surfaces and evaluator isolation; it does not measure the causal training value of generated environments.

competitive_landscape.title: PCGRL: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: PCGRL casts level design as an RL problem and trains fast generators without example corpora. It occupies learned content generation, while the proposed program evaluates whether generated training environments produce sealed transfer rather than only high content-quality reward.

competitive_landscape.title: Open-Ended Learning Leads to Generally Capable Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: XLand dynamically changes task distributions and objectives in a vast multi-agent world and reports broad held-out behavior. Its iterative progress measure is not candidate-level causal attribution or a prospectively calibrated unseen-fidelity selector.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
competitive_landscape.difference: This work measures how optimizing a learned proxy can reduce a gold reward and how that relation changes with optimization method, KL, model size, and reward-model data. It makes optimizer strength and hidden-outcome divergence mandatory axes rather than a single exploit-rate check.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalization through Diversity: Improving Unsupervised Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: DRED selects diverse environments using a task-relevant distance so high-learning-potential tasks are not redundant. It is a direct diversity baseline; the proposal must show that causal transfer and exploit resistance add value beyond diversity-aware UED.

competitive_landscape.title: MAESTRO: Open-Ended Environment Design for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: MAESTRO builds joint curricula over environments and co-player policies with minimax-regret guarantees in two-player zero-sum settings. It occupies multi-agent environment design but not sealed cross-family causal-value prediction.

competitive_landscape.title: Enabling Adaptive Agent Training in Open-Ended Simulators by Targeting Diversity
competitive_landscape.difference: DIVA evolves diverse tasks in complex open-ended simulators and combines domain structure with flexible environment design for meta-RL. It makes evolutionary diversity in realistic simulators non-novel; the remaining claim concerns prospective causal value and confirmation isolation.

competitive_landscape.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Absolute Zero trains one model to propose and solve verifier-backed code and math tasks without external data and reports results across scales and model classes. Autonomous task generation and post hoc multi-scale gains are occupied; untouched candidate-value calibration is not.

competitive_landscape.title: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
competitive_landscape.difference: TRACED adds transition-prediction error and Co-Learnability to ACCEL-style task priority. Its shadow test finds only mild one-step temporal persistence (Pearson 0.3998; Spearman 0.2013), and its long runs oscillate, so it is a mandatory interaction baseline rather than a causal or long-horizon certificate.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Small Training Runs Reliably Guide Data Curation? Rethinking Proxy-Model Practice
competitive_landscape.difference: This work shows small-run data rankings can flip under small hyperparameter changes and argues for recipe-specific tuning, with reduced learning rates improving agreement with tuned large runs. It strengthens the requirement to vary optimization fidelity and compare simple frozen ranking rules.

competitive_landscape.title: AutoEnv: Automated Environments for Measuring Cross-Environment Agent Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: AutoEnv factorizes transition, observation, and reward distributions, builds 36 heterogeneous environments, and shows fixed learning methods degrade as diversity grows. It occupies broad cross-environment generation and adaptive method selection, but does not prospectively validate candidate causal transfer at an untouched fidelity.

competitive_landscape.title: EnvFactory: Scaling Tool-Use Agents via Executable Environments Synthesis and Robust RL
competitive_landscape.difference: EnvFactory automatically explores and verifies 85 stateful tool environments and synthesizes grounded multi-turn trajectories with reported downstream gains. It makes automated tool-environment construction non-novel but does not freeze a causal-value selector or immutable target evaluator.

competitive_landscape.title: Distilling Game Code World Model Generation into Lightweight Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: GameCWM distills verified game-environment code generation into a 3B model with SFT and RLVR. It shows small models can generate mechanically valid environments, but it does not establish that those environments create useful transferable learning signal.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Synthetic Environments and Reward Networks for Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work evolves both neural proxy dynamics and reward networks, evaluates multiple RL algorithms, and reports transfer to unseen agents. It makes joint proxy-environment and reward evolution established; the proposed delta is inaccessible confirmation, separate causal estimands, and prospective target-fidelity calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: EnvGen: Generating and Adapting Environments via LLMs for Training Embodied Agents
competitive_landscape.difference: EnvGen repeatedly adapts simulator configurations to a small learner's observed weak skills in Crafter and Heist. It occupies LLM-guided environment adaptation and small-agent training gains, but does not freeze candidate-value predictions or test independent exploit resistance at an unseen family and scale.

competitive_landscape.title: From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: The current RL checkpoint diagnoses failure trajectories and edits the next-stage environment configuration. It makes learner-conditioned environment redesign current and direct; the proposed delta is causal allocation value, independent exploit confirmation, and untouched family and optimizer tests.

competitive_landscape.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
competitive_landscape.difference: Countdown-Code reports that a small fraction of hacked SFT trajectories can teach reward hacking that reappears under RL and generalizes beyond the training domain. It requires contamination, recurrence, and cross-domain persistence tests in addition to stronger-policy exploit search.

brief.novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after a 65-record direct landscape and the canonical-union 85-record field audit checked through 2026-08-24: environment evolution, heterogeneous factored generation, quality-diversity archives, learned descriptors, autotelic curricula, procedural content generation, learner-local difficulty and Co-Learnability scoring, zero-data self-play, realized marginal benefit, target-task performance gain, executable verification, learned-exploit contamination, and post hoc multi-size gains are occupied. The surviving conjunction is narrower: freeze one union candidate pool and causal-value predictor without confirmation outcomes, keep immutable generator-inaccessible confirmation evaluator and exploit suites, and prospectively falsify separately named allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, target-tier selection regret, held-out-family and held-out-optimizer regret, calibration, and exploit resistance across explicit multi-fidelity axes.
brief.evidence_note: This flagship has eight page-anchored collection readings spanning 258 pages, 85 findings, 246 anchors, and 73 checked per-paper primary competitors, plus a 65-record direct brief landscape and the canonical-union 85-record field audit at data/reviewed/audits/evo.json, checked through 2026-08-24. Several 2026 sources are preprints, not independent replications, and four readings contain material claim or proof boundaries; they are retained as negative evidence rather than endorsements. The revised 5.1 feasibility reflects the fixed 1,152-cell pilot and 9,120-cell main study required by the identifiable factorization.
